children.text: Vādivāgīśvara: Mānamanohara
children.translated_text: <s>Vādivāgīśvara</s>: <s>Mānamanohara</s>

children.text: namastasyai mahābhūtabaddhān amṛtasevanāt /
children.translated_text: Salutation to that great <s>Śakti</s> (power), who, though situated beyond lineage, through the partaking of the nectar [of knowledge],

children.text: mocayatyakulasthāpi yā śaktiścitsvarūpiṇī // 1 //
children.translated_text: liberates those bound to the great elements — that <s>Śakti</s> whose nature is consciousness. (1)

children.text: vāgīśvarācāryasutena vādivāgīśvareṇa kriyate gabhīraḥ /
children.translated_text: By <s>Vādivāgīśvara</s>, the son of <s>Vāgīśvara-ācārya</s>, this profound [work] is composed—

children.text: kathāsu garjatprativādigarvapraśāntaye mānamanoharo 'yam // 2 //
children.translated_text: this <s>Mānamanohara</s> ('Crusher of Pride'), for the pacification of the thundering pride of opponents in debates. (2)

children.text: siddhiprakaraṇam
children.translated_text: Chapter on Proofs (<s>Siddhiprakaraṇa</s>)

children.text: īśvarasiddhiḥ
children.translated_text: Proof of <s>Īśvara</s> (God)

children.text: 1) vivādādhyāsitaṃ karma prayatnādhārajaṃ karmatvāt, yatkarma tat prayatnādhārajaṃ yathā - sampratipannaṃ karma, tathā vivādādhyāsitaṃ karma, tasmātprayatnādhārajam /
children.translated_text: 1) The action that is the subject of dispute is produced from a support of effort (<s>prayatna</s>), because it is action; whatever is action is produced from a support of effort, like presently observed action; likewise the action that is the subject of dispute — therefore it is produced from a support of effort.

children.text: 2) vivādādhyāsitaṃ mūrtaṃ prayatnādhārajam, paramāṇuvyatiriktatve sati mūrtatvāt /
children.translated_text: 2) The subject of dispute is a corporeal [entity] produced from a support of effort, because while being distinct from atoms (<s>paramāṇus</s>), it possesses corporeality.

children.text:
3) gandhaḥ prayatnajaḥ, gandhatvāt, ghaṭavattadgatagandhavacca /
na ca śarīriṇājanyatvādityanena prakaraṇasamatvam, nāpi tajjanyatvamupādhiḥ, akāryatvasyoprādheḥ, vyarthaviśeṣaṇatvācca /
etena vyāptidarśanakāle karmatvakāryatvāderaṅkaratajjananādau kevalasyāpi darśanād vyāptaniścaya iti parākṛtam, upādhisadbhāvasyā 'nirūpitatvāt /
yāvadupādhirna nirūpyate, tāvadekasminnapi piṇḍenayoḥ sambandhaniyame prayojakatvaṃ vācyam /
anyāprayuktasambandhasyāpi sādhyaparityāge svabhāvaparityāgaprasaṅgāt, nirūpādhikasambandhatvācca vyāpteḥ /
children.translated_text: 3) Smell (<s>gandha</s>) is produced from effort, because it is smell, like a pot and the smell residing in it. And this does not commit the fallacy of equal reasoning (<s>prakaraṇasama</s>) by [objecting] 'because it is not producible by an embodied being,' nor is 'being produced by that' a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>), because 'not being an effect' is the [real] limiting condition, and because it would be a pointless qualifier. By this, the [objection] that 'at the time of observing <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion), since action-ness and effect-ness are seen even alone — without the generation [by effort] — the ascertainment of pervasion [holds]' is refuted, because the existence of the limiting condition has not been disproven. As long as the limiting condition is not disproven, the compelling force of the invariable connection of the two [terms] must be stated even in a single instance. Because even a connection not compelled by something else, when it abandons the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), would entail the abandonment of its own nature; and because <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is a connection without limiting conditions.

children.text: 4) kiṃ ca vivādhyāsite pṛthivyudake prayatnavatā ghṛte, gurutve satyapātitvāt karatalāmalakavat /
children.translated_text: 4) Moreover, in the subject of dispute — earth and water sustained by one possessing effort — when heaviness is present, there is non-falling, like a gooseberry on the palm of the hand.

children.text:
5) īśvarajñānaṃ nityam, dviṣṭhavyatiriktatve sati īśvaraniṣṭhatvāt, tadgatamahatvavat /
na ca jñānatvādityanena prakaraṇasamatvam, kāraṇasadbhāvasyopādheḥ /
tasyāpi sādhane bādhaḥ --- na hi draṣṭurddaṣṭerviparilopo vidyate (bṛha 4.3.23) ityāgamabādhaḥ /
anyathā jalaparamāṇurūpamanityam, rūpatvādityapi syāt /
na ca tatrāpi kāraṇasadbhāva upādhiḥ, tasyāpi sādhanādbādhāyā abhāvāt /
children.translated_text: 5) God's (<s>Īśvara</s>'s) knowledge is eternal, because while being distinct from what resides in two [substrates], it resides in <s>Īśvara</s>, like the greatness residing therein. And this does not commit the fallacy of equal reasoning by [objecting] 'because it is knowledge,' because 'the existence of a cause' is the limiting condition. In establishing that [limiting condition] too, there is a counter-argument — 'the vision of the seer is never lost' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.3.23) — this is a scriptural counter-argument. Otherwise, the form of a water-atom would be non-eternal, because it is form — this too would follow. And in that case too, 'the existence of a cause' is not a limiting condition, because from establishing that [condition] too, there is no counter-argument.

children.text:
6) vivādādhyāsitam nityaviśeṣaguṇādhārajam kāryatvādāpyadvayṇukavat /
yaśca nityaviśeṣaguṇādhāraḥ, sa eveśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: 6) The subject of dispute is produced from a support of eternal, specific qualities, because it is an effect, like a dyad (<s>dvyaṇuka</s>). And that which is the support of eternal, specific qualities — that alone is <s>Īśvara</s> (God).

children.text:
7) bauddhaṃ prati īśvarasādhanam --- vivādādhyāsito vikalpaḥ tadatirikte pramā, pramātvāt, nirvikalpakapramāvat /
na cāśrayāsiddhisvarūpāsiddhī, īśvarādiṣu bhaktānāṃ taddhetulyādikalpanā /
children.translated_text: 7) Proof of <s>Īśvara</s> against the Buddhist — the conceptualization that is the subject of dispute is valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>) regarding what is other than it, because it is valid cognition, like non-conceptual valid cognition. And there is neither the fallacy of unestablished locus (<s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>) nor unestablished essential nature (<s>svarūpāsiddhi</s>), [because] the constructions regarding the cause and the like of devotees of <s>Īśvara</s> and others—

children.text: vāsanāmātrabhāvinyo jāyante vividhāḥ sphuṭam //
children.translated_text: manifestly arise in various forms, born merely from impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>).

children.text: (ta saṃ 282) iti tvayaivābhyupagateḥ, mama sutarāmiṣṭatvāt, tvanmate svaprakāśatvena sarvajñānānāṃ pramātvāt, mama tu prakṛte 'vipratipatteśca /
children.translated_text: (<s>Tattvasaṃgraha</s> 282) — since this is accepted by you yourself, it is all the more established for me; because in your system all cognitions are valid by being self-luminous; and because in the matter at hand there is no disagreement on my part.

children.text: 8) etajjñānam, etadutpādakānityavyatiriktajñānajam, kāryatvāt, sampratipannavat /
na cātraitadvyatiriktatvamupādhiḥ, tava vyarthaviśeṣaṇatvāt, mama nityeṣvapi sambhavāt /
children.translated_text: And here, 'being other than that' is not a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>), because for you it would be a pointless qualifier, and because for me it occurs even in eternal [entities].

children.text: kāryatve satīti viśeṣaṇe pūrvadoṣānuṣaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the qualifier 'when there is effect-ness' [is added], the previous fault follows.

children.text: nityajñānādhāra īśvara itīśvaralakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: The definition of <s>Īśvara</s> (God) is: <s>Īśvara</s> is the support of eternal knowledge.

children.text: tadevaṃ kāryatvādibhirhetubhiḥ siddha īśvaraḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus, by reasons such as being an effect, <s>Īśvara</s> is established.
8) This knowledge is produced by knowledge other than that which is the eternal producer of this, because it is an effect, like presently [observed knowledge].

children.text: avayavisiddhiḥ
children.translated_text: Proof of <s>avayavi</s> (the composite whole)

children.text: 1) savikalpakaṃ savikalpakavyatirikte pramā, pramātvāt, nirvikalpakapramāvat /
children.translated_text: 1) Determinate cognition (<s>savikalpaka</s>) is valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>) regarding what is other than determinate cognition, because it is valid cognition, like indeterminate valid cognition (<s>nirvikalpaka-pramā</s>).

children.text: 2) etatkāryam, etadutpādakajñānavyatiriktajanyam, kāryatvāt /
children.translated_text: 2) This is an effect, produced by knowledge other than the knowledge that produces this, because it is an effect.

children.text:
3) nirvikalpakam, nirvikalpakotpādakajñānavyatiriktajanyam, kāryatvād, jñānāntaravat, savikalpakavacca /
na ca nirvikalpakatvamupādhiḥ vaiyarthādviśeṣaṇasya /
children.translated_text: 3) Indeterminate cognition (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) is produced by knowledge other than the knowledge that produces indeterminate cognition, because it is an effect, like another cognition, and like determinate cognition. And 'being indeterminate' is not a limiting condition, because the qualifier would be pointless.

children.text:
yatprakāśate tajjñānam, yathā sampratipannam /
prakāśate vivādapadamiti nātra prakaraṇasamatvam, ubhayavādisiddhāśrayasya durnirūpatvāt /
etena vastutvādayo nirastāḥ /
vimataṃ jñānātmakam, vastutvāt sattvāt, sampratipannavaditi /
children.translated_text: Whatever is manifest is knowledge, like what is presently [manifest]. The subject of dispute is manifest — therefore this does not commit the fallacy of equal reasoning, because the locus established by both disputants is difficult to disprove. By this, [objections based on] 'substance-ness' and so forth are also refuted. [The argument:] 'the subject of dispute is of the nature of knowledge, because it is a substance, because it exists, like what is presently [observed].'

children.text:
4) sthūlavikalpo bāhye 'rthe pramā, pramātvād, rūpadarśanavadityavayavisiddhiḥ /
na ca vṛttivikalpādibādhitatvādyutthānam, teṣāmeva pratyakṣabādhitatvāt /
indriyaṃ dravyagrāhakaṃ na bhavati, indriyatvād, rasanavaditi tu vyāptyasiddhisvarūpāsiddhidṛṣṭāntāsiddhiduṣṭatvādasādhanam /
pratiyogino 'jñāne vyatirekasya jñātumaśakyatvād indriyasvarūpasya dravyaviśeṣaṇatvācca /
children.translated_text: 4) The gross determinate cognition is valid cognition regarding external objects, because it is valid cognition, like the perception of form — thus the composite whole (<s>avayavi</s>) is established. And the objection raised [by opponents] regarding invalidation by conceptual cognition and so forth does not stand, because those very [objections] are themselves invalidated by direct perception. And the [argument] 'the sense organ does not apprehend substance, because it is a sense organ, like the tongue' is not a valid proof due to the faults of unestablished pervasion, unestablished essential nature, and unestablished example. Because in the absence of knowledge of the counter-correlate, the negative concomitance cannot be known; and because the essential nature of the sense organ is a qualifier of substance.

children.text:
apare tu gandho 'gandhopādānaḥ, kāryatvādrūpavadityavayavisiddhiṃ bruvate /
tatra copādānaśabdasya samavāyikāraṇavācakatve dṛṣṭāntābhāvaḥ, sajātīyamātravācakatve siddhasādhanatā, atyantasajātīyavācakatve pratijñāpadayorvyāghātaḥ /
kāryatve sati sparśavadavayavītyavayavilakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Others, however, state the proof of the composite whole thus: 'smell is not produced from smell as its material cause, because it is an effect, like form.' Therein, if the word '<s>upādāna</s>' (material cause) denotes the inherence cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>), there is absence of an example. If it denotes merely 'of the same class,' it is the fallacy of proving what is already established. If it denotes 'of the exact same class,' there is a contradiction between the thesis and the terms. When there is effect-ness, it is like touch and the composite whole — distinguished from the composite.

children.text: paramāṇusiddhiḥ
children.translated_text: Proof of <s>paramāṇu</s> (atoms)

children.text:
1) vivādādhyāsito gandha etadgandhakāraṇena janyate gandhatvāt, kāryatvādetadvat /
na ca piṇḍasyevopādhitvam, tatsamānakṣaṇānāṃ rūpādīnāmapi tathābhāvaprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: 1) The smell that is the subject of dispute is produced by the cause of this smell, because it is smell, because it is an effect, like this [present smell]. And the objection that the aggregate itself is the limiting condition does not hold, because of the undesirable consequence that forms and so forth existing at the same moment would also be [subject to] the same [objection].

children.text:
2) vipratipannaṃ kāryam, etannīlakāraṇajam, kāryatvāt, gṛhyamāṇanīlavat /
na cānugrāhakatarkābhāvaḥ, ante 'pi sthirapadārthānabhyupagame kāryakāraṇabhāvanirvāhāt, anvayavyatirekaprayojakābhāvāt /
kalpanayā tatsiddhyabhyupagame vastuno 'sattvena tanmūlasya kāryakāraṇabhāvasyāsattvaprāptau viśvāsattvaprasaṅgaḥ /
arthakriyākāritvasya sattvātsamarthasya kṣepāyogādityādi sahakārisadasadbhāvaprayuktatvena pariharaṇīyam /
sahakāriṇāmeva hetutvamastviti (cenna) teṣāmeva caramatvaniyame tadupayogaḥ syāt /
atyantatantusaṃyogādiṣvapyavacchedakatvena tantūnāmupayogāt /
teṣāṃ cāniyāmakatve 'nyatrāpi paṭotpattiprasaṅgaḥ /
krameṇa kāryakaraṇārhaṃ sthiraṃ tadviparītaṃ kṣaṇikamiti vipratipatterviṣaya udghāṭanīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 2) The subject of disagreement is an effect produced from the cause of this blue [color] which is other than it, because it is an effect, like the blue being apprehended. And there is no absence of supporting reasoning — because even without accepting stable substances at the ultimate level, the relation of cause and effect is maintained; because there is no absence of what compels positive and negative concomitance. If by [mere] conceptual construction one accepts the establishment of that, then since the thing is non-existent, the undesirable consequence arises that the cause-effect relation based on that would also be non-existent, leading to the consequence of universal unreliability. [The objection] 'because substance-ness is the nature of performing purposeful action, what is capable cannot be rejected' and so forth — this is to be answered by showing its dependence on the presence or absence of auxiliary causes. If the auxiliaries alone are the cause, [this does not work because] their use would apply only to determining which is the final [cause]. Because even in the case of the conjunction of extreme threads and so forth, threads serve as delimiters. And if those [threads] were non-determining, the undesirable consequence would be that cloth could arise elsewhere too. That which is capable of producing effects gradually is stable; what is the opposite of that is momentary — thus the scope of the disagreement should be laid open.

children.text:
3) vivādādhyāsitā gandhādayaḥ pṛthivyārambhakā na saṃbhavanti, saṃyogavyatiriktatve sati bhūtaguṇatvād, vibhāgavat /
rasa udakārambhako na bhavati, rūpaṃ teja ārambhakaṃ na bhavati, sparśo vāyujanako na bhavati, śabdo dravyārambhako na bhavati, bhūtaviśeṣaṇaguṇattvādbāhyaikaikendriyagrāhyaguṇatvādvā gandhavat /
na cātraupādhikaśaṅkā 'pyasti gandhatvasya, tasyābhāve 'pi gurutvādiṣu sādhyasya darśanāt /
na ca śabdavyatiriktamupādhi caramasyānumānasya, nāpi prathamasya rasavyatiriktatvaṃ prayojakam, tadvyatiriktasyāpi saṃyogāderudakārambhakatvadarśanāt /
etena madhyamayorupādhiśaṅkā nirākṛtā /
ato gandhādivyatiriktopādānasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 3) The smells and so forth that are the subject of dispute are not possible as the producers of earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>), because while being distinct from conjunction, they are qualities of elements (<s>bhūtaguṇa</s>), like separation (<s>vibhāga</s>). Taste is not the producer of water. Form is not the producer of fire. Touch is not the producer of wind. Sound is not the producer of substance — because it is a quality specific to elements, or because it is a quality apprehended by a single external sense organ, like smell. And there is no suspicion of a limiting condition here regarding smell-ness, because the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is observed even in heaviness and so forth where that [smell-ness] is absent. And the distinctness from sound is not a limiting condition for the last inference, nor is the distinctness from taste a compelling factor for the first, because even what is distinct from that — such as conjunction — is observed as a producer of water. By this, the suspicion of a limiting condition for the middle [inferences] is also refuted. Therefore, the existence of a material cause distinct from smell and so forth is established.

children.text:
4) vivādādhyāsitaṃ kāryaṃ samavāyikāraṇakaṃ bhāvakāryatvādghaṭavat /
na ca vyarthaviśeṣaṇatvam, kāryatvamātrasya dhvaṃsādiṣu vyabhicārāt /
children.translated_text: 4) The subject of dispute, being an effect, has an inherence cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>), because it is a positive effect, like a pot. And this is not a pointless qualifier, because mere effect-ness has deviation [from the <s>sādhya</s>] in destruction and so forth.

children.text:
5) vivādādhyāsitaṃ kāryaṃ samavāyikāraṇakaṃ kāryatvāt, mahāmūrtatvādvāghaṭavaditi kecit /
vivādādhyāsitaṃ kāryaṃ mahat, samavāyikāraṇatvāditi bruvate /
taistu yogipratyakṣaṃ samadhigamya paramāṇuṣvanaikāntikatvaparihārārthamasmadādīti viśeṣaṇīyam /
tathā ca vyarthaviśeṣaṇatvam, prativādino vyāvṛttyabhāvāt, manasi vyabhicāraśca /
tasmāt tryaṇukaparamāṇusiddhiḥ /
kāryadravyājanyaṃ mūrttamaṇuḥ /
nityo mūrttaḥ paramāṇuḥ /
children.translated_text: 5) The subject of dispute, being an effect, has an inherence cause, because it is an effect, or because it has great corporeality, like a pot — so some say. [Others] say: the subject of dispute, being an effect, is great, because it has an inherence cause. But by them, to avoid the fault of non-exclusiveness regarding atoms, [the reason] should be qualified as 'by us and others,' having ascertained yogic perception. And thus it would be a pointless qualifier, because of the absence of exclusion of the opponent; and there is deviation in the mind. Therefore, the triad-atom (<s>tryaṇuka</s>) and [thereby] the atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>) are established. An atom is a corporeal [entity] that is not produced by an effect-substance. The atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>) is eternal and corporeal.

children.text: dravyaprakaraṇam
children.translated_text: Chapter on Substance (<s>Dravyaprakaraṇa</s>)

children.text: pṛthivyā nirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of Earth (<s>Pṛthivī</s>)

children.text:
1) vivādādhyāsitaṃ pṛthivīsamavāyikāraṇakam, kāryatve sati gandhatvāt, sampratipannavat /
na ca sopādhikatvaṃ syāt, mahāpṛthivītvasya rūpādau sādhyāvyāpakatvāt /
nityamūrttārambhātiriktatve sati kāryatvasyodakādiṣvapi sambhavāt /
pārthivatvena viśeṣaṇe viśeṣyavaiyarthyāt /
nirupādhikasya sādhyaparityāge svabhāvaparityāgaprasaṅgāt /
tasmātpārthivena paramāṇunā pārthivamevārabhyata iti niyamaḥ /
nityatve sati gandhavān pārthivaḥ paramāṇuriti pārthivaparamāṇulakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
1) The subject under dispute has earth as its <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> (inherent cause), because, being an effect, it possesses <s>gandha</s> (smell), like the acknowledged [earth substance].
Nor is there a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>), because <s>mahāpṛthivītva</s> (great-earth-ness) does not pervade the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) in form etc.
Since effectness is possible in water etc. too when they differ from the eternal, corporeal, and originating [atoms],
if one qualifies with 'earthen' (<s>pārthivatva</s>), the qualifier renders the qualificand redundant.
If one abandons the unconditional <s>sādhya</s>, there would be the unwanted consequence of abandoning its very nature.
Therefore, the rule is: by an earthen <s>paramāṇu</s> (atom), only an earthen [substance] is produced.
The definition of an earthen atom is: that which, being eternal, possesses <s>gandha</s> (smell) — that is an earthen <s>paramāṇu</s>.

children.text:
2) devaśarīramayonijaṃ na bhavati, śarīratvādityanaikāntikaṃ śalabhādiśarīre /
viśiṣṭasaṃsthānavatvamapi tasyāsiddham, trinayanasahasrākṣacaturbhujādibhedabhinnatvāt /
vivādādhyāsitaḥ śarīrasantāno 'yonijaśarīrakaḥ, śarīrasantānatvād, gomayajanitavṛścikaśarīrasantānavat /
na cānukūlatarkacintā kāryā, anyathāgamārthasyaivānupapattiprasaṅgāt /
hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgre bhūtasya jātaḥ patireka āsīt (ṛ saṃ 10.121.1) iti śruteḥ /
gandhavaccharīraṃ pārthivam /
children.translated_text:
2) A divine body is not non-womb-born; [the reason] 'because it is a body' is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), as seen in the body of a moth etc.
The possession of a distinctive configuration is also unestablished for that [divine body], because of the difference into three-eyed, thousand-eyed, four-armed, etc.
The subject under dispute — the bodily continuum — has a non-womb-born body, because it is a bodily continuum, like the continuum of the scorpion body born from cow-dung.
Nor should one employ favorable reasoning (<s>tarka</s>), for otherwise there would be the unwanted consequence that the meaning of scripture itself would be untenable.
[This is established] from the <s>śruti</s>: '<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> arose at the beginning of creation; he was the one lord of all that was born' (<s>Ṛg Veda</s> 10.121.1).
A body possessing <s>gandha</s> (smell) is earthen.

children.text:
3) gandhopalabdhiḥ karaṇajanyā, kāryatvāt, kuṃkumagandhābhivyañjakaghṛtavat /
gandhavadindriyaṃ ghrāṇam /
gandhavatī pṛthivī /
rūparasagandhasparśasaṅkhyāparimāṇapṛthaktvasaṃyogavibhāgaparatvāparatvagurutvadravatvasaṃskāravatī pṛthivī /
children.translated_text:
3) The perception of <s>gandha</s> (smell) is produced by an instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), because it is an effect, like clarified butter that manifests the smell of saffron.
The sense organ that possesses smell is the <s>ghrāṇa</s> (nose).
Earth possesses <s>gandha</s>.
Earth possesses <s>rūpa</s> (color), <s>rasa</s> (taste), <s>gandha</s> (smell), <s>sparśa</s> (touch), <s>saṃkhyā</s> (number), <s>parimāṇa</s> (magnitude), <s>pṛthaktva</s> (separateness), <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), <s>vibhāga</s> (disjunction), <s>paratva</s> (priority), <s>aparatva</s> (posteriority), <s>gurutva</s> (heaviness), <s>dravatva</s> (fluidity), and <s>saṃskāra</s> (tendency).

children.text: udakasya nirūpaṇam --
children.translated_text: Examination of water:

children.text:
udakatvasāmānyaṃ śarīrasamavetaṃ paramāṇujātitvāt, sattāvat /
vipratipannāḥ paramāṇavaḥ paramparayā śarīrārambhakāḥ, guruparamāṇutvāt /
na ca pārthivaparamāṇutvamupādhiḥ, tadabhāve 'pi sādhyasyānugamadarśanena dvyaṇukādiṣu samavyāptikatvābhāvāt /
adṛṣṭaviśeṣākṛṣṭatvameva tatrāpi prayojakamityanye /
tañca pūrvānumānena sādhayituṃ śakyate iti na kaścid doṣaḥ /
śītasparśavaccharīramāpyam /
rasopalabdhiḥ karaṇajanyā, kāryatvādgandhopalabdhivat /
rasanamāpyam, rūparasayormadhye rasasyaivābhivyañjakatvāllālāvat /
śītasparśavadindriyaṃ rasanam /
snehavad dravyamudakam /
rūparasasparśasaṃkhyāparimāṇapṛthaktvasaṃyogavibhāgaparatvāparatvagurutvadravatvasnehasaṃskāravadudakam /
children.translated_text:
The universal <s>udakatva</s> (water-ness) is inherent in the body [of water], because it is an atomic universal (<s>paramāṇujāti</s>), like <s>sattā</s> (existence).
The atoms under dispute successively produce bodies, because they are heavy atoms (<s>guruparamāṇu</s>).
Nor is earthen-atom-ness a limiting condition, because even in the absence of that, the <s>sādhya</s> is seen to follow [the <s>hetu</s>] — since there is no co-extensive pervasion in dyads etc.
Others [say] that the real operative factor there too is being attracted by a special unseen force (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>).
That can be established by the previous inference, so there is no fault.
A body possessing cold touch is watery (<s>āpya</s>).
The perception of <s>rasa</s> (taste) is produced by an instrument, because it is an effect, like the perception of smell.
The tongue (<s>rasana</s>) is watery, because among color and taste, it is taste alone that it manifests, like saliva.
The sense organ that possesses cold touch is the tongue.
A substance possessing <s>sneha</s> (viscosity) is water.
Water possesses <s>rūpa</s> (color), <s>rasa</s> (taste), <s>sparśa</s> (touch), <s>saṃkhyā</s> (number), <s>parimāṇa</s> (magnitude), <s>pṛthaktva</s> (separateness), <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), <s>vibhāga</s> (disjunction), <s>paratva</s> (priority), <s>aparatva</s> (posteriority), <s>gurutva</s> (heaviness), <s>dravatva</s> (fluidity), <s>sneha</s> (viscosity), and <s>saṃskāra</s> (tendency).

children.text: tejaso nirūpaṇam --
children.translated_text: Examination of fire:

children.text:
1) vivādādhyāsitāḥ paramāṇavaḥ paramparayā śarīrārambhakāḥ, rūpiparamāṇutvāt, pārthivaparamāṇuvat /
na cāpārthivaparamāṇutvādityanena manaḥparamāṇuvatprakaraṇasamatvam, so 'gnerdevayonyā āhutibhyaḥ sambūya hiraṇyaśarīra ūrdhvaṃ svargalokametītyāgamabādhāt /
na ca viśiṣṭādṛṣṭākṛṣṭatvamupādhiḥ sādhanavyāpakatvāt /
uṣṇasparśavaccharīraṃ taijasam /
children.translated_text:
1) The atoms under dispute successively produce bodies, because they are corporeal atoms (<s>rūpiparamāṇu</s>), like earthen atoms.
Nor is there equal standing with the case of mental atoms (<s>manaḥparamāṇu</s>) through [the counter-reason] 'because they are non-earthen atoms,' since this is contradicted by scripture: 'He, being born of the divine womb, from the oblations of fire, having combined into a golden body, ascends upward to the heavenly world.'
Nor is 'being attracted by a special <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen force)' a limiting condition, because it pervades the <s>sādhana</s> (probans).
A body possessing hot touch is fiery (<s>taijasa</s>).

children.text:
2) rūpopalabdhiḥ karaṇajanyā, kāryatvāt /
cakṣuḥ taijasam, rūparasayormadhye rūpasyaiva vyañjakatvādālokavat /
uṣṇamindriyaṃ taijasam /
children.translated_text:
2) The perception of <s>rūpa</s> (color) is produced by an instrument, because it is an effect.
The eye (<s>cakṣus</s>) is fiery, because among color and taste, it manifests color alone, like light.
The sense organ that is hot is fiery.

children.text: 3) vivādādhyāsitāḥ paramāṇavo na pārthivāḥ, atyantāgnisaṃyoge bhasmānārambhakatvāt, jalaparamāṇuvat /
children.translated_text: 3) The atoms under dispute are not earthen, because when in extreme conjunction with fire they do not produce ash, like water atoms.

children.text: vivādādhyāsitaṃ taijasam, aśītatve sati apākajarūpādhāraparamāṇujanyadravyatvāt, sampratipannāgnivat /
children.translated_text: The subject under dispute is fiery, because, being non-cold, it is a substance produced from atoms that are the substratum of color not produced by heating (<s>apākajarūpa</s>), like acknowledged fire.

children.text: uṣṇasparśavattejaḥ /
children.translated_text: Fire possesses hot touch.

children.text: rūpasparśasaṃkhyāparimāṇapṛthaktvasaṃyogavibhāgaparatvāparatvadravatvasaṃskāravattejaḥ //
children.translated_text: Fire possesses <s>rūpa</s> (color), <s>sparśa</s> (touch), <s>saṃkhyā</s> (number), <s>parimāṇa</s> (magnitude), <s>pṛthaktva</s> (separateness), <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), <s>vibhāga</s> (disjunction), <s>paratva</s> (priority), <s>aparatva</s> (posteriority), <s>dravatva</s> (fluidity), and <s>saṃskāra</s> (tendency).

children.text: iti ca tejaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus [the discussion of] fire [is concluded].

children.text: vāyornirūpaṇam --
children.translated_text: Examination of wind:

children.text:
1) vivādādhyāsitāḥ (vāyavīyāḥ) paramāṇavaḥ paramparayā śarīrārambhakāḥ, sparśavatparamāṇutvāt, sampratipannaparamāṇuvat /
arūpaṃ śarīraṃ vāyavīyam, mūrtatve sati tvagindriyānyatve ca sati vyāptyā tvagindriyasaṃyogādhāraḥ śarīram /
children.translated_text:
1) The atoms under dispute (of wind) successively produce bodies, because they are atoms possessing touch, like acknowledged atoms.
A formless body is of wind; being corporeal and being other than the skin-organ, through pervasion, the body is the substratum of conjunction with the skin-organ.

children.text:
2) sparśopalabdhiḥ karaṇajanyā kāryatvādrūpopalabdhivat /
sparśanaṃvāyavīyam, rūpasparśayormadhye sparśasyaivābhivyañjakadravyatvād, vyajanānilavat /
arūpāvayavīndriyaṃ sparśanam /
pūrveṣvatra ca śarīrendriyavyatirikto 'vayavī viṣayaḥ ityavagantavyam /
children.translated_text:
2) The perception of <s>sparśa</s> (touch) is produced by an instrument, because it is an effect, like the perception of color.
The organ of touch (<s>sparśana</s>) is of wind, because among color and touch, it is touch alone whose manifesting substance [it is], like the breeze from a fan.
The formless sense organ that has parts is the organ of touch.
With regard to the preceding [elements] and this one, it should be understood that a composite substance (<s>avayavin</s>) distinct from the body and the sense organ is the subject.

children.text:
3) vāyurasmadādipratyakṣaviṣayo na bhavati, vāyutvātparamāṇuvāyuvat /
na ca paramāṇutvamupādhiḥ, vāyudvayaṇukādiṣu sādhyasyānanugamadarśanāt /
vāyurasmadādipratyakṣaviṣayo na bhavati, arūpidravyatvādākāśavat /
na cāsparśavaddravyatvamupādhiḥ, sādhyāvyāpakatvāttatraivābhāvāt /
na codbhūtasparśābhāvo mahattve sati prayojakaḥ, vāristhite tejasi abhāvāt /
na ca tasyāpi pratyakṣatvam, uṣṇaṃ jalamiti vibhramānupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text:
3) Wind is not an object of our perception, because it is wind, like atomic wind.
Nor is atom-ness a limiting condition, because the <s>sādhya</s> is seen not to follow [the <s>hetu</s>] in wind-dyads etc.
Wind is not an object of our perception, because it is a formless substance, like <s>ākāśa</s> (space).
Nor is 'being a substance without touch' a limiting condition, because it does not pervade the <s>sādhya</s> — it being absent right there [in wind].
Nor is 'absence of manifest touch together with largeness' the operative factor, because of its absence in fire situated in water.
Nor is that [fire in water] also perceptible, because the illusion 'the water is hot' cannot be accounted for [otherwise].

children.text:
4) sparśanaṃ nīrūpadravyagrāhakaṃ na bhavati, bāhyendritvāccakṣurvat /
na ca vāyurasmadādipratyakṣaḥ, anudbhūtarūpānadhikaraṇatve sati udbhūtasparśādhikaraṇatvādghaṭavaditi sāmpratam, paramāṇau vyabhicārāt /
na ca mahattve satīti viśeṣaṇīyam, pratyakṣasāmagrīsadbhāvasyopādheḥ /
sā cānuvicāryamāṇā udbhūtarūpasparśamahattvānnātiricyate /
tasyāpi sādhane 'pasiddhantaḥ /
tathā nāsmadādibāhyendriyapratyakṣo vāyuḥ, asmadādyapratyakṣasaṃkhyādhikaraṇatvānnabhovat /
children.translated_text: Likewise, wind is not perceptible to our external senses, because it is a substratum of number not perceptible to us, like <s>ākāśa</s> (space).

children.text: anyathā tasyāpi bāhyendriyapratyakṣatvaprasaṅgaḥ, ubhayorapi samānasāmagrīgrāhyatvāditi /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, there would be the unwanted consequence that <s>ākāśa</s> too would be perceptible to external senses, since both are equally apprehensible by the same aggregate [of conditions].

children.text: nirūpaḥ sparśavān vāyuḥ /
children.translated_text: Wind is formless and possesses touch.

children.text: sparśasaṃkhyāparimāṇapṛthaktvasaṃyogavibhāgaparatvāparatvasaṃskāravān vāyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Wind possesses <s>sparśa</s> (touch), <s>saṃkhyā</s> (number), <s>parimāṇa</s> (magnitude), <s>pṛthaktva</s> (separateness), <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), <s>vibhāga</s> (disjunction), <s>paratva</s> (priority), <s>aparatva</s> (posteriority), and <s>saṃskāra</s> (tendency).

4) The organ of touch does not apprehend formless substances; because it is an external sense organ, like the eye.
Nor is 'wind is perceptible to us, because, while not being a substratum of non-manifest color, it is a substratum of manifest touch, like a pot' — this [argument] is correct [only] at present, because there is deviation in atoms.
Nor should one qualify with 'when large,' because that is a limiting condition of the presence of the perceptual aggregate.
And that [aggregate], when analyzed, does not differ from [the requirement of] largeness together with manifest color and touch.
In establishing that too, there is the fallacy of an unaccepted principle (<s>apasiddhānta</s>).

children.text: ākāśasya nirūpaṇam --
children.translated_text: Examination of space:

children.text:
1) vivādādhyāsitā śabdopalabdhiḥ karaṇajanyā, kāryatvādrūpopalabdhivat /
taccendriyaṃ bāhyaṃ bāhyarthaprakāśakatvāccakṣurvat /
śabdaḥ kvacidāśritaḥ, guṇatvādrūpavat /
śabdāśraya itarebhyo bhidyate, śabdāśrayatvādvyatirekeṇa rūpavat /
children.translated_text:
1) The perception of <s>śabda</s> (sound), which is the subject under dispute, is produced by an instrument, because it is an effect, like the perception of color.
That sense organ is external, because it illuminates external objects, like the eye.
<s>Śabda</s> (sound) resides in something, because it is a quality (<s>guṇa</s>), like color.
The substratum of sound differs from the others, because, by negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>), it is the substratum of sound, like color [differs from other qualities].

children.text:
2) anye tu śabdo 'ṣṭadravyātiriktadravyāśritaḥ, tadvṛtau bādhakopapattau guṇatvādvyatirekeṇa rūpavaditi bruvate /
tadasat, vyāptasiddheḥ /
vyatirekasyābhāvarūpatvena pratiyogisādhyajñānādhīnajñānatvāt, tajjñāne 'numānavaiyarthyāt /
na ca sarvāvinābhāvānāmucchedaḥ, yatra vyatirekasya bhāvarūpatvaṃ tatraitaddoṣasyābhāvāt /
ākāśagatamahattvasapakṣasyāpi saṃbhavānna kevalavyatirekitvam /
sādhye 'ṣṭadravyātiriktāśritatvamātraprayoge asādhāraṇatvam, rūpatvādisāmānyānāmapi sapakṣatvāttebhyo hetorvyāvṛtteḥ /
children.translated_text:
2) Others, however, say: sound resides in a substance other than the eight [acknowledged] substances, because, when there is a defeater for that [position], it is a quality — by negative concomitance, like color.
That is wrong, because the pervasion is [already] established.
Since negative concomitance, being of the nature of absence, depends on the knowledge of the counterpositive and the <s>sādhya</s>, and since inference becomes redundant for that knowledge.
Nor is there the destruction of all invariable concomitances, because where the negative concomitance has a positive nature, this fault does not arise.
Since a co-extensive positive example with largeness in space is also possible, it is not exclusively negative.
If the <s>sādhya</s> is formulated as merely 'residing in something other than the eight substances,' there is the fault of being an uncommon [reason], since even the universals like <s>rūpatva</s> (color-ness) etc. are positive instances, and the reason is excluded from them.

children.text:
3) vipratipannamacākṣuṣam, arūpidravyatvāt, sarvagatatvāt, sarvadā sparśarahitadravyatvāt, nityendriyatvāt, ātmavat manovacca /
ākāśarūpam, mahattve sati rūpājanakatvāt, nityamahattāt, sarvadāsparśarahitadravyatvād vāyuvadātmavacca /
vipratipannaṃ mūrtamanena saṃyuktaṃ murtatvātsampratipannavat /
aneneti vipratipannaviṣayābhiprāyeṇa /
children.translated_text:
3) The subject under dispute is non-visual, because it is a formless substance, because it is all-pervading, because it is a substance always devoid of touch, and because it is an eternal sense organ — like the <s>ātman</s> (self) and like <s>manas</s> (mind).
The nature of <s>ākāśa</s> (space) [is determined as follows]: being large, it does not produce color, it has eternal largeness, and it is a substance always devoid of touch — like wind, like the <s>ātman</s>, and like <s>manas</s>.
The subject under dispute is corporeal, being conjoined with this [corporeal substance], because of being corporeal, like the acknowledged [corporeal substances].
'With this' is intended with reference to the subject under dispute.

children.text:
4) ākāśaṃ parimāṇavat, saṃyogitvādghaṭavat /
na ca kriyāvattvamupādhiḥ, anutpannakriyasyāpi kasyacinnāśāt /
tasya tadādhāratvayogyatāṃ vihāya na kiñcidanyadasarvagatatvādatiricyate, tacca parimāṇaviśeṣaḥ /
na ca svātmani svasyopādhitvaṃ, tadatiriktasādhyākārānabhyupagamāt /
asarvagatatvasya rūpādiṣvapi saṃbhavāt, dravyatvena viśeṣaṇe viśeṣyavaiyarthyāt /
sparśavattvasya prayojaktve manaso 'parimāṇatvaprasaṅgaḥ, manasi ca tadabhāvāt /
taccāṇviti vakṣyāmaḥ /
ākāśamaparimitam, akriyatvādrūpavadityatrādravyatvamupādhiḥ /
children.translated_text:
4) <s>Ākāśa</s> (space) possesses magnitude, because it has conjunction, like a pot.
Nor is 'possessing activity' a limiting condition, because the destruction of something that has not yet produced activity [still occurs].
Nothing other than non-omnipresence (<s>asarvagatatva</s>) differs from its capacity to be the substratum of that [conjunction], and that is a specific magnitude.
Nor is something a limiting condition of itself, because one does not accept a form of the <s>sādhya</s> beyond that.
Since non-omnipresence is possible in color etc. too, qualifying with 'substance' renders the qualificand redundant.
If 'possessing touch' were the operative factor, there would be the unwanted consequence that <s>manas</s> would lack magnitude, since <s>manas</s> lacks that [touch].
And we shall state that it [manas] is atomic.
[As for the argument:] '<s>ākāśa</s> is unlimited, because it lacks activity, like color' — here 'being a non-substance' is a limiting condition.

children.text:
5) ākāśaṃ saṃyogi vibhāgi ca, dravyatvādghaṭavat /
na ca sāvayatvamupādhiḥ, tasya maduktahetugarbhitatvād, dravyate sati ārabhyatvasya tattvāt /
sarvagatendriyamākāśaṃ tadeva śrotram /
na caivaṃ sarvatra śabdopalambhaḥ, vaktṛśrotṛśarīrasannidhiśabdopalabdhiprasaṅgaḥ, tasyāpi karṇaśaṣkulyavacchinnākāśasya vidyamānatvāt /
upādhibhedācca bheda ityanarthabījam, ātmāntaḥkaraṇādīnāmapi tathābhāve virodhābhāvat /
śabdavadākāśam /
śabdasaṃkhyāparimāṇapṛthaktvasaṃyogavibhāgavat /
children.translated_text:
5) Space (<s>ākāśa</s>) possesses conjunction and disjunction, because it is a substance, like a pot.
Nor is having parts (<s>sāvayavatva</s>) a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>), since that [objection] is already contained within the stated reason — because when substancehood obtains, being producible is its true nature.
Space, which is an all-pervading sense-faculty, is itself the organ of hearing (<s>śrotra</s>).
Nor does this entail the apprehension of sound everywhere, [for that would lead to] the undesirable consequence that sound would be apprehended merely from the proximity of the speaker's and hearer's bodies, since even that [space] delimited by the ear-cavity exists [everywhere].
And the objection that difference [of space] follows from the difference of limiting adjuncts is a seed of futility, because there is no contradiction if the self (<s>ātman</s>), inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), and the like were also to be [differentiated] thus.
Space is like sound.
[Space possesses] number, measure, separateness, conjunction, and disjunction, like sound.

children.text: dikkālayornirūpaṇam --
children.translated_text: Examination of direction and time —

children.text:
vivādādhyāsitaḥ saṃyogo viśeṣaguṇarahitebhyo dravyebhyo janyate, saṃyogatvād, antaḥkaraṇarūpadvayasaṃyogavat /
vivādāspadaṃ viśeṣaguṇarahitadravyadvayajanyam, kāryatvāt, tadvadeva /
na cāntaḥkaraṇadvayasaṃyogatvamupādhiḥ, vyarthaviśeṣaṇatvāt tadvadeva /
na cāntaḥkaraṇadvayaguṇatvamupādhiḥ, dvayaguṇatvenaivopapattau viśeṣaṇavaiyarthyāt /
nirupādhikasya (sādhya)parityāge svābhāvaparityāgaprasaṅgāt /
na ca sādhye bahuvacanakṣepaṇātiprasaṅga iti vācyam, dṛṣṭāntāsiddheḥ bhūṣaṇasya saṃkhyānabhyupagamena manogatatvasya dūrāpāstatvāt /
na mano manasā saṃyujyate nityadravyatvāditi sādhane dṛṣṭāntāsiddhiḥ /
ata eva saṃyogābhyupagamenāsparśavattvād dravyānārambhakatvamityāha bhāṣyakāraḥ /
anyathā sajātīyataṃyogābhāvameva hetuṃ brūyāt, kāraṇatvātsaṃyogasya /
tathā ca vyomaśivaḥ-- `parakīyena ca manasā sūkṣmaśarīrasthaṃ manaḥ maryāyeṇābhisambandhayati' /
na cānaikāntikatvam, ajasaṃyogāsiddheḥ /
na ca vimatipadaṃ viśeṣaguṇarahitadravyābhyāṃ na janyate, antaḥkaraṇasaṃyogātiriktatvād vyomavaditi sāmpratam, akāryatvasyopādheḥ /
tayośca dikkālasajñeti /
saṃkhyāparimāṇapṛthaktvasaṃyogavibhāgayuktau dikkālau, sarvagatatvāditi pūrvavatsādhanīyam /
children.translated_text:
The conjunction under dispute is produced from substances devoid of specific qualities (<s>viśeṣaguṇa</s>), because it is a conjunction, like the conjunction of the inner organ and a pair of forms.
The object of dispute is produced from a pair of substances devoid of specific qualities, because it is an effect, in the same manner.
Nor is being a conjunction-of-two-inner-organs a limiting condition, since the qualifier would be purposeless, in the same manner.
Nor is being a quality of a pair of inner organs a limiting condition, since the qualifier would be redundant when the matter is established merely by being a quality of a pair.
If the unqualified [relation] is abandoned in the probandum, there would be the undesirable consequence of abandoning its own nature.
Nor should it be said that there is an over-extension of the plural number in the probandum, because the counter-example is unestablished — since <s>Bhūṣaṇa</s> does not accept the enumeration [of mental substances], the thesis of [conjunction being] mental has been thoroughly refuted.
The mind does not conjoin with [another] mind because it is an eternal substance — in this proof the counter-example is unestablished.
For this very reason, the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> states that, given the acceptance of conjunction, [the mind] does not produce substances because it lacks tangibility.
Otherwise one should state the very absence of conjunction with things of the same kind as the reason, since conjunction is a cause.
Thus <s>Vyomaśiva</s> [states]: 'It relates to the mind situated in the subtle body of another by means of another's mind in a regular manner.'
Nor is there inconclusiveness, since the conjunction of goats [as a counter-example] is unestablished.
Nor is the current [position] that the subject of doubt is not produced by two substances devoid of specific qualities — because it is different from the conjunction of inner organs, like space — since non-effectness would be the limiting condition.
And these two are designated as direction (<s>dik</s>) and time (<s>kāla</s>).
Direction and time possess number, measure, separateness, conjunction, and disjunction, and are all-pervading — this is to be established as before.

children.text: ātmano nirūpaṇam --
children.translated_text: Examination of the self (<s>ātman</s>) —

children.text: vivādādhyāsito 'haṃpratyayo 'haṃpratyayavyatirikte pramā pramātvāt, saṃpratipannavat /
children.translated_text: The 'I'-cognition under dispute is a valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>) regarding [something] different from the 'I'-cognition, because it is a valid cognition, like an accepted [instance of valid cognition].

children.text: ātmaiva jñānādhāraḥ--
children.translated_text: The self itself is the substratum of knowledge —

children.text:
tasya ca ko viṣaya iti cintāyāṃ paraśarīraparātmādiṣvatiprasaṅganirākaraṇārthaṃ yatra svayaṃ samavetaḥ, sa eva tasya viṣaya iti vaktavyamiti sthite ---
na śarīraṃ tatsamavāyi, kāryatvādghaṭavat /
na cāśarīratvamupādhiḥ, mṛtaśarīre tadabhāve 'pi sādhyasādhanayoranugamadarśanāt /
na cājīvaccharīratvamupādhiḥ, suṣuptau jīvaccharīre 'pi tadabhāvāt /
avasthāviśeṣavataḥ śarīrasya pakṣatvānna doṣaḥ, tathā śarīratvāt mṛtaśarīravaditi vācyam /
children.translated_text:
When one inquires what is the object of that ['I'-cognition], in order to prevent the over-extension to another's body, another's self, and so forth, the position established is that only that in which [the cognition] itself inheres is its object.
The body is not [the object] that inheres in it, because it is an effect, like a pot.
Nor is incorporeality a limiting condition, because even in a dead body, when that [self] is absent, the co-presence of probandum and probans is observed.
Nor is the body's being-without-a-living-soul a limiting condition, because even in deep sleep, when the living body is present, that [I-cognition] is absent.
It should not be said that there is no fault because the body of a particular state is the thesis-subject, and therefore [the dead body is] like a dead body because it is a body of that [same] kind.

children.text: vivādādhyāsitaḥ prāṇo na jñānādhāraḥ, kāryatvādvāyutvāt, prāṇatvāt suṣuptāvasthaprāṇavat /
children.translated_text: The vital breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) under dispute is not the substratum of knowledge, because it is an effect, because it is air, because it is a vital breath — like the vital breath in the state of deep sleep.

children.text:
vivādādhyāsitaṃ bodhādhārajaṃ kāryatvāt, ceṣṭāvat /
na ca yogyānulabdhibādhaḥ, prayatnādhārasyeva bodhādhārasya yogyatvenāpi sambhavāt, gauratvādivad bodhasya parapratyakṣāsiddheḥ /
tadviśiṣṭasyātīndriyatvānmanasaḥ parabodhagrahaṇe sāmarthyābhāvāt /
śarīrasya tu yogyānupalabdhyā bādha iti cet /
kiṃ cātaḥ? tasyaiva bodhādhāratvāttadabhāve bodhādhārasyāpi abhāva iti cet /
na, niyamāsiddheḥ /
vyāptatvānnaivamiti cet, tarhyanumānena bādho vakyavyaḥ, tatra cāśrayanirūpaṇaṃ durghaṭam /
vivādādhyāsitaṃ bodhādhārajaṃ na bhavati, śarīrajanyatvādākāśavaditi prāgeva vyudastam /
śarīrajanyatvopādhivāde 'pi mṛtaśarīrakriyādiṣu vyabhicāravāraṇārthaṃ bodhādhārapūrvakatvamabhyupagantavyam /
tadvyatiriktatve satīti viśeṣaṇaṃ copādeyam /
tatrāpi suṣuptaśarīrakriyādiṣu vyabhicāraparihārāya jāgrata iti viśeṣaṇaprāpte, atrāpyudāsīnasyākasmikanipatitakriyāparihārārthaṃ kurvata iti vaktavyam /
svasyaiva prayāsādhikyamuktaṃ syādvyarthaviśeṣaṇatvaṃ coktaṃ pūrvam /
upādhiravinābhūtadharmadharmatvena bhavatyevaitaddūṣaṇam /
anyathānumānāntareṣvapi tanna syāt /
nirupādhikasya sambandhasya vyāptitvenopādhibhaṅge jāte, kvacitsambandhe ca dṛṣṭe, anyatra kevalasya hetordarśanamapi na doṣamāvahatītyavocamityalam /
children.translated_text:
The subject of dispute is an effect of the substratum of cognition, because it is an effect, like bodily effort.
Nor is there the defeat of non-apprehension by a competent observer (<s>yogyānupalabdhi</s>), because the substratum of cognition, like the substratum of effort, is also possible as a competent [object], since cognition, being like heaviness and the like, is not established as perceivable by others — and because the mind, being supersensory, lacks the capacity to apprehend another's cognition, since what is qualified by that [cognition] is beyond the senses.
If [one objects:] 'there is a defeat by non-apprehension by a competent observer with respect to the body' —
what follows from that? If [one argues:] 'since that [body] itself is the substratum of cognition, in its absence the substratum of cognition would also be absent' —
no, because the invariable concomitance is not established.
If [one argues:] 'this is so because of pervasion,' then the defeat should be stated through inference, and therein establishing the locus is difficult to accomplish.
The subject of dispute is not an effect of the substratum of cognition, because it is produced by the body, like space — this was already refuted previously.
Even on the view that 'produced by the body' is a limiting condition, in order to prevent deviation in cases such as the actions of a dead body, one must accept that [it is] preceded by the substratum of cognition.
And the qualifier 'being different from that [substratum]' should be adopted.
Therein too, in order to prevent deviation in cases such as the actions of a sleeping body, when the qualifier 'waking' is due, here again, to prevent the actions of an indifferent person struck unexpectedly, one should state 'of one who acts.'
This would mean excessive effort on one's own part, and the purposelessness of the qualifiers was already stated.
A limiting condition consists precisely in having the relation of property and property-possessor as an inseparable attribute — this is the very refutation.
Otherwise, it would not apply to other inferences either.
When the invariable connection without limiting conditions is [accepted] as pervasion, and once the limiting condition is broken, and when the connection is observed in some case, the observation of the bare reason elsewhere also does not bring about a fault — so we have stated. Enough of this.

children.text: prabhākaramatanirāsaḥ --
children.translated_text: Refutation of the <s>Prābhākara</s> view —

children.text:
anye tu sarvārthavittiṣu grāhakatvena ātmasiddhiriti bruvate /
tadasat, ātmano 'pi cākṣuṣatvaprasaṅgāt, tajjanitajñāne bhāsamānatvasyaiva tattvāt /
yadi ca nīrūpadravyasyāpi cākṣuṣatvam, tadā nabhaso 'pi tathātvaprasaṅgāt /
na cātmā cākṣuṣajñāne prakāśate nīrūpadravyatvādgaganavat /
vivādādhyāsitaṃ jñānamātmapratibhāsam, jñānatvādahamitisampratipannavaditi cet, na, kālātyayāpadeśāt /
tathā hi --- asti tāvat saugatatacchiṣyāṇāmanātmavāsanāto viṣayebhyo nivṛtiḥ, anātmavāsanātaśca pravṛtiriti /
na ca te pramāṇamūle eveti niyamaḥ, rajjusarpavivekāgrahaṇādvā vibhramādvā śuktirajatavivekāgrahaṇādvā vibhramādvānayoranudayaprasaṅgāt /
na ca te na nivṛttī, nāpi pravṛttī vā /
na cājñānupūrvikā nivṛttiḥ pravṛttirvā svasthasya saṃbhavati /
na cātmajñāne teṣāṃ tadupapadyate, tathānabhyāsadaśāyāṃ ko 'hamitya(dhyavasāyānupapattirniścīyate), anadhyavasāye 'tiprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text:
Others, however, maintain that the self is established through being the apprehender in all cognitions of objects.
This is wrong, because there would be the undesirable consequence that the self too would be perceptible by the eye, since appearing in the cognition produced by that [eye] is precisely what constitutes being [visual].
If even a substance without form were visual, then there would be the consequence that space too would be likewise.
Nor does the self appear in visual cognition, because it is a formless substance, like the sky.
If [one argues:] 'the cognition under dispute has the self as its appearance, because it is a cognition, like the accepted "I" [-cognition]' — no, because of the fault of advancing an expired argument (<s>kālātyayāpadēśa</s>).
For consider: there is indeed, on the part of the Buddhists and their followers, withdrawal from objects due to the habitual impression of non-self, and engagement due to habitual impressions of non-self.
Nor is there a necessary rule that these are based on valid means of knowledge, for otherwise the non-arising of [withdrawal from] a rope-snake due to either non-apprehension of the distinction or error, or [non-arising of] shell-silver due to either non-apprehension of the distinction or error, would follow.
Nor do they [i.e., the Buddhists] not have withdrawal, nor do they not have engagement.
Nor is withdrawal or engagement preceded by [that specific] knowledge possible for one who is in a normal state.
Nor, if they had self-knowledge, would that be tenable for them, since in the state of non-habituation, the impossibility of the determination 'who am I?' is ascertained — because over-extension would follow in the absence of such determination.

children.text:
kiṃ ca kaḥ punastatpratibhāse sambandhārthaḥ? karmatvam, tadatiriktaṃ vā? prathame 'pasiddhantaḥ, dvitīye dṛṣṭāntāsiddhiḥ* /
[* -eḥ edn] viṣayatvaṃ ca prathamānnātiricyate /
grāhakagṛhītibhāve tu siddhasādhanam /
ato 'tiriktasyānugatasambandhamātrasyāsiddhiḥ /
kiṃ ca yogināṃ viyuktāvasthāyāṃ paramāṇurūpādiviṣayacākṣuṣajñānasya pakṣīkāre bhavatāmāśrayaikadeśāsiddhaḥ, anyathāsmākamanaikāntaḥ /
na ca mānasapratyakṣatve tatsāmagrayāḥ sarvadā sannihitatvāt suṣuptāvasthāyāmapyātmajñānaprasaṅgaḥ, ahaṃ śarīramitivivekāgrahaṇādiṣu ahaṃjñānotpattau bāhyendriyavyatiriktakārakagrāmasyaiva tvayāpi vaktavyatvāttadbalenaiva sarvasyopapatteḥ, tathāvidhakarmavaikalyādvā /
tasmānna sarvavittiṣvātmanaḥ* pratibhāsaḥ /
[* sarvavidiṣvā]
children.translated_text:
Moreover, what is the relational meaning in that appearance [of self]? Is it objectness, or something beyond that? In the first case, there is a contravention of one's own doctrine; in the second, the example is unestablished.
And objectness is not different from the first.
But [establishing] the apprehender-apprehension relation would be proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>).
Therefore the invariably accompanying relation beyond [objectness] is unestablished.
Moreover, for yogins in the state of disjunction, when the visual cognition having atomic form and the like as its object is taken as the thesis, there is a partial failure of your own basis; otherwise, for us, inconclusiveness.
Nor, if [the cognition were] mental perception, would there be the undesirable consequence of self-knowledge even in deep sleep — since the assemblage of [conditions for] that is always present — because even in cases of non-apprehension of the distinction 'I am the body,' when I-cognition arises, the group of causal factors other than external sense-faculties must be acknowledged by you as well, and everything is explained by the force of that alone — or because of the deficiency of <s>karma</s> of that kind.
Therefore, the self does not appear in all cognitions.

children.text: ātmano jñānarūpatvanirāsaḥ--
children.translated_text: Refutation of the self being of the nature of knowledge —

children.text:
sa ca jñānāśrayo na tu vijñānātmakaḥ, na hi draṣṭurdṛṣṭerviparilopo vidyate (bṛha 4.3.23) iti śrutau draṣṭṛdṛṣṭyoḥ sambandhapratīteḥ /
na cāmnāyapratīto bhrānto bhavitumarhati, aviśeṣāt /
na ca siddhārthe vācakābhāvaḥ, apasiddhāntāt /
na cātatparatvam, tasyānyato 'siddhatvena viśiṣṭaparatvāt /
na ca rāhoḥ śira itivadupacaritatvam, mukhye bādhakābhāvāt /
na cādvaitaśrutirbādhikā, viparyaye pratyuta tasya bhedagrāhakatvāt /
na ca tatra tasya sāmarthyaṃ nāstīti vācyam, sāmarthye sati virodhābhāvāt /
na ca sambandhābhāve grahaṇāsambhavaḥ, adoṣatvāt /
na cātiprasaṅgaḥ, anupalabdherniyāmakatvāt /
pratiyogitatprayuktavyatiriktasāmagrīsānnidhye sati pratiyogijñāne ca sati niyāmakatvāt /
athavā karaṇasambandhasyaiva niyāmakatvāt /
tathā hi -- ghaṭasaṃyuktena cakṣuṣā janitaṃ jñānaṃ ghaṭamevāvagāhate nārthāntaram, asambaddhatvāt /
kiñcāsti tāvadiyaṃ prasiddhiḥ, 'ata eva vyavaharāmaḥ' itivacanāt /
tasyāśca kāraṇābhāve sati nityatvaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text:
And that [self] is the support of knowledge (<s>jñānāśraya</s>), but not of the nature of consciousness (<s>vijñānātmaka</s>), for in the <s>śruti</s> "the vision of the seer is never lost" (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.23), a relation between the seer (<s>draṣṭṛ</s>) and seeing (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) is apprehended.
Nor can what is apprehended through scripture (<s>āmnāya</s>) be erroneous, since there is no distinguishing reason [to think so].
Nor is there absence of a signifying word for an established referent, since that would violate the accepted doctrine (<s>apasiddhānta</s>).
Nor is [the scripture] not intended for that [meaning], because since that [meaning] is otherwise unestablished, [the scripture] has the force of establishing precisely that qualified [meaning].
Nor is it figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>) as in "the head of <s>Rāhu</s>," since there is no sublating cognition against the primary meaning.
Nor does the <s>Advaita</s> scripture sublate [this], for in the contrary case it would rather be that [scripture] which grasps difference.
Nor should it be said that it has no capacity there, for where there is capacity there is no contradiction.
Nor is apprehension impossible in the absence of a relation [between knower and known], since that is not a defect.
Nor is there overextension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>), because non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) serves as the delimiter;
since the delimiter operates when the aggregate of conditions other than those produced by the counter-positive (<s>pratiyogin</s>) is present, and when there is cognition of the counter-positive.
Alternatively, because the instrumental relation (<s>karaṇasambandha</s>) itself is the delimiter.
Thus — cognition produced by the eye conjoined with a pot apprehends only the pot and not some other object, due to the absence of connection [with other objects].
Moreover, this much is well-established, as stated by the dictum "it is for this very reason that we engage in ordinary practice."
And in the absence of a cause for [the destruction of] that [well-established cognition], it would be eternal.

children.text:
na caivamapratyakṣatvaṃ bhedasya, samyagaparokṣānubhavaviṣayasyaiva sattvāt /
nityatve ca trayāṇāṃ siddheḥ /
na cāpasiddhāntaḥ, asmākamapi nityapratītisiddheḥ /
na ca bhedānavasthā bādhikā, bhedāntaraprasaktau mūlābhāvāt /
bhedabhedinau bhinnāviti lokavyavahāradarśanāt /
na caikabhedabalenānyabhedānumānam, dṛṣṭāntabhedāvighātenotthāne doṣābhāvāt /
so 'yaṃ piṇyākayācanārthaṃ gatasyāpi śākādinaḥ khārikātailadātṛtvābhyupagama iva /
dṛṣṭāntabhedavighāte tvanumānānutthānameva, upajīvyasya prabalatvena tenaiva bādhāt /
svātmavyātakatvena jātitvāt /
etenādṛśyatvādayo nirastāḥ /
children.translated_text:
Nor is difference thereby imperceptible, since it exists only as the object of correct non-mediate experience (<s>samyag aparokṣānubhava</s>).
And if [difference is] eternal, the triad [of knower, known, and knowledge] is established.
Nor is there violation of accepted doctrine (<s>apasiddhānta</s>), since for us too the eternality of cognition [of difference] is established.
Nor does an infinite regress of differences sublate [our position], because when a further difference is entailed, there is absence of the ground [for regress];
for it is observed in ordinary practice that "difference and that which differs are themselves different."
Nor is another difference inferred merely on the strength of one difference, since there is no fault when [inference] arises without disruption of the example's difference.
This is like the case of one who, having gone to beg for oil-cake, is [also] acknowledged as a giver of a <s>khārikā</s>-measure of oil and the like.
But when the example's difference is disrupted, there is simply no arising of the inference, since that which is depended upon (<s>upajīvya</s>) is stronger and sublates by its own force.
[Difference has] the nature of a universal (<s>jāti</s>) by pervading its own locus (<s>svātmavyātakatva</s>).
By this, [objections based on] invisibility and the like are also refuted.

children.text:
na cānirvacanīyatvaṃ bhedasya, tatra pramāṇābhāvāt /
khyātibādhānyathānupapattiḥ pramāṇamiti cet, anyathāpyupapattau virodhabhāvāt /
asato bhāsamānāyogāt, bādhāyogātsataḥ, atra cobhayaṃ dṛśyate iti cet, na; prathame 'satpadasya bodhakatve bhāsamānāyogādityanena vyāghātaḥ /
anyathāpārthakatvam, prayuktapadārthānāṃ sambhūyakāritvaniyamāt /
dvitīye sata iti ko 'rthaḥ? kiṃ sattāyuktasya, āhosvidabādhitasya, brahmāsvarūpasya vā? prathame sattāyuktasyābādhitatvena vyāptiḥ kutraḥ dṛṣṭā? prapañcasya bādhyatvād, brahmaṇo nirdhamakatvena sattābhāvāt /
dvitīye sādhyāviśiṣṭatā /
tṛtīye siddhasādhanatā /
tasmānnānirvacanīyatvamapi /
children.translated_text:
Nor is difference of the nature of the indescribable (<s>anirvacanīya</s>), since there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) for that.
If it is said that the impossibility of explaining otherwise the [simultaneous] appearance and sublation is the <s>pramāṇa</s> — [we reply:] since there is no contradiction even when explained otherwise.
If it is said: because what is non-existent (<s>asat</s>) cannot appear, and because what is existent (<s>sat</s>) cannot be sublated, and here both are observed — no; in the first [alternative], if the word "non-existent" (<s>asat</s>) is taken as conveying [mere] awareness, there is contradiction with the statement "because what is non-existent cannot appear."
Otherwise it would be purposeless, since the meanings of the words employed are necessarily jointly operative.
In the second [alternative]: what is the meaning of "existent" (<s>sat</s>)? Is it that which possesses existence (<s>sattā</s>), or that which is unsublated, or that which is the very nature of <s>Brahman</s>? In the first case, where has the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) been observed that what possesses <s>sattā</s> is unsublatable? — since the empirical world (<s>prapañca</s>) is [admitted by you to be] sublatable, and since <s>Brahman</s>, being beyond predication (<s>nirdharmaka</s>), lacks <s>sattā</s>.
In the second case, there is no distinction from the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved).
In the third case, it is the fallacy of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>).
Therefore, indescribability (<s>anirvacanīyatva</s>) is also untenable.

children.text: akhaṇḍārthatvakhaṇḍanam--
children.translated_text: Refutation of the doctrine of indivisible meaning (<s>akhaṇḍārtha</s>)

children.text:
etena yadāhurekadaṇḍinaḥ -- satyādipadamakhaṇḍaparam, lakṣaṇavākyatvād, gandhavatī pṛthivītivat, ghaṭaḥ kalaśa itivadvā /
tadapi nirastam, akhaṇḍaparanityanyūnānatiriktārthamityartho yata iti /
na cārdvatapakṣe satyajñānānandādiśabdānāṃ sahaprayogo ghaṭate, paryāyatvāt /
aparyāyatve 'dvaitahāniḥ /
na ca `prakṛṣṭaḥ prakāśaḥ savitā' itivat śabdadvayenāpi eka evārthaḥ pratipādyate iti yuktam, dṛṣṭāntāsiddheḥ /
prakṛṣṭaśabdasyetaretarābhāvādinimittasavyapekṣatayā pravṛtteḥ, prakāśaśabdasya prakāśatvabalāt, anyathā tatrāpi paryanuyogasya tulyatvāt /
children.translated_text:
By this, what the followers of <s>Ekadaṇḍin</s> [i.e., Advaita <s>sannyāsins</s>] say — that the words "existence" (<s>satya</s>) and so on refer to an indivisible meaning (<s>akhaṇḍārtha</s>), because ["<s>satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma</s>"] is a definitional sentence (<s>lakṣaṇavākya</s>), like "earth has smell" or like "a pot is a <s>kalaśa</s>" —
that too is refuted, since the meaning [of our refutation] is that there is no meaning that is invariably neither less nor more than an indivisible referent.
Moreover, on the Advaita position, the co-occurrence of the words "existence" (<s>satya</s>), "knowledge" (<s>jñāna</s>), "bliss" (<s>ānanda</s>), and so on is not coherent, since [on that view] they are synonyms (<s>paryāya</s>).
If they are not synonyms, then non-duality (<s>advaita</s>) is lost.
Nor is it proper [to claim] that even with two words, only a single meaning is conveyed, as in "the brilliant one, the luminous one, is the sun" — because the example is not established;
for the word "brilliant" (<s>prakṛṣṭa</s>) is used with dependence on factors such as mutual absence [of other qualities], while the word "luminous" (<s>prakāśa</s>) [is used] on the strength of the property of luminosity; otherwise the same objection would apply there too.

children.text:
kiṃ ca loke yathā prakṛṣṭaprakāśaśabdayoḥ parasparavyatirekeṇa prayogaḥ --- prakṛṣṭaḥ pumān, pradīpaḥ prakāśa iti /
dvayoścaikatra mayūkhamālini prayuktayostu arthaviśeṣabodhakatvam /
na caivaṃ jñānānandaśabdayorasti, laukikajñānānandasyāpi brahmarūpatvāt /
bhedena vyutpattau bhagno 'dvaitavādaḥ /
tasmādānandaśabdo duḥkhabhāvamātre prayuktaḥ, mukhye bādhakasambhavāt --- 'aśarīraṃ vāva santaṃ na priyāpriye spṛśataḥ' (chā u 8.12.1) iti vacanāt /
na cāsya sāṃsārikasukhaniṣedhaparatvam, sukhadvayasyābhāvāt /
loke 'pi mātrayā paramānandapratītirityabhyupagamāt /
na cātrāvacchinnasukhaniṣedhārtham, tatrāpyavacchedasyaiva niṣedho na sukhasya /
na ca sāmānyaśabdasya saṃkoce pramāṇamasti /
na cānandaśrutiḥ pramāṇam, tasyā upacaritārthatvāt /
na ca viparyayaḥ, ānandasya sarvadā-adarśanenānityatvaprāptau mokṣatvavyāghātāt /
yogarddhisamāsāditacirakālopabhogayogyasukhaviśeṣaparatvenāpyupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text:
Furthermore, in ordinary usage, the words "brilliant" (<s>prakṛṣṭa</s>) and "luminous" (<s>prakāśa</s>) are used independently of each other — as in "a brilliant man" and "a lamp is luminous."
When both are applied together to a single [object], such as the sun (<s>mayūkhamālin</s>), they convey a specific qualified meaning.
But this is not the case with the words "knowledge" (<s>jñāna</s>) and "bliss" (<s>ānanda</s>), since even ordinary knowledge and bliss would [on the Advaita view] be of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>.
If [these words] are learned as conveying different meanings, the <s>Advaita</s> doctrine is broken.
Therefore the word "bliss" (<s>ānanda</s>) is used merely in the sense of the absence of suffering, since a sublating cognition against the primary meaning is possible — from the statement: "when one is incorporeal, pleasant and unpleasant [experiences] do not touch [one]" (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.12.1).
Nor is this [statement] intended merely to negate worldly pleasure, since there are not two kinds of pleasure.
Since it is accepted that even in ordinary life, supreme bliss is experienced in [limited] measure.
Nor is the purpose here to negate limited (<s>avacchinna</s>) pleasure, for there too it is only the limitation that is negated, not the pleasure itself.
Nor is there a <s>pramāṇa</s> for restricting [the scope of] a general term.
Nor is the <s>ānanda</s> scripture a [valid] <s>pramāṇa</s> [for positive bliss as <s>Brahman's</s> nature], since its meaning is figurative (<s>upacāra</s>).
Nor is the reverse [the case], for since <s>ānanda</s> is never always observed [as eternal], the consequence of impermanence would contradict [its being] the state of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>).
Because it can also be explained as referring to a special pleasure suitable for long enjoyment attained through yogic powers (<s>yogarddhi</s>).

children.text:
anantatvādiśrutistu āpekṣikasukhādyapekṣayā bahukālatvena vyākhyeyā, 'amṛtā devā' itivat /
na ca pravṛttyanupapattiḥ, nityatve sutarāmanupapatteḥ /
na hi siddhasya sampādanāya kaścid yatate 'tra /
avacchedanivṛttyarthamiti cet, tarhi prāptāprāptavivekino 'trāvacchedanivṛttireva kṛtyuddeśyā, anyasya vidyamānasyāpyatantratvāt /
na caikanityasukhavāde kāraṇopādānaṃ ghaṭate, tadviśeṣe tu kaiva kathā? na caikasyaivātiśayānatiśayau śaṅkārhau, ekatvavyāghātāt /
avacchedanivṛttyarthaṃ kāraṇaviśeṣopādānamiti vaktavyam, tatra ca duḥkhābhāvasya sukhatvenānubhavasya niratiśayatvāt, tadanupapattiriti yo 'yaṃ doṣa uktaḥ, sa samānaḥ /
tasmād duḥkhābhāvātiriktasukhasādhanaparyālocanayā janyamanityamanekaṃ cābhyupeyam /
na ca tathāvidhasya muktau kathāsambhava iti /
children.translated_text:
The scripture [speaking of] infinitude and the like should be explained as [indicating] long duration relative to lesser pleasures, like [the expression] "the gods are immortal" (<s>amṛtā devāḥ</s>).
Nor is there the problem of non-motivation [for practice], since if [bliss were] eternal, the problem of motivation would be even greater;
for no one here strives to achieve what is already accomplished.
If it is said [the striving is] for the removal of limitation (<s>avaccheda</s>) — then for one who discriminates between what is [already] attained and what is not attained, only the removal of limitation is the intended goal, since anything else, even if present, is not relevant.
Moreover, on the doctrine of a single eternal pleasure, the specification of a [particular] cause is not coherent — and regarding a specific [degree of] that, what need even to speak? Nor can the doubt of degrees of intensity and non-intensity apply to a single [entity], as that would contradict its unity.
It must be said that the specification of a particular cause is for the purpose of removing limitation, but then the objection already stated applies equally — since the experience of the absence of suffering as pleasure is unsurpassable, [and hence] that [specification of cause] is inexplicable.
Therefore, a pleasure distinct from mere absence of suffering must be accepted as the means [of liberation], and it must be acknowledged as produced, impermanent, and manifold.
Nor is it the case that such [a pleasure] is impossible in the state of liberation (<s>mukti</s>).

children.text:
jñānaśabdaśca jñāyate 'sminnityadhikaraṇavācakaḥ /
ānantyaṃ punarūbhayāntābhāva eva, tatraiva lokavyutpatteḥ /
ekamiti ca dvairūpyanirākaraṇaparam, ekatvasaṃkhyāṃ vācaṣṭe, loke tatraiva vyutpatteḥ, lokāvagataśakteśca vede bodhakatvāt /
tasmājjñānāśraya ātmeti siddham /
children.translated_text:
And the word "knowledge" (<s>jñāna</s>) means "that in which [things] are known" — it denotes a permanent substratum (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>).
Infinitude (<s>ānantya</s>), moreover, is simply the absence of both ends [i.e., beginning and end], since ordinary usage is established only in that sense.
And "one" (<s>eka</s>) is intended to negate duality of form, [and] it denotes the number oneness (<s>ekatvasaṃkhyā</s>), since ordinary usage is established in that sense alone, and because in the <s>Veda</s>, words convey meaning through their powers as understood in ordinary usage.
Therefore, it is established that the self (<s>ātman</s>) is the support of knowledge (<s>jñānāśraya</s>).

children.text: ātmano nānātvam--
children.translated_text: The multiplicity of the self (<s>ātman</s>)

children.text:
vivādādhyāsitaṃ mayā sambaddhaṃ mūrtatvāt, maccharīravad -- iti nityatvānāditvasarvagatatvasiddhiḥ /
tasya cānekatvam, vyavasthānyathānupapatteḥ /
anirvacanīyatve nirākṛte jīvabhede 'vipratipatteśca /
dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānaṃ vṛkṣaṃ pariṣasvajāte /
tayoranyaḥ pippalaṃ svādvattyanaśnannanyo abhicākaśīti /
(mu 3.1.1) iti śruteḥ /
asyā arthaḥ -- dvau suparṇau ātmānau sayujau = sahavartamānau sakhāyau = ekakāryakāritvena, samānaṃ vṛkṣam = ekaṃ śarīraṃ pariṣasvajāte = āliṅgitavantau /
tayorātmanormadhye eko = bhoktā pippalaṃ svādu atti = sukhaviśeṣaṃ bhuṅkte /
anaśnan anyaḥ = abhoktā īśvaraḥ abhicākaśīti = sarvato 'tyarthaṃ prakāśate iti vispaṣṭo jīvabrahmaṇorbhedaḥ /
ajāmekāṃ lohitaśuklakṛṣṇāṃ bahvīḥ prajāḥ sṛjamānāṃ sarūpāḥ /
ajo hyeko juṣamāṇo 'nuśete jahātyenāṃ bhuktabhogāmajo 'nyaḥ /
(śvetā 4.5) itivat /
na ca śrutipratīto 'nyathā bhavitumarhati /
children.translated_text:
"That which is superimposed in the dispute is connected with me, because it is corporeal (<s>mūrtatva</s>), like my body" — thus are established eternality, beginninglessness, and omnipresence [of the self].
And its multiplicity [is established] because the orderly arrangement [of different experiences among different persons] cannot be explained otherwise.
Since indescribability (<s>anirvacanīyatva</s>) has been refuted, and since there is no dispute regarding the difference of individual souls (<s>jīva</s>),
[the <s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s> states:] "Two birds, companions, always united, cling to the same tree.
Of these two, one eats the sweet fruit, while the other, not eating, merely watches."
(<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.1.1) — thus says the <s>śruti</s>.
The meaning of this is: the two birds are two selves (<s>ātman</s>), "united" (<s>sayuj</s>) means co-existing, "companions" (<s>sakhā</s>) means working toward a common purpose, "the same tree" means a single body, and "cling to" means they have embraced [i.e., are associated with it].
Of these two selves, one — the enjoyer (<s>bhoktā</s>) — "eats the sweet fruit" means enjoys a particular pleasure.
"Not eating, the other" — the non-enjoyer, <s>Īśvara</s> — "shines forth" means illumines everything exceedingly — thus the difference between the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) and <s>Brahman</s> is clearly [stated].
[Similarly, the <s>Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad</s> states:] "The unborn one (<s>ajā</s>), the one [<s>Prakṛti</s>] of red, white, and black [colors], producing many offspring of similar form;
the one unborn male (<s>aja</s>) lies with her, enjoying; the other unborn one (<s>aja</s>) abandons her whose pleasures have been consumed."
(<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 4.5) — and so on.
Nor can what is apprehended through <s>śruti</s> be otherwise [than its apparent meaning].

children.text:
kathaṃ tarhi `neha nānāsti kiṃcana' (bṛha 4.4.19) iti, `mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyumāpnoti, ya iha nāneva paśyati' (kaṭha 4.10) iti ca, (liṅgāt) nānātvadarśane tadbhāvopacārāt /
na ca sati prayojane nimitte copacāraḥ pravartate, na cātra prayojanamastīti vācyam, niyamāsiddheḥ /
ajñātamukhyeṣu yavavarāhādiṣu gauṇaśabdaprayogeṣu tadabhāvāt /
sattābodhakalākṣaṇikagośabde ca, yathā gaurvāhīkaḥ /
yathāhurvārtikakārāḥ ---
children.translated_text:
Then how [do you explain]: "there is no multiplicity here whatsoever" (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.19), and "he who sees multiplicity here, as it were, goes from death to death" (<s>Kaṭha</s> 4.10)? — [We reply:] from the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) [in these passages], when multiplicity is perceived, [the statements are] figurative attribution of that [non-difference] to [the state of seeing difference].
Nor should it be said that figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>) requires both a purpose and an occasion, and that here there is no purpose — because that restriction is not established;
since in the figurative uses of words like "barley" (<s>yava</s>), "boar" (<s>varāha</s>), and so on, whose primary meanings are unknown, that [requirement] is absent.
And [consider] the word "cow" (<s>go</s>) used in a conventional sense to mean a <s>Vāhīka</s> person, [where the connection is] merely through the <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) that conveys existence (<s>sattā</s>), as in "that <s>Vāhīka</s> is a cow."
As the authors of the <s>Vārtika</s> say —

children.text: bahujātiguṇadravyakarmabhedāvalambinaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Words] dependent on the distinctions of many universals (<s>jāti</s>), qualities (<s>guṇa</s>), substances (<s>dravya</s>), and actions (<s>karman</s>) —

children.text: pratyayān sahasājātān śrautalākṣaṇikātmakān //
children.translated_text: cognitions that arise simultaneously, of the nature of Vedic (<s>śrauta</s>) and inferential (<s>lākṣaṇika</s>) [criteria]—

children.text: na lokaḥ kāraṇābhāvānnirdhārayitumicchati /
children.translated_text: ordinary people, due to the absence of [discerning] causes, do not wish to determine [them];

children.text: balābalādisidhyarthaṃ vākyajñāstu viviñcate //
children.translated_text: but those who know sentences (<s>vākyajñas</s>) discriminate [them] for the purpose of establishing [relative] strength and weakness.

children.text: (ślo vā??)
children.translated_text: (<s>Ślokavārttika</s> [?])

children.text:
asmadādigauṇapratīterhi cintā /
vṛddhavyavahārāgateṣu gauṇaprayogeṣu ko 'yamāgrahaḥ, yathā sarṣaparase tailaśabdaḥ? mukhyeṣu bādhakābhāvāt kathamupacāra iti nāśaṅkanīyam, pratyakṣeṇa śrutyā ca bhedapratīteḥ /
ātmā dravyatvavyatiriktāparajātyādhārabhedena nānā, aśrāvaṇaviśeṣaguṇādhikaraṇatvāt, pṛthivyādivat /
tatra na mūrtatvamupādhiḥ, rūpādau tadabhāve 'pi sādhyānugamadarśanāt /
children.translated_text: Now the examination of the secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>) cognition with respect to 'I' and so forth. In secondary usages that have come down through the conventions of the learned, what is this insistence, as with the word 'oil' (<s>taila</s>) applied to mustard extract? It should not be objected 'how can there be figurative usage when there is no invalidator for the primary [meaning],' because the distinction [between self and body] is cognized through direct perception and scripture. The self (<s>ātman</s>) is multiple, being differentiated by being the substrate of a distinct class (<s>jāti</s>) other than substance-ness, because it is the substrate of non-Vedically-revealed specific qualities, like earth and so forth. Therein, corporeality (<s>mūrtatva</s>) is not a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>), because even in form and so forth where that [corporeality] is absent, the accompaniment of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is observed.

children.text:
makarandastu vivādapadāni śarīrāṇi, ekenātmanātmavanti, śarīratvāt, maccharīravaditi /
tasya nityatvam /
viśeṣaguṇā dravyatvena sādhanīyāḥ /
tasya guṇāḥ -- buddhisukhaduḥkhecchādveṣaprayatnadharmabhāvanāsaṃkhyāparimāṇapṛthaktvasaṃyogavibhāgāḥ /
prayatnāśraya ātmā /
children.translated_text: <s>Makaranda</s>, however, [argues]: the bodies that are the subject of dispute are possessed of a single self, because they are bodies, like my body. That [self] is eternal. The specific qualities are to be established through substance-ness. Its qualities are: cognition (<s>buddhi</s>), pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), pain (<s>duḥkha</s>), desire (<s>icchā</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), effort (<s>prayatna</s>), merit (<s>dharma</s>), mental impression (<s>bhāvanā</s>), number (<s>saṃkhyā</s>), magnitude (<s>parimāṇa</s>), separateness (<s>pṛthaktva</s>), conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), and disjunction (<s>vibhāga</s>). The self (<s>ātman</s>) is the substrate of effort.

children.text: manaso nirūpaṇam--
children.translated_text: Examination of Mind (<s>manas</s>)

children.text:
vivādapadamindriyajajñānaviṣayaḥ, vastutvād ghaṭavat /
vivādādhyāsito mūrtasaṃyogāsamavāyikāraṇakaviśeṣaguṇādhāraḥ, nityatve sati anityaviśeṣaṇaguṇavattvāt, pārthivaparamāṇuvat /
na ca tattvamupādhiḥ, tvanmate ghaṭasyāpyagnisaṃyogajaviśeṣaguṇādhāratvāt /
na ca pārthivatvamupādhiḥ, tvanmate ghaṭasyāpyagnisaṃyogajaviśeṣaguṇādhāratvāt /
na ca pārthivatvamupādhiḥ, apakvanaṣṭaghaṭe vyabhicārāt /
na cāsmākamādyamupādhiḥ, nabhasi tadabhāve 'pi sādhyānugamadarśanāt /
children.translated_text: The subject of dispute is the object of knowledge produced by the sense organs, because it is a real entity (<s>vastu</s>), like a pot. The subject of dispute is the substrate of specific qualities having conjunction with corporeal [entities] as a non-inherence cause (<s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>), because while being eternal, it possesses non-eternal specific qualities, like an earthen atom (<s>pārthiva-paramāṇu</s>). And that-ness is not a limiting condition, because in your view too, a pot is the substrate of specific qualities produced by conjunction with fire. And earthen-ness (<s>pārthivatva</s>) is not a limiting condition, because in your view too, a pot is the substrate of specific qualities produced by conjunction with fire. And earthen-ness is not a limiting condition, because of deviation in an unbaked and destroyed pot. And for us the first is not a limiting condition, because even in space (<s>nabhas</s>), where that [earthen-ness] is absent, the accompaniment of the <s>sādhya</s> is observed.

children.text:
manaḥ paramāṇu, paraviśeṣaguṇāsamavāyikāraṇāśrayatve sati nityatvāt, taijasaparamāṇuvaditi kecit /
tanna, sparśavattve sati nityatvopādheḥ /
aṇutvamātrasādhane sparśavadamahattvamupādhiḥ /
mūrtatvamātrasādhane ca nityapadavaiyarthyam /
tadvyatirikttasya hetutve kāśikākṛto mate sparśavattvamupādhiḥ /
tamodravyatvapakṣe sparśavattvasya tamasyeva sādhyavyāpakatve dravyasamavāyidravyatvamupādhiḥ /
etena mano mūrtaṃ vibhusaṃyogitvādghaṭavadityapi nirastam, uktopādhikatvāt /
children.translated_text: The mind (<s>manas</s>) is atomic (<s>paramāṇu</s>), because while being the substrate of specific qualities distinct from others as a non-inherence cause, it is eternal, like a fiery atom — so some say. This is not so, because 'possessing touch' is a limiting condition when the qualifier is eternality. In establishing mere atomicity, 'possessing touch but not being great' is a limiting condition. In establishing mere corporeality, the word 'eternal' would be pointless. If what is distinct from that is the reason, according to the view adopted in the <s>Kāśikā</s>, 'possessing touch' is a limiting condition. In the position that darkness is a substance, when 'possessing touch' pervades only the <s>sādhya</s> regarding darkness itself, 'being a substance inherent in a substance' is a limiting condition. By this, the [argument] 'the mind is corporeal, because it is conjoined with what is all-pervading, like a pot' is also refuted, because it has the stated limiting condition.

children.text:
sukhādayo mūrtasaṃyogāsamavāyikāraṇakāḥ, anityatve sati nityaviśeṣaguṇatvāt, pārthivaparamāṇurūpadivaditi vibhāgajaśabdajaśabdenānaikāntādasādhanam /
aśabdatve satīti viśeṣaṇe parasyaiva vaiyarthyam /
mūrtaṃ manaḥ śrotravyatiriktendriyatvādityapi nirastam, pūrvoktopādheḥ /
