avibhutve ca sparśavattvaṃ sādhanāvacchinnasādhyavyāpaka upādhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Pleasure and so forth have conjunction with corporeal [entities] as a non-inherence cause, because while being non-eternal, they are specific qualities of an eternal [substrate], like the form of an earthen atom — but this is not a valid proof, because of non-exclusiveness due to sound produced by disjunction and sound produced by sound. If the qualifier 'when being non-sound' [is added], this is pointless for the opponent alone. The [argument] 'the mind is corporeal, because it is a sense organ distinct from the ear' is also refuted, because of the previously stated limiting condition. And for non-all-pervasiveness, 'possessing touch' is a limiting condition that pervades the <s>sādhya</s> as delimited by the proof.

children.text:
etenāvibhu nityadravyatvādityanenāmahattvasādhane sādhyavyāpakatvāt sparśavattvaṃ nopādhiriti śrīvallabhoktaṃ nirastam /
na ca mano vibhu,
1 sarvadā sparśarahitadravyatvāt (nyā ku 3.1),
2 sadā viśeṣaguṇarahitadravyatvāt,
3 niravayavendriyatvāt,
4 dravyānārambhakanityadravyatvāt,
5 nityendriyatvāt,
6 vijñānasamavāyikāraṇasaṃyogādhārendriyatvāt,
7 sarvadā sparśarahitadravyatvāt,
8 nityaguṇagrāhakendriyatvāt,
9 abhūtatve satyarūpitvāt, kālavad, ātmavad, ākāśavaditi satpratipakṣadūṣaṇe kathaṃ svapakṣasiddhiriti vācyam, manasaḥ sarvagatatvābhyupagame ākāśakālātiriktasya sādhayitumaśakyatvena dharmigrāhakapramāṇabādhāśrayāsiddhayoranyatarākrāntatvāditi spaṣṭataramasmannyāyalakṣmīvilāse /
prathamasya tamodravyatvavādinastatraivānaikāntikatvam, sarvadetyasya ca vyarthatvāt /
etena dvitīyatṛtīye dūṣite, saptame 'pivaiyarthyam, navame 'pi arūpipadasya paraṃ prati vaiyarthyam, tamaso 'bhāvatvāt /
kiṃ bahunā dravyatvāvāntarajātyaindriyāsajātīyadravyatvamupādhiḥ /
1 sparśarahitatve sati aṇu manaḥ,
2 vijñānāsamavāyikāraṇasaṃyogādhāratve sati mūrttaṃ vā,
3 sukhagrāhakendriyaṃ vā,
4 aṇvindriyaṃ vā,
5 jñānajanakasaṃyogāśrayaṃ jaḍaṃ manaḥ,
6 jñānāsamavāyisaṃyogāśrayamindriyaṃ vā /
tasya guṇāḥ-- saṃkhyāparimāṇapṛthaktvasaṃyogavibhāgaparatvāparatvasaṃskārāḥ /
eṣāṃ mūrtatvadravyatvābhyāṃ siddhiḥ /
1 samavāyikāraṇaṃ dravyam,
2 guṇavad dravyam /
children.translated_text: By this, the statement of <s>Śrīvallabha</s> that 'because it is an eternal substance that is non-all-pervading' and so forth, in establishing non-greatness, 'possessing touch' is not a limiting condition because it pervades the <s>sādhya</s> — this is refuted. And the mind is not all-pervading (<s>vibhu</s>): 1) because it is a substance always devoid of touch (<s>Nyāyakusumāñjali</s> 3.1); 2) because it is a substance always devoid of specific qualities; 3) because it is a partless sense organ; 4) because it is an eternal substance not producing [other] substances; 5) because it is an eternal sense organ; 6) because it is a sense organ that is the substrate of conjunction which is the non-inherence cause of cognition; 7) because it is a substance always devoid of touch; 8) because it is a sense organ that apprehends eternal qualities; 9) because while being non-elemental, it possesses form — like time, like the self, like space. But it may be asked: when refuting the counter-position, how is one's own position established? Because if the all-pervasiveness of the mind is accepted, since it is impossible to establish anything beyond space and time, [the argument] necessarily falls into either the fallacy of invalidation of the means of knowledge apprehending the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) or unestablished locus — this is explained more clearly in our <s>Nyāyalakṣmīvilāsa</s>. For the first [argument], against the proponent of darkness as a substance, there is non-exclusiveness in that very [context], and the word 'always' is pointless. By this, the second and third are refuted; in the seventh too there is pointlessness; in the ninth too, the word 'non-form-possessing' is pointless for the opponent, because darkness is non-existent. In short, 'being a substance of a sub-class distinct from the same class as the sense organ' is a limiting condition. [Alternatively:] 1) the mind is atomic, when being devoid of touch; 2) or corporeal, when being the substrate of conjunction as non-inherence cause of cognition; 3) or a sense organ apprehending pleasure; 4) or an atomic sense organ; 5) the mind is insentient, being the substrate of conjunction that generates knowledge; 6) or a sense organ that is the substrate of non-inherent conjunction of knowledge. Its qualities are: number (<s>saṃkhyā</s>), magnitude (<s>parimāṇa</s>), separateness (<s>pṛthaktva</s>), conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), disjunction (<s>vibhāga</s>), priority (<s>paratva</s>), posteriority (<s>aparatva</s>), and latent impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>). The establishment of these is through corporeality and substance-ness. 1) The inherence cause is substance. 2) What possesses qualities is substance.

children.text: 10 tamasa ālokābhāvamātratvanirūpaṇam--
children.translated_text: 10. Examination of darkness (<s>tamas</s>) as merely the absence of light

children.text:
1) tamo nāma dravyantaramasti /
tadapi nirūpaṇīyamiti cet, na, pramāṇāsiddheḥ /
nīlaṃ tama iti pratītiḥ pramāṇamiti cet, nīlabuddhyasiddheḥ /
uktaṃ ca śālikanāthenāpi-- apratītāvevāyaṃ pratītibhramo mandānām' (pra paṃ 321) iti /
kathaṃ tarhi padaprayogaḥ? sitābhāvavadupacārāt /
asitaṃ nīlamiti laukikaḥ prayogaḥ /
mukhye bādhakābhāvāditi cet, ālokanirapekṣacakṣuṣo rūpapratyayajanakatvāsiddheḥ /
kāraṇābhāve kāryaṃ jāyate iti durghaṭametat /
anyathā nīlaghaṭasyāpi grahaṇaprasaṅgaḥ /
kathaṃ tarhi chāyāyāṃ kṛṣṇasarpabhrama iti cet, doṣavaśāt /
pūrvadṛṣṭakṛṣṇasarpādhyāropako doṣa iti /
kimatra sādṛśyamiti cet, sitābhāvatvam /
na caivamatiprasaṅgaḥ, sādṛśyamātrasyaiva bhrāntijñānasāmagrītvāsiddheḥ /
upayujyante hi viśeṣādarśanādayo 'pi ālokābhāvasahakāriṇo dharmādayo 'pi, vakradīrghāvayavīndriyasaṃyogādayaśca doṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: 1) Is there a separate substance called darkness (<s>tamas</s>)? If it is said that this too must be examined — no, because the means of knowledge [for its existence] is not established. If the cognition 'darkness is blue' is [proposed as] a means of knowledge — [this fails] because the cognition of blue is not established. As <s>Śālikanātha</s> too has said: 'This delusion of cognition [occurs] only in the case of non-cognition, for the dull-witted' (<s>Prakaraṇapañcikā</s> 321). Then how is the word used? By figurative usage, like [the word for] 'absence of white.' The popular usage is 'dark is blue.' If [it be objected] 'because there is no invalidator for the primary [meaning]' — [the response is:] because it is not established that the eye, independent of light, generates the cognition of form. That an effect arises in the absence of a cause — this is untenable. Otherwise, there would be the undesirable consequence of apprehending even a blue pot [in darkness]. If asked 'then how is there the erroneous perception of a black snake in shadow?' — that is due to a defect. The defect is the superimposition of a previously seen black snake. If asked 'what is the similarity here?' — the absence of whiteness. And there is no over-extension, because mere similarity is not established as the complete causal complex for erroneous cognition. For non-perception of particulars and so forth are also employed as auxiliaries [for error], along with the absence of light, merit (<s>dharma</s>) and so forth, and defects such as conjunction of the sense organ with crooked and elongated composite objects.

children.text:
2) mānasameva vā svapnavibhramādīti kecit /
na caivamatiprasaṅgaḥ, cākṣuṣalokābhāve karituragādismaraṇaviśeṣasyāpi tatra hetutvābhyupagamānnātiprasaṅgaḥ /
etena saṃkhyākriyādipratītirapi nirastā, tatraiva vipratipatteḥ, śabdaprayogasyopacāreṇāpyupapatteḥ, laukikavyavahārasya ca samyugdhatvāt /
children.translated_text: 2) Or it is merely mental, like the error in dreams and so forth — so some say. And there is no over-extension, because it is accepted that in the absence of light for the visual [sense], a specific memory of horses and so forth also serves as a cause therein — hence no over-extension. By this, the cognition of number, action, and so forth [in darkness] is also refuted, because there is disagreement in that very [matter], because the usage of words can be explained even through figurative usage, and because conventional worldly transaction is erroneous.

children.text:
3) ekadeśinaḥ punarnīlapratītimabhyupagamya bhrāntatvamācakṣate /
yathāhuḥ --- añjanapuñja iva śārvaraṃ tama iti bhrāntiprakaraṇe tatra pratibhāsikabādhānupapatteḥ /
anenāpahṛtaviṣayatvenānutthānādbādhakanirūpaṇaṃ durghaṭamiti paśyāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: 3) Others, however, accepting the cognition of blue [in darkness], declare it to be erroneous. As they say: 'the nocturnal darkness, like a mass of collyrium' — since in the context of error, the invalidation of what appears [as real] is not tenable. We observe that since [the object] has been removed as subject matter, the task of demonstrating an invalidator is untenable.

children.text:
4) śabdena vinā pratītisādhanaṃ ca /
tamaḥ śabdasya tarhi ko 'rtha iti cet, ubhayavādipratipanna ālokasaṃsargābhāvaḥ /
ālokaviśeṣe satyapi ālokāntarābhāvasyāpi sambhavāt prayogaprasaṅga iti cet, tatra kimālokābhāvaprayogo 'sti, na vā? asti cet, tamaḥśabdaprayogo 'pyastu, kā no hāniḥ? paryāyaśabdatvāt /
atha yathā jvālāyā āśutaravināśitvena madhye vināśe vidyamāne 'pi tatsadṛśajvālotpattyā tirohitatvānna nāśavyavahāraḥ, tadāloke satyālokāntarābhāvasya tirodhānānna tadabhāvavyavahāra iti /
laukikapratītistu bhramatvenocyate /
tattulyaṃ te tarkakarkaśamaterapyuktaparihāraścakṣurālokāsahakṛtaṃ rūpigrāhakaṃ dravyagrāhakendriyatvāttvagvaditi vādinaḥ kālagrāhakaghrāṇenānaikāntikaṃ vyarthaviśeṣaṇatā ca /
cakṣurālokanirapekṣaṃ dravyaṃ gṛhṇāti, indriyatvāditi sādhane ghrāṇena prativādinānaikāntikatā vivakṣitā---sādhakatvaṃ ca /
na hi tava tathāvidhaṃ tama eveti lakṣaṇaṃ kālāderapi ālokanirapekṣendriyagrāhyatvāt /
children.translated_text: 4) And the proof of [darkness as mere absence of light through] cognition without [recourse to] words. If asked 'what then is the meaning of the word <s>tamas</s> (darkness)?' — it is the absence of contact with light, accepted by both disputants. If [it be objected] that even when a particular light is present, the absence of another light is also possible, and therefore this usage would apply [universally] — [the reply is:] is the usage of 'absence of light' present there or not? If it is, then let the usage of the word <s>tamas</s> also apply — what is our loss? Because they are synonymous words. But just as when a flame, due to its rapid destruction, perishes in between, yet because of the arising of a similar flame, due to concealment there is no convention of destruction — so when light is present, the absence of other light is concealed, hence there is no convention of 'absence of that.' Ordinary cognition, however, is declared to be erroneous. Your [objection] is equally [applicable to your own position] — and to one whose intellect is hardened by logical reasoning, the stated answer applies: the [argument] 'the eye without the aid of light apprehends corporeal [objects], because it is a substance-apprehending sense organ, like the skin' — by the proponent — is non-exclusive due to the nose apprehending time, and the qualifier is pointless. The [argument] 'the eye apprehends substance independently of light, because it is a sense organ' — in this proof, the opponent intends non-exclusiveness through the nose — and [claims] probative force. For it is not the case that [darkness is] a thing of such a nature for you alone — because time and so forth are also apprehended by a sense organ independent of light.

children.text:
5) ālokabhāvasyobhayavādisampratipannatvāt tamaḥśabdavācyatve nāsti vipratipattirnātra prakaraṇaṃ vācyam /
vivādādhyāsitaḥ ālokabhāvaḥ tamaḥśabdavācyaḥ, itaretarābhāvavyatiriktālokābhāvatvāt /
yaditthaṃ na bhavati, taditthamapi na bhavati, yathāloka eva /
anye tu tama ālokābhāvaḥ, ālokānapekṣacakṣuṣi satyevāsati ca liṅgādau gṛhyamāṇatvāt, sampratipannālokābhāvavaditi bruvate /
tatra kau pakṣasapakṣau? bhinnābhinnāviti cintanīyamiti /
yogimānasagrāhyatvāccāvadhāraṇāsambhavena hetvasiddhiśca /
tasmādevaṃ prayogakramaḥ --- tamaḥpadamālokābhāvavācakam, ālokānapekṣacakṣurgrāhyavācakatvād, ālokābhāvapadavat /
children.translated_text: 5) Since the absence of light is accepted by both disputants, there is no disagreement regarding its being denoted by the word '<s>tamas</s>' (darkness) — no special topic need be stated here. The subject under dispute: the absence of light is denoted by the word '<s>tamas</s>' (darkness), because it is an absence of light distinct from mutual absence. Whatever is not of such a nature is also not of such another nature, just like light itself. Others, however, say that <s>tamas</s> (darkness) is the absence of light, because it is apprehended when there is a sense organ of sight not dependent on light and when there is no <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark) and so forth, just like the accepted absence of light. In that case, what are the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) and <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar instance)? Whether they are different or identical must be considered. And since it is graspable only by the <s>yogin</s>'s mind, there is the impossibility of ascertainment, and hence the <s>hetu</s> (reason) is unestablished. Therefore the order of the argument is as follows: the word '<s>tamas</s>' (darkness) denotes the absence of light, because it denotes what is graspable by a sense organ of sight not dependent on light, just like the expression 'absence of light.'

children.text: nirūpito dravyapadārtha eṣa, navaprakāro mudamātanotu /
children.translated_text: This <s>dravya-padārtha</s> (category of substance), of nine kinds, has been established — may it bestow delight!

children.text: navātmakasya tridaśādhipasya, trilokapūjyatripurāntakasya //
children.translated_text: Of the nine-formed lord of the gods, worshipped by the three worlds, the destroyer of the three cities —

children.text: iti śrīmānamanohare dravyapadārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>dravya-padārtha</s> (category of substance) in the illustrious <s>Mānamanohara</s>.

children.text: guṇaprakaraṇam
children.translated_text: Chapter on <s>Guṇa</s> (Quality)

children.text: 1-4 rūparasagandhasparśāṇāṃ nirūpaṇam--
children.translated_text: 1-4: Determination of <s>rūpa</s> (color/form), <s>rasa</s> (taste), <s>gandha</s> (smell), and <s>sparśa</s> (touch) —

children.text:
1) pratyakṣaṃ rūpe pramāṇam /
vivādapadaṃ ghaṭotpattyanantarakāle jāyate, ghaṭaguṇatvāt, sampratipannaghaṭasaṃyogavat /
na ca sāmānyaguṇatvamupādhiḥ, tadgataparimāṇādīnāmapi paścādutpattiprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: 1) Perception is the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) with respect to <s>rūpa</s> (color/form). The subject under dispute arises at the moment immediately after the origination of the pot, because it is a quality of the pot, just like the accepted <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction) of the pot. Nor is being located in an effect a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>), because there would be the undesirable consequence that <s>parimāṇa</s> (magnitude) and other qualities located in that [effect] would also arise subsequently.

children.text:
2) vivādapadaṃ kāryaṃ pārthivaviśeṣaguṇatvādghaṭarūpavat /
na ca kāryagatatvamupādhiḥ, paramāṇusaṃyogasaṃskārādyavyāpanāt /
children.translated_text: 2) The subject under dispute is a product, because it is a particular quality of an earthy [substance], just like the <s>rūpa</s> (color) of a pot. Nor is being located in an effect a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>), because it does not pervade <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction) of atoms, <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression), and so forth.

children.text: 3) vivādapadaṃ kāryaṃ saṃkhyāparimāṇapṛthaktvagurutvasaṃskāravyatiriktatve sati pārthivaguṇatvāt pārthivaparamāṇusaṃyogavat /
children.translated_text: 3) The subject under dispute is a product, because while being distinct from <s>saṃkhyā</s> (number), <s>parimāṇa</s> (magnitude), <s>pṛthaktva</s> (distinctness), <s>gurutva</s> (heaviness), and <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression), it is a quality of an earthy [substance], just like the <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction) of earthy atoms.

children.text: 4) vivādapadamagnisaṃyogajaviśeṣaguṇavad, anityaviśeṣaguṇatve sati nityatvādātmavat /
children.translated_text: 4) The subject under dispute possesses a particular quality produced by contact with fire; while being a non-eternal particular quality, it is eternal, just like the <s>ātman</s> (self).

children.text: 5) vivādapadamavayavyāśrayakāle na rūpajanakamāśrayatvājjalāṇuvat /
children.translated_text: 5) The subject under dispute, at the time of inhering in a composite whole, does not generate <s>rūpa</s> (color), because it is a substratum, just like a water atom.

children.text: 6) vivādapadamāśrayanāśanāśyamānakāryavyatiriktaguṇāśrayaḥ, guṇavattvātsamavāyikāraṇatvādātmavat /
children.translated_text: 6) The subject under dispute is the substratum of a quality other than the effect destroyed by the destruction of its substratum, because it possesses qualities and because it is a <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> (inherent cause), just like the <s>ātman</s> (self).

children.text: 7) rūpatvamanāśrite 'pi samavetam, rūpajātitvātsattāvat /
children.translated_text: 7) <s>Rūpatva</s> (the universal 'color-ness') inheres even in what is not a substratum [of color], because it is a <s>jāti</s> (universal) of <s>rūpa</s> (color), just like <s>sattā</s> (existence/being).

children.text:
8) vivādāśrayo 'nekarūpādhikaraṇam na bhavati, avayavitvāt, śuklatantuvat /
vivādapadaṃ na nīlatvādhikaraṇam, pītārabdhatvāt, vivādapadaṃ na pītatvādhikaraṇam, nīlārabdhatvātpītavannīlavacca /
children.translated_text: 8) The locus of the dispute is not a substratum of multiple <s>rūpas</s> (colors), because it is a composite whole, just like a white thread. If one argues: the subject under dispute is not a substratum of blue-ness, because it is produced from yellow [constituents], just like a yellow [thing] — no, because this is vitiated by the inclusion of contradictory universals; otherwise there would be the undesirable consequence of including [arguments] such as 'the subject under dispute is not a substratum of yellow-ness,' and so forth.

children.text:
9) vivādapadaṃ pītatvādhikaraṇam, pītārabdhatvāt, pītavaditi cet na, viruddhajātisamāveśena bādhitatvāt, anyathā vivādapadaṃ gotvādhikaraṇam, pārthivādityāpi syāt /
rūpatvāvāntarapītatvavyatiriktajātyanāśrayarūpatvaṃ copādhiḥ /
etena śuklaṃ rūpamekameveti nirastam, taratamabhāvasyāpi dṛṣṭeḥ /
children.translated_text: 9) If one argues: the subject under dispute is a substratum of yellow-ness, because it is produced from yellow [constituents], just like a yellow [thing] — no, because this is vitiated by the inclusion of contradictory universals; otherwise there would be the undesirable consequence of including [arguments] such as 'the subject under dispute is not a substratum of blue-ness.' Here too it would be established by convention, since when there is production from yellow, there is the non-existence of production from blue.

children.text:
10) nityatve satyanekārthe vartamānatvātsāmānyamityuktaṃ syāt, tasya ca yāvaddravyabhāvitvāt /
pākajeṣu raktapratyayo durghaṭaḥ /
tadanekaprakāram /
guṇatve sati cakṣuḥsparśanayormadhye cakṣuṣaiva grahaṇārhaṃ rūpam /
etena rasagandhasparśā api nirūpitāḥ /
citrā api te 'vagantavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 10) If it is eternal and operates in multiple objects, it would be said to be a <s>sāmānya</s> (universal), and that [universal] exists as long as the <s>dravya</s> (substance) exists. In things produced by heating (<s>pakaja</s>), the cognition of redness is twofold: the cognition of redness belonging to the atom, and the cognition of redness belonging to the stage of heating. And the [redness] corresponds to the stage of heating, so they say. There, the [redness] belonging to the atom is the same everywhere.

children.text: 11) guṇatve sati rasanagrāhyo rasaḥ /
children.translated_text: 11) <s>Rasa</s> (taste), while being a <s>guṇa</s> (quality), is what is grasped by the tongue.

children.text: 12) guṇatve sati ghrāṇagrāhyo gandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 12) <s>Gandha</s> (smell), while being a <s>guṇa</s> (quality), is what is grasped by the nose.

children.text:
pṛthivī sparśavatī rūpitvāt, tejovat /
vivādapadaṃ sparśavad, dravyārambhakatvāt, tejovat /
children.translated_text: Earth possesses <s>sparśa</s> (touch) because it possesses <s>rūpa</s> (color/form), just like <s>tejas</s> (fire). The subject under dispute possesses <s>sparśa</s> (touch), because it is a cause of [composite] substances, just like <s>tejas</s> (fire).

children.text: cakṣuḥsparśanayormadhye sparśanenaiva grāhyo guṇaḥ sparśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Among the eye and the organ of touch, the quality <s>sparśa</s> (touch) is grasped by the organ of touch alone.

children.text: 5-6 saṃkhyāpṛthaktvayornirūpaṇam--
children.translated_text: 5-6: Determination of <s>saṃkhyā</s> (number) and <s>pṛthaktva</s> (distinctness) —

children.text: (I. ekatvaikapṛthaktvayoḥ siddhiḥ)
children.translated_text: (I. Establishment of <s>ekatva</s> (oneness) and <s>ekapṛthaktva</s> (single distinctness))

children.text:
1) sparśavad guṇāsamavāyikāraṇādviṣṭhaguṇayorāśrayaḥ, dravyatvād mūrtatvāt, paṭārambhakatantuvat /
na ca sparśavattvamupādhiḥ, sparśavatāṃ ghaṭādīnāmapi tathāvidhaguṇadvayāśrayatvaprasaṅgāt /
na ca dravyāsamavāyikāraṇatvamupādhiḥ, viśeṣaṇavaiyarthyāt /
nirūpādhikasya sādhyaparityāge svabhāvaparityāgaprasaṅgāt /
tatrākāśādiṣu yau guṇau, tayorekamekatvaṃ, aparamekapṛthaktvam /
anyatrāpi tau pūrvoktahetoreva sādhyau /
children.translated_text: 1) [The subject] possessing <s>sparśa</s> (touch) is the substratum of two qualities that are distinct from the non-inherent cause of a quality, because it is a <s>dravya</s> (substance) and because it is corporeal (<s>mūrta</s>), just like the threads that are the cause of a cloth. Nor is possessing <s>sparśa</s> (touch) a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>), because that is what is to be proved, since <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-ness) and <s>mūrtatva</s> (corporeality) serve as the <s>hetu</s> (reason).

children.text: 2) vipratipannaḥ saṃyogaḥ svato 'dhikavṛttikāryaikārthasamavetatvārhaḥ, saṃyogatvāt, tritantukārambhakasaṃyogavat /
children.translated_text: 2) The disputed <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction) is fit to be co-inherent in a single locus with an effect having a greater extension than itself, because it is a <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), just like the conjunction that causes a three-threaded [cloth].

children.text: 3) paramāṇavaḥ saṃyogādhikavṛttikāryasamavāyikāraṇam, aṇutvād, dvyaṇukavat /
children.translated_text: 3) Atoms are the <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> (inherent cause) of an effect having a greater extension than conjunction, because they are atomic, just like a dyad.

children.text:
4) vipratipanno 'vayavī kāraṇatvārheṇa saha tulyāśrayaḥ, avayavitvād, dvyaṇukavad dvitantukavacca /
rūpādīnāmekāśrayavṛttitvāt, saṃyogasya dviṣṭhatvāt /
tricaturārabdhatvānna siddhasādhanatā /
anenaiva yathā parimāṇasiddhirapi /
children.translated_text: 4) The disputed composite whole shares its substratum with what is fit to be a cause, because it is a composite whole, just like a dyad or a two-threaded [cloth]. Because <s>rūpa</s> (color) and other [qualities] possess the property of existing in a single substratum, each one individually is the substrate in which <s>ekatva</s> (oneness) and <s>pṛthaktva</s> (distinctness) inhere.

children.text: (II. anekatvānekapṛthaktvayoḥ siddhiḥ)
children.translated_text: (II. Establishment of <s>anekatva</s> (plurality) and <s>anekapṛthaktva</s> (plural distinctness))

children.text:
1) vivādādhyāsito buddhijaguṇayorāśrayaḥ, dravyatvātsamavāyikāraṇatvād, ātmavat /
na cātmatvamupādhiḥ, īśvare vyabhicārāt /
atraikam-- anekatvasaṃkhyā, aparam-- anekapṛthaktvamiti /
children.translated_text: 1) The subject under dispute is the substratum of a pair of qualities born of cognition, because it is a <s>dravya</s> (substance) and because it is a <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> (inherent cause), just like the <s>ātman</s> (self). Nor is <s>ātmatva</s> (self-ness) a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>), because there is deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) in the case of <s>Īśvara</s> (God).

children.text:
2) tadevaṃ siddhayoḥ saṃkhyāpṛthaktvayorvyavahāreṇāpi siddhiḥ /
asti ca tāvadekaṃ dve trīṇi ityādivyavahāraḥ /
na cāsau nirnibandhanaḥ, padatvavyāghātaprasaṅgāt /
na cābheda ekatvaṃ bhedasamuccayaḥ punaranekatvamiti yuktam /
abhedaḥ kiṃ paṭastadatirikto vā? ādye (ekaḥ paṭa iti) sahaprayogānupapattiḥ, paryāyatvāt /
dvitīye saṃpratipattidharmapadārtho 'sāviti cet, kimatra pramāṇam? guṇādāvabhedavyavahāra iti cenna, vyavahāramātrādarthāsiddheḥ, tasya gauṇasyāpi bahuśo darśanāt /
mukhye bādhakābhāvāt, kathaṃ gauṇatvamiti cet, na; sādhakasyāpyabhāvāt /
utpattikāraṇābhāvasya vispaṣṭatvāt /
samavāyyasamavāyikāraṇayorabhāvāt, nimittakāraṇamātrādevotpattistu tatsiddhau satyāṃ kalpanīyā, apratītestadasiddheḥ /
children.translated_text: 2) Thus, <s>saṃkhyā</s> (number) and <s>pṛthaktva</s> (distinctness) having been established, their establishment is [confirmed] also through ordinary usage. And indeed there is the usage 'one, two, three,' and so forth. Nor is that usage an error like the enumeration of honey-natured [things] and so on, because of repeated corroboration.

children.text:
3) yadyapyapekṣābuddhivaijātyasamavāyād dvitvatritvadivyavahārāṇāmapi bhedasamuccayo na saṃkaramāpādayati, tathāpyananusaṃhitavaijātyādīnāṃ bālagopālādīnāṃ dvāviti vyavahāro 'yaṃ na tannibandhanaḥ dvyaṇukaparimāṇaṃ dvitvasaṃkhyayā vinā na ghaṭate /
nityaparamāṇuparimāṇābhyāṃ paramāṇuparimāṇasyānārambhāt, pracayasya cānāśaṅkanīyatvāt /
kāraṇaparimāṇatvasya na sādhakateti vācyam, atrāvāntarātiśayavattvasyopādheḥ, pracayajanye 'pi parimāṇe tasyānārambhakatvācca /
tathāpekṣābuddhyāpi janyate, idamekamidamekamiti jñānānvayavyatirekānuvidhāyitvāt /
na ca vyañjakatvenopapattiḥ, samānendriyagrāhyasamānadeśāvasthitānāṃ yugapadindriyasambaddhānāmindriyasambandhavyatirekeṇa niyatavyañjakavyaṅgyatvādarśanāt /
ataḥ saṃyogasamānatā dvitvasyeti /
children.translated_text: 3) Although from the difference in relative cognition and the inherence of dissimilarity, the usages of <s>dvitva</s> (twoness), <s>tritva</s> (threeness), and so forth also involve a combination of differences that does not lead to confusion, nevertheless, since without recollection there is no <s>saṃkhyā</s> (number) arising from relative cognition, the case is the same with <s>ekatva</s> (oneness) and <s>pṛthaktva</s> (distinctness) whose object is the recollection of one's own nature.

children.text:
4) eke dvitvaṃ buddhijaṃ niyamenaikapratipattṛvedyatvādityāhuḥ /
teṣāṃ jñānaprāgabhāvena vyabhicāraḥ --- guṇatve satīti viśeṣaṇe īśvarecchāyām, kāryatve satīti viśeṣaṇe jāgarādijñāne /
anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ cāpekṣābuddhyabhāve dvitvābhāvopalambhāttadvināśasya dvitvavināśahetutvam /
anumānakramastu --- dvitvaṃ nimittakāraṇanāśanāśyavyaktisamavetam, tajjātitvātsattāvat /
sattādinimittakāraṇībhūtadehanāśanāśyamāne yuñjānasyāntyasukhajñāne samavetam /
evaṃ sarvaṃ pṛthaktve vaktavyamiti /
children.translated_text: 4) Some say that <s>dvitva</s> (twoness) is necessarily born of cognition, because it is apprehended by a single cognizer. Against them there is deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) through the prior absence of knowledge — and even with the qualifier 'while being a <s>guṇa</s> (quality),' there is no escape, because prior absence, while being a quality, is grasped by knowledge.

children.text: 7 parimāṇasya nirūpaṇam--
children.translated_text: 7: Determination of <s>parimāṇa</s> (magnitude) —

children.text:
1) vivādādhyāsitaṃ dviṣṭhaguṇānasamavāyikāraṇānityaviśeṣaṇaguṇavyatiriktādviṣṭhaguṇāśrayaḥ, dravyatvājjalaparamāṇuvat /
na ca sparśavattvamūrtatve upādhī, pavanapārthivaparamāṇau vyabhicārāt /
īśvaro nityaviśeṣaguṇavyatiriktānasamavāyikāraṇādviṣṭhaguṇāśrayaḥ, ātmatvājjīvavat /
nityaikatvaikapṛthaktvaparimāṇasādhanavivakṣāyāmanasamavāyikāraṇamiti na vācyam /
adviṣṭha iti dviṣṭhaguṇatvāvāntarajātirahita iti boddhavyam, anyathā ekatvena siddhasādhanatā /
children.translated_text:
1) The subject under dispute is a substratum of qualities that do not reside in two [substrata], distinct from qualities whose non-inherent cause is a quality residing in two [substrata] and whose qualifier is non-eternal — because of being a substance, like a water atom.
Nor are 'possessing touch' and 'being corporeal' limiting conditions, because there is deviation in wind and earthen atoms.
<s>Īśvara</s> (God) is a substratum of qualities residing not in two [substrata], distinct from qualities whose non-inherent cause is an eternal specific quality — because of being a self (<s>ātman</s>), like a <s>jīva</s> (individual soul).
It should not be said that the non-inherent cause is intended [merely] to establish eternal oneness and single separateness and magnitude.
'Not residing in two' should be understood as 'devoid of the sub-universal of the quality-type that resides in two'; otherwise, there would be the fallacy of proving what is already established through oneness.

children.text:
2) tathā vyavahāreṇāpi sādhanīyam --- asti tāvadayaṃ mahān, ayaṃ mahāniti vyavahāraḥ /
na cātra mahattvasāmānyameva nimittam, taratamabhāvasyānupapattiprasaṅgāt /
anyathā madhurarasasyāpyucchedaprasaṅgāt, madhuratvasāmānyādeva dravyāśritād vyavahāropapatteḥ /
children.translated_text:
2) Likewise, [magnitude] is to be established through practical usage as well — there is indeed the usage 'this is large, this is large.'
Nor is the universal of largeness (<s>mahattvasāmānya</s>) alone the cause [of this usage], because there would be the unwanted consequence that degrees of comparison would be inexplicable.
Otherwise, there would be the unwanted consequence that sweet taste too would be eliminated, since practical usage is explicable from the universal of sweetness alone residing in a substance.

children.text:
3) pracayasaṃkhyāparimāṇānāmanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ tadutpattau kāraṇatvam /
vivādādhyāsito 'ṇuparimāṇavyatiriktaparimāṇāśrayaḥ, dravyatvāt /
vivādādhyāsito mahatparimāṇavyatiriktaparimāṇāśrayaḥ, dravyatvādghaṭavat paramāṇuvacca /
na cātrāṇutvamahattve upādhī, rūpādiṣu vyabhicārāt /
dravyatvena viśeṣaṇe vaiyarthyam /
hrasvadīrghavyavahārayoranyathānupapattiśca pramāṇam /
āśrayanāśānnāśa ityatra prācīnamanumānaṃ vācyam /
children.translated_text:
3) The causal status of accumulation, number, and magnitude in the production of that [magnitude] is [established] through positive and negative concomitance.
The subject under dispute is a substratum of magnitude distinct from atomic magnitude, because of being a substance.
The subject under dispute is a substratum of magnitude distinct from great magnitude, because of being a substance, like a pot and like an atom.
Nor are atomic-ness and greatness limiting conditions here, because there is deviation in color etc.
Qualifying with 'substance' renders [the qualificand] redundant.
The impossibility of otherwise [explaining] the usage of 'short' and 'long' is also evidence.
Regarding '[magnitude] perishes from the perishing of the substratum,' the earlier inference should be stated.

children.text: 4) dvitvāsamavāyikāraṇakavṛttiguṇatvāvāntarajātīyaṃ parimāṇam /
children.translated_text: 4) <s>Parimāṇa</s> (magnitude) belongs to the sub-universal of the quality-type that occurs in [substances having] duality as their non-inherent cause.

children.text: 8 saṃyogasya nirūpaṇam--
children.translated_text: 8. Examination of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>):

children.text:
1) vivādapadamasamavāyikāraṇajanyaṃ kāryatvādrūpavat /
na ca pradhvaṃse vyabhicāraḥ, prāgabhāvapratiyogitvasya bhāvatve satīti viśeṣitasya tatrāsiddheḥ /
na cātropādhiśaṅkāpyadhirohati, vispaṣṭaśca ghaṭau saṃyuktāviti pratyayaḥ /
nirākṛtaśca kṣaṇabhaṅga iti nāviraladeśe utpādastannimittatvenāśaṅkanīyaḥ /
karmasaṃyogayoḥ tajjanakatvaṃ pratyakṣasiddhameva /
children.translated_text:
1) The subject of dispute is produced by a non-inherent cause, because it is an effect, like color.
Nor is there deviation in destruction (<s>pradhvaṃsa</s>), because the qualified [property] — 'being a counter-positive of prior absence while being a positive entity' — is unestablished there.
Nor does the suspicion of a limiting condition even arise here, for the cognition 'the two pots are conjoined' is manifest.
And since momentary destruction (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) has been refuted, arising in a non-distant location is not to be suspected as its cause.
The productive capacity of action and conjunction [with respect to conjunction] is established by direct perception itself.

children.text:
2) ākāśa ātmanā saṃyujyate, dravyatvāditi kecit /
tanna, kriyāvattvamūrtatvayoḥ paratvāparatvayorvopādhitvāt /
ātmā ākāśena na saṃyujyate, amūrtatvādrūpavat /
na cātrādravyatvamupādhiḥ, ākāśe tadabhāvena sapakṣāvyāpakatvāt /
children.translated_text:
2) Some [say]: <s>ākāśa</s> (space) is conjoined with the <s>ātman</s> (self), because of being a substance.
That is wrong, because 'possessing activity' and 'being corporeal,' or 'priority' and 'posteriority' serve as limiting conditions.
The <s>ātman</s> is not conjoined with <s>ākāśa</s>, because it is incorporeal, like color.
Nor is 'being a non-substance' a limiting condition here, because of its absence in <s>ākāśa</s>, it does not pervade the positive instance.

children.text:
3) vibhāgāśrayanāśābhyāṃ ca tasya nāśaḥ /
āśrayanāśottarasaṃyogābhyāṃ ca vibhāganāśaḥ /
saṃyogasya tvāśrayanāśavibhāgābhyāmeva nāśa ityuktam /
nityatvātparamāṇvākāśayorāśrayanāśanāśyatvaṃ tatsaṃyogasya na sambhavati /
sarvamuktipakṣe ca virodhiguṇaprādurbhāvo 'pi durghaṭaḥ /
ato nimittanāśanāśyatvamaṅgīkriyate iti /
anityaḥ sambandhaḥ saṃyogaḥ, ghaṭajanakatadavayavaniṣṭhaguṇatvāvāntarajātīyaḥ saṃyogaḥ /
children.translated_text:
3) The destruction of that [conjunction] is through disjunction and the destruction of the substratum.
The destruction of disjunction is through the conjunction subsequent to the destruction of the substratum.
But it has been stated that the destruction of conjunction is through disjunction and the destruction of the substratum alone.
Since atoms and <s>ākāśa</s> are eternal, destruction of their conjunction through the destruction of the substratum is not possible.
And in the position of universal liberation, the manifestation of a contrary quality is also difficult to establish.
Therefore, destruction through the destruction of the occasioning cause (<s>nimitta</s>) is accepted.
Conjunction is a non-eternal relation; it belongs to the sub-universal of the quality-type of qualities that inhere in the components of the pot and its parts.

children.text: 9 vibhāgasya nirūpaṇam--
children.translated_text: 9. Examination of disjunction (<s>vibhāga</s>):

children.text:
1) karma saṃyogavyatiriktāsamavāyikāraṇam, saṃyogavyatiriktatve sati asamavāyikāraṇatvādrūpavat /
na cākarmatvamupādhiḥ, ākāśādiṣu vyabhicārāt /
asamavāyikāraṇatve satīti viśeṣaṇe kevalasaṃyogārambhakeṇa saṃyogena vyabhicārāt /
saṃyogavyatiriktatve satīti viśeṣaṇe vaiyarthyam /
na ca saṃyogavyatiriktāsamavāyikāraṇatvāditi saṃyogasyaivāsamavāyikāraṇatvaṃ pratīyate iti bādhitaviṣayatvam, bhavatāṃ karmaṇaḥ karmāsamavāyikāraṇatvāt /
na caivaṃ prathamānumāne siddhasādhyatā, mandagatau tadabhāvāt vyatiriktāsiddheḥ /
tava ca saṃskārasyāpyasiddheḥ /
antyakarmaṇaḥ karmājanakatvāt, mama tasyaiva pakṣatvāt /
children.translated_text:
1) <s>Karma</s> (action) is a non-inherent cause distinct from conjunction, because, being distinct from conjunction, it is a non-inherent cause, like color.
Nor is 'being a non-action' a limiting condition, because there is deviation in <s>ākāśa</s> etc.
If one qualifies with 'being a non-inherent cause,' there is deviation through the conjunction that produces mere conjunction.
The qualification 'being distinct from conjunction' is redundant.
Nor should it be said that from 'being a non-inherent cause distinct from conjunction,' the non-inherent cause-hood of conjunction itself is understood — [which would be] a case of a contradicted subject — because, according to you, action is the non-inherent cause of action.
Nor is there the fallacy of proving what is already established in the first inference, because in slow motion, that [action as non-inherent cause] is absent — hence there is deviation.

children.text:
2) kiṃ cāsti tāvadayaṃ vibhāgavyavahāraḥ /
na cāsau nirnibandhanaḥ /
na ca saṃyogābhāvo nimittam, saṃyoganāśe eva kāraṇabhāvāt /
na ca karmaṇaḥ tatra kāraṇatvam, guṇānāṃ karmavināśyatvādarśanāt /
vipratipannaḥ saṃyogo na karmanāśyaḥ, guṇatvātsampratipannavat /
na ca vibhāgavināśyo 'pi na bhavati, tasmādeveti sāmpratam, pratiyogyasiddhyā vyāptyasiddheḥ /
siddhi vā tadvināśakatvenaiva kalpanā, niṣkāraṇakāryasiddheḥ /
children.translated_text:
2) Moreover, there is indeed this practical usage of disjunction.
Nor is it without basis.
Nor is the absence of conjunction the cause, because it serves as a cause only in the destruction of conjunction.
Nor does action have causal status there, because the destruction of qualities by action is not observed.
The subject under dispute — conjunction — is not destroyed by action, because it is a quality, like the acknowledged [qualities].
Nor should it be said that [disjunction] too is not destroyed by disjunction, 'since it is [destroyed] by that very [disjunction]' — this is correct [only] at present, because the pervasion is unestablished due to the counter-positive being unestablished.
Or if established, the postulation is as a destroyer of that [conjunction] itself; since an effect without a cause is established.

children.text:
3) sa ca dvividhaḥ --- karmajavibhāgajabhedāt /
vivādādhyāsito vibhāgo na karmāsamavāyikāraṇakaḥ, karmaikārthasamavetatvācchabdavat /
vivādapadamātmātiriktaṃ dravyaṃ vibhāgajanyaguṇādhikaraṇam, nityadravyatvādātmavat /
na cātmatvamupādhiḥ, īśvare vyabhicārāt /
ākāśe ca vyāptyabhāvāt /
children.translated_text:
3) And that [disjunction] is of two kinds — from the division of action-born and disjunction-born.
The subject under dispute — disjunction — does not have action as its non-inherent cause, because it is co-inherent with action in one [substratum], like sound.
The subject — a substance other than the <s>ātman</s> — is a substratum of a quality produced by disjunction, because of being an eternal substance, like the <s>ātman</s>.
Nor is <s>ātman</s>-ness a limiting condition, because there is deviation in <s>Īśvara</s>.
And because pervasion is absent in <s>ākāśa</s>.

children.text:
4) anye tu dravyārambhakasaṃyogavirodhivibhāgotpattikāle nāvayavakarma ākāśādideśād vibhāgārambhakam, karmatvāditi bruvate /
tadasat, ākāśadeśena vibhāgamārabhate karmatvādityapi vaktuṃ śakyatvāt /
tasmānna kāraṇavibhāgādvibhāgaḥ syāt /
vivādapadamātmanā vibhajyate dravyatvāditi pūrvavaddūṣaṇīyam /
children.translated_text:
4) Others, however, say: at the time of the production of disjunction opposed to the conjunction that produces a substance, the action of the components does not originate disjunction from the location of <s>ākāśa</s> etc., because it is an action.
That is wrong, because one could equally say: [action] originates disjunction with the location of <s>ākāśa</s>, because it is an action.
Therefore, disjunction does not arise from the disjunction of a cause.
The subject under dispute 'is disjoined from the <s>ātman</s>, because of being a substance' — this should be refuted as before.

children.text:
5) āśrayavināśottarasaṃyogābhyāṃ ca tadvināśaḥ /
uttarasaṃyogādvināśaḥ paścādapi kathaṃ vibhāgapratyayānuvṛtterapi na vācyam, pratyayasyaivāsiddheḥ, śabdaprayogasya cānyathāpyupapatteḥ, śravaṇamātrādeva mukhyatvānirṇayāt /
saṃyogasaṃsargābhāve vibhāgapadasyāpi na pṛthak saṃketaḥ, saṃyogaprāgabhāve 'pi vyavahāradarśanāt /
saṃyogasamānāśrayatve sati saṃyogavināśako vibhāgaḥ /
children.translated_text:
5) The destruction of that [disjunction] is from the destruction of the substratum and from subsequent conjunction.
Nor should it be said: how [can there be destruction] from subsequent conjunction, when the cognition of disjunction continues even afterward — because the cognition itself is unestablished, because the use of the word [disjunction] is explicable otherwise, and because from hearing alone, the primary [meaning] is not determined.
In the absence of connection with conjunction, the word 'disjunction' too does not have a separate convention, since usage is observed even in the prior absence of conjunction.
Disjunction is that which, being co-located with conjunction, destroys conjunction.

children.text: 10-11 paratvāparatvayornirūpaṇam--
children.translated_text: 10-11. Examination of priority (<s>paratva</s>) and posteriority (<s>aparatva</s>):

children.text:
1) vivādapadaṃ paramāṇuvṛttyadviṣṭhaguṇajanakam, paramāṇavo vā kāryavṛttyadviṣṭhaguṇajanakā mūrttatvāt, pārthivaparamāṇuvadghaṭavacceti /
vivādapadaṃ svārabdhadravye guṇajanakam, dravyatve sati dravyārambhakatvādīśvaravat /
vivādapadaṃ paramāṇujanyam, karmahetvadviṣṭhaguṇāśrayam, mūrttatvādaguṇatvātpārthivaparamāṇuvat /
tadevaṃ siddhayoḥ parāparavyavahārādapi siddhiḥ /
anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ cādityaparivartanadeśasaṃyuktasaṃyogālpīyastvabhūyastvajñānasya hetutvam /
vyañjakatve pūrvavad doṣo 'nusandheyaḥ /
children.translated_text:
1) The subject under dispute produces a quality residing not in two [substrata] that occurs in atoms, or: atoms produce a quality residing not in two that occurs in effects — because of being corporeal, like an earthen atom and like a pot.
The subject under dispute produces a quality in its own originated substance, because, being a substance, it is a substance-producer, like <s>Īśvara</s>.
The subject under dispute is atom-produced, is a substratum of a quality that is not action-caused and does not reside in two — because of being corporeal and not being a quality, like an earthen atom.
Thus being established, there is also establishment from the practical usage of priority and posteriority.
Through positive and negative concomitance, the causal status of the cognition of lesser and greater extent of conjunction with the location conjoined by the revolution of the sun is [established].
If manifestation [is proposed], the fault is as before.

children.text:
2) vivādādhyāsito 'dviṣṭhabuddhijaguṇayorāśrayaḥ, vijñānāsamavāyikāraṇādhāratvādātmavat /
aśrotrāṇāmaviśeṣaguṇavatvāt /
kāryadravyeṇa svasamavāyikāraṇena kṛtādviṣṭhaguṇena guṇatvāvāntarajātīyaṃ paratvam /
samavāyikāraṇena svakārye kriyamāṇenādviṣṭhaguṇena guṇatvāvāntarajātīyamaparatvam /
kāraṇavināśād vināśaḥ /
children.translated_text:
2) The subject under dispute is a substratum of both cognition-produced quality and quality that does not reside in two [substrata], because of being a substratum that sustains the non-inherent cause of cognition, like the <s>ātman</s>.
Because those without ears possess non-specific qualities.
<s>Paratva</s> (priority) belongs to the sub-universal of quality-type, being a quality that does not reside in two, produced by the effect-substance in its own inherent cause.
<s>Aparatva</s> (posteriority) belongs to the sub-universal of quality-type, being a quality that does not reside in two, produced by the inherent cause in its own effect.
Destruction [occurs] from the destruction of the cause.

children.text: 12 buddhernirūpaṇam--
children.translated_text: 12. Examination of cognition (<s>buddhi</s>):

children.text:
1) buddhau pramāṇaṃ na vaktavyam, sarvatantrasiddhāntasiddhatvāt /
tadanabhyupagame svavacanavirodhādayaḥ prasañjanīyāḥ /
jñānatvaṃ asmadādimānasapratyakṣavyaktisamavetam, jñānajātitvātsattāvat /
asmadādītyavivakṣāyāṃ prameyatvādikaṃ yogipratyakṣasādhakamanusandheyam /
pratyakṣatvānabhyupagame jñānābhyupagamo nirmūlaḥ, tatkāraṇenaiva tatkalpakavyavahāropapatteḥ /
anavasthā tu nāsti, adṛṣṭādikāraṇasāmagryā niyāmakatvāt /
rūpādivadudbhūtatvasyāpi jñāne 'nabhyupagatatvāt, tathāvidhasyaiva pratyakṣatvāt /
children.translated_text:
1) A means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) need not be stated for cognition, since it is an established principle in all systems.
If one does not accept that, contradictions with one's own statement etc. should be pressed.
<s>Jñānatva</s> (cognition-ness) is co-inherent with instances perceptible to our mental perception, because it is a universal of <s>jñāna</s> (cognition), like <s>sattā</s> (existence).
If 'our etc.' is not intended [as a qualifier], <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability) etc. should be investigated as establishing yogic perception.
If the direct perceptibility [of cognition] is not accepted, the acceptance of cognition is baseless, since practical usage that postulates it is explicable by its cause alone.
But there is no infinite regress, because the aggregate of causes including <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit) serves as the determiner.
Since manifest-ness (<s>udbhūtatva</s>), as in the case of color etc., is also not accepted in cognition, only that which is of such a nature is directly perceptible.

children.text:
2) prabhākaramate vivādapadaṃ na mānasapratyakṣaṃ jñānatvāditi na sāmpratam, sarvamuktipakṣe dṛṣṭāntāsiddheḥ, anyasminnapi prabhākarasya sarvadā ekatve niścāyakābhāvāt /
na ca ghaṭaṃ jānāmītyatra kalpanālāghavādekameva jñānaṃ kalpanīyam --- ityarthāpattyupanyāso doṣaḥ syāt, na hi pareṇānekatvasādhane sopanyastā /
children.translated_text:
2) In the <s>Prābhākara</s> school, [the argument] 'the subject under dispute is not mental perception, because it is a cognition' is not correct [at present], because in the position of universal liberation, the example is unestablished; and in any other [position] too, the <s>Prābhākara</s> lacks a determiner that [cognition] is always one.
Nor would the presentation of <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) — 'in the [cognition] "I know the pot," a single cognition alone should be postulated due to parsimony of postulation' — be a fault, since the opponent has not adduced it in proving multiplicity.

children.text:
3) kiṃ ca jñānaṃ pratyakṣaṃ vastutvādghaṭavat /
na cājñānatvamupādhiḥ, tava sarvajñānasya pratyakṣatvāsiddheḥ /
nañaścetaretarābhāvavācakatve 'pi viśeṣaṇavaiyarthyāt /
jñānavyatiriktatvamiti tasyārthaḥ /
tatra ca na jñānapadasyopayogaḥ /
na ca jñānaṃ mānasapratyakṣaṃ na bhavati, jñānatvāditi sāmpratam, asādhāraṇatvāt /
na ca mānasapratyakṣatve 'navasthādoṣaḥ, yogyabhyupagamavādināṃ tasyāsambhavādadoṣācca /
tasmājjñānaṃ mānasapratyakṣamiti /
children.translated_text:
3) Moreover, cognition is perceptual (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), because it is a real entity, like a pot.
Nor is non-cognition-ness a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>), since the perceptuality of all your cognitions is unestablished.
Even if the negative particle conveys mutual absence, the qualifier would be purposeless.
The meaning of that is 'being different from cognition.'
And therein the word 'cognition' serves no purpose.
Nor is the current [objection] that cognition is not mental perception because it is a cognition — [valid], since it [the reason] is uncommon (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>).
Nor is there the fault of infinite regress in [asserting] mental perceptuality, since for those who hold the doctrine of competence (<s>yogyabhyupagamavādin</s>), that [regress] is impossible, and hence not a fault.
Therefore, cognition is mental perception (<s>mānasapratyakṣa</s>).

children.text: (1 akhyātivādanirāsaḥ--)
children.translated_text: (1. Refutation of the <s>akhyāti</s> doctrine —)

children.text:
atha kecidakhyātiṃ samarthayanti, vivādapadaṃ rajataviṣayaṃ rajatajñānatvāditi bruvate /
te tu praṣṭavyāḥ--- kimidaṃ rajatajñānaṃ nāma? 1 rajatasya jñānaṃ rajatajñānam? 2 rajataṃ tajjñānaṃ ca rajatajñānamiti vā? 3 rajataśabdollekhi jñānaṃ vā? 4 rajatārthinaḥ pravṛttihetubhūtaṃ jñānaṃ vā?
children.translated_text:
Now, some advocate non-apprehension (<s>akhyāti</s>), saying that the subject of dispute has silver as its object because it is a cognition of silver.
They should be asked: what is this so-called 'cognition of silver'? (1) Is it a cognition of silver [in the genitive sense]? (2) Or is silver together with its cognition [called] 'silver-cognition'? (3) Or is it a cognition suggested by the word 'silver'? (4) Or is it a cognition that is the cause of activity for one who desires silver?

children.text:
na prathamaḥ, ṣaṣṭhyarthasya viṣayaviṣayibhāvavyatirekeṇānyasyāsambhave
sādhyāviśiṣṭatvāt /
na dvitīyaḥ, ubhayāsiddheḥ, jñānasya nirākāratvāt /
nāpi tṛtīyaḥ, ullekhārthasya viśeṣaṇatve 'siddheḥ /
tajjñānajanitasmṛtimātrayogitve pūrvapadajñānenāpi rajatapadasya smaraṇasambhavena vyabhicārāt /
na caturthaḥ, vivekāgrahaṇavādināmidamiti jñānasyāpi śuktikālambanasya taddhetutvena vyabhicārāt /
etena rajatamiti pratyuktam, pūrvoktapakṣādbahirbhāvābhāvāt /
children.translated_text:
Not the first, since besides the subject-object relation no other meaning of the genitive is possible, and [the probandum] would be indistinguishable from what is to be proved.
Not the second, because both [parties] reject it, since cognition is formless (<s>nirākāra</s>).
Nor the third, since the meaning of 'suggestion' is unestablished as a qualifier.
If it merely requires the capacity for memory produced by that cognition, there would be deviation, since remembrance of the word 'silver' is possible even through cognition of the first element.
Not the fourth, because for those who hold the view of non-apprehension-of-the-distinction, even the 'this'-cognition that has the shell as its basis would be a cause of that [activity], resulting in deviation.
With this, [the position] 'it is silver' is also answered, since there is no going beyond the previously stated alternatives.

children.text:
yacca vimataṃ jñānaṃ yathārthaṃ jñānatvāditi bruvate, tatrobhayavādipratipannajñānavyakterasiddhatvādāśrayāsiddhiḥ /
rajatārthinaḥ pravṛttyanyathānupapattiparikalpitatajjanakajñānamātrasya pakṣīkāre pramāṇabādhaḥ, svasamānaviṣayeṣṭasādhanajñānajanyatvātpravṛtteḥ /
tvayāpyetasya samyagrajatapravṛttāvabhyupagamāt /
tatrāpi vivekagrahaṇamātrasyaiva prayojakatve padānāmanvitābhidhāyitvabhaṅgaprasaṅgaḥ /
bālakasya svātmani vivekāgrahaṇamātrātpravṛttiṃ paśyata uttamavṛddhavākyaprayogānantaraṃ pravarttamānamadhyamavṛddhapravṛtterapi tanmātrapūrvakatvakalpanāt /
tadakāraṇibhūtamapi tatra viśiṣṭajñānamavyabhicārabalena pravṛttipūrvakṣaṇe kalpyate /
tatra ca śabdasya kāraṇatvamiti vadato 'bhyupagatasiddhāntabhaṅgaḥ, tasya ca pravṛttimātreṇaiva kalpanābhāvāt /
children.translated_text:
And when they say 'the cognition in dispute is veridical, because it is a cognition' — therein, there is failure of the basis (<s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>), since the particular cognition accepted by both disputants is unestablished.
If one takes as the thesis merely the cognition that generates [activity], imagined through the impossibility of otherwise explaining the activity of one who desires silver, there is defeat by a means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇabādha</s>), since activity arises from the cognition that is the instrument for establishing the desired object having the same content as one's own.
Because even you accept this in the case of correct activity toward silver.
And therein, if the mere apprehension of a distinction were the operative factor, there would be the consequence of destroying the theory that words denote connected meanings (<s>anvitābhidhāna</s>).
Observing that a child's activity arises from the mere non-apprehension of distinction regarding its own self, and then imagining that even the middle-level adult's activity following upon the utterance of an authoritative elder's statement is also preceded by that alone —
even that qualified cognition, which is not the [actual] cause, is posited in the moment prior to activity by the force of non-deviation.
And for one who says that the word is the cause therein, there is a breaking of the accepted doctrine, since there is no positing of that [word] merely through activity alone.

children.text:
cakṣuścākṣuṣasatyajñānātiriktajñānajanakam, indriyatvāttvagvat /
vivādapadaṃ svasmāritapadārthānvayabodhakam, ākāṅkṣāsannidhimatpadakadambatvātsampratipannavat /
na ca yogyatāvattvamupādhiḥ, anākāṃkṣitāsannihitapadānāṃ yogyatāvattve 'pyabodhakatvāt /
ākāṃkṣāsannidhibhyāṃ viśeṣaṇe viśeṣyavaiyarthyāt /
tasmādastyayathārthaṃ jñānam /
children.translated_text:
The eye produces cognition other than valid visual cognition, because it is a sense faculty, like the sense of touch.
The subject of dispute produces cognition of the connection of the meanings of the words it recalls, because it is a collection of words possessing expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) and proximity (<s>sannidhi</s>), like an accepted [sentence].
Nor is possessing competence (<s>yogyatā</s>) a limiting condition, since even words that are not expected or proximate, though possessing competence, do not produce cognition.
Qualifying with expectancy and proximity renders the qualificand [competence] purposeless.
Therefore, there exists non-veridical cognition.

children.text: (2 apramājñānasya bhedāḥ--)
children.translated_text: (2. Types of non-valid cognition —)

children.text:
tacca lokapravṛttyanusāreṇa niścayāniścayabhedena bhinnam /
aniścayo 'pyanadhyavasāyaḥ saṃśaya iti /
mithyāniścayo viparyayaḥ /
viruddhakoṭisaṃsparśyaniścayaḥ saṃśayaḥ /
viruddhakoṭyasaṃsparśyaniścayo 'nadhyavasāyaḥ, asmābhirapyanavadhāraṇatvasya saṃśayānadhyavasāyayorabhyupagateḥ /
tena cāsmaduktāvāntarabhedasyābhyupagatatvādbhāsarvajñena sahāsmākaṃ nāsti vipratipattiriti nātra prapañcyate /
tarkastu nānyo 'sti, anadhyavasāyalakṣaṇenaiva saṃgṛhītatvāt /
children.translated_text:
And that [non-valid cognition], following worldly practice, is divided by the distinction of determinate and indeterminate.
Indeterminate cognition is [further] non-determination (<s>anadhyavasāya</s>) and doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>).
Wrong determinate [cognition] is error (<s>viparyaya</s>).
A non-determinate cognition touching contradictory alternatives is doubt.
A non-determinate cognition not touching contradictory alternatives is non-determination — since we also accept the non-ascertainment character of both doubt and non-determination.
And since our stated sub-divisions are accepted thereby, we have no disagreement with <s>Bhāsarvajña</s> on this point, so it is not elaborated here.
As for <s>tarka</s> (suppositional reasoning), it is not something separate, since it is already included under the definition of non-determination.

children.text: 3 pratyakṣajñānasya nirūpaṇam--
children.translated_text: 3. Examination of perceptual cognition —

children.text:
cakṣuścakṣurjanyasavikalpakavyatiriktajñānajanakam, indriyatvānmanovat /
vivādapadaṃ pratyakṣam, vastutvātprameyatvādghaṭavat /
pratyakṣasāmagryasadbhāva upādhiriti kaścit /
tanna, tasyāpi sādhanāt /
anupapannametad, bādhitaviṣayatvād, bāhyendriyāsambaddhaviṣayatvāt, manaso bāhye 'rthe 'svātantryāt /
anyathātiprasaṅgāditi cet, nātiprasaṅgo hi bādhakaḥ syāt, tanniyāmakamukhena sādhako 'pi bhaviṣyati /
ātmā jñātavya iti vākyaprasiddho yogajo dharmaḥ sarvadarśitvādiphalakaḥ /
na ca nāsau dharmakalpakaḥ, tena vinānupapatterabhāvāditi sāmpratam, yogavatāṃ viśiṣṭakule 'pyutpādasya tattvajñānopayogino dharmaviśeṣamantareṇāsambhavāt /
yadāha bhagavān svayameva-- `śucīnāṃ śrīmatāṃ gehe yogabhraṣṭo 'bhijāyate' (gī 6.11) iti /
children.translated_text:
The eye produces cognition different from the determinate cognition it generates, because it is a sense faculty, like the mind.
The subject of dispute is perceptual, because it is a real entity, because it is knowable, like a pot.
'The existence of the assemblage [of conditions] for perception is a limiting condition' — so says someone.
That is not so, since that [assemblage] too is established [by the argument].
This is untenable, because the object is sublated, because the object is not connected with an external sense-faculty, and because the mind lacks independence with respect to external objects.
If [one objects:] 'otherwise there would be over-extension' — no, for the over-extension would itself be the refuter, and through what determines that [limit], it would also become the establisher.
The self is to be known — the <s>dharma</s> born of <s>yoga</s>, well-known from scripture, has fruits such as omniscience.
Nor is the current [objection] that 'that [yoga] does not produce <s>dharma</s>, because of the absence of impossibility-without-it' [valid], since even for those possessing <s>yoga</s>, [birth] in a distinguished family — [which is] useful for knowledge of reality — is impossible without a special <s>dharma</s>.
As the Blessed One himself says: 'One who has fallen from <s>yoga</s> is born in the house of the pure and prosperous' (<s>Gītā</s> 6.41).

children.text:
asmadādijñānotpattyarthamindriyamarthena saṃyogasamavāyāvapekṣya yathāyogaṃ karoti /
saṃyuktasamavāyastu na saṃyogasamavāyavyatirekeṇānyo 'sti /
anyathā padārthāntaratvaprasaṅgāditi na prapañcyate /
nityamīśvarajñānaṃ yathārthaparokṣamiti pratyakṣam /
children.translated_text:
For the purpose of the arising of cognition for us and others, the sense-faculty acts upon the object requiring conjunction and inherence (<s>saṃyogasamavāya</s>) as appropriate.
Conjunctive inherence (<s>saṃyuktasamavāya</s>) is not something different from conjunction and inherence.
Otherwise there would be the consequence of being a separate category — so this is not elaborated.
The eternal cognition of <s>Īśvara</s> (God) is perceptual because it is veridical and non-mediate (<s>parokṣa</s>).

children.text: (4 anumitijñānasya nirūpaṇam--)
children.translated_text: (4. Examination of inferential cognition —)

children.text:
(4.1 syādetat --) anumitau kiṃ pramāṇamiti cet, pratyakṣamiti brūmaḥ /
bhavati hi vahnimān parvata iti jñānamiti hi dūradeśasthasya kasyāpi matiḥ /
tathāpi tena tasyānumititvaṃ kathamavagamyate iti mā vocaḥ, pratyakṣatve' pi samānatvāt /
tatkāraṇānumāne kiṃ pramāṇamityapi na vaktavyam, tatkiṃ pramāṇamātraṃ siddham, yena viśeṣe praśnaḥ syāt? tatsiddhau cānena pramāṇenānvayavyatirekāparanāmnā pratyakṣasāmagrīpraviṣṭenānyena vā siddhiriti yatkiñcidetat /
children.translated_text:
(4.1 Possible objection —) If one asks: what is the means of valid knowledge for inference? We say: perception.
For there is the cognition 'the mountain possesses fire' — thus thinks someone situated at a distance.
Even so, do not ask 'how does one know that to be an inference?' — because the same [question] would apply even to perception.
Nor should one ask 'what is the means of valid knowledge for the inference of its cause?' — for is mere pramāṇa-hood established, on the basis of which one could raise a question about a particular [type]? And when that is established, the establishment is either by this means of valid knowledge, alternatively called positive-and-negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>), included in the assemblage of conditions for perception, or by another — this is all inconsequential.

children.text: (4.2 vyāptisvarūpam--) nanu karaṇaṃ bhavadbhirucyamānamanupapannam, vyāpterabhāvāt, siddhāyāṃ vā jñātumaśakyatvāt, na, nirupādhikasambandhasya vyāptitvāt /
children.translated_text: (4.2 The nature of pervasion —) Objection: the instrument [of inference] as stated by you is untenable, because pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) does not exist, or because even if it exists it cannot be known. Reply: no, because the relation without a limiting condition is what constitutes pervasion.

children.text:
kaḥ punarupādhiriti cet, yena vinā yayoḥ sahabhāvādarśanaṃ tatra yena yasya vyabhicāraḥ, sa tasminnupādhiriti /
dṛṣṭāntamātravyāpako vā, sādhanavyāpakatve sati sādhyavyāpako vā /
sa dvividhaḥ--- anvayopādhirvyatirekopādhiriti /
ubhāvapi śaṅkitau niścitau ca /
vivādapadaṃ sattārahitaṃ jātitvātsattāvadityatra sattāsvarūpamupādhiḥ śaṅkyate /
agniṣomīyahiṃsā pāpasādhanaṃ hiṃsātvādityatra niṣiddhatvamupādhirniścīyate, sādhanenāvinābhāvābhāve 'pi sādhyena saha suvarṇasteyādiṣupādheranugamadarśanāt /
kṣityādikamakartṛkaṃ śarīriṇājanyatvādvyomavadityatrājanyatvamupādhirniścitaḥ, viśiṣṭasya prayojakatvakalpanāyāṃ pramāṇābhāvāt /
sarvaṃ kāryaṃ nityaprayatnapūrvakaṃ kāryatvādvyatirekeṇākāśavadityatrāprayatnapūrvakatvamupādhiḥ /
sādhye viśeṣaṇasyopādānamanvayini dūṣaṇam, vyatirekiṇi tu tadabhāvasya sādhanatvenopayoge tasya vyavacchedakatve nopayoga iti viśeṣaṇavaiyarthyam /
dhūmagatakaṭukatvādivad dūṣaṇameva /
etena śaṅkitopādhirapyūhyaḥ /
sādhyasādhanabhāvaśca vyāptisthala eva vivakṣita iti /
vyatirekeṇāpi tatrānvayisamānatvameveti caramalakṣaṇasyāpi tatra sambhavaḥ /
na copādhyabhāvo jñātuṃ na śakyate /
adṛṣṭānāṃ prathamapiṇḍa evābhāvenopādhitvānupapatteḥ /
na hyavidyamānaṃ japākusumamupādhirbhavati /
teṣāṃ pañcapiṇḍādarśanenābhāvo niścīyate /
atīndriyopādhiprasañjanaṃ tu nānumānamātrasadbhāve 'pi bhavitumarhati, nirbījatvāt /
anumānaviśeṣe tu vādiprativādyabhyupagataṃ tatpadārthaviśeṣasvarūpanirūpaṇena nirākartavyamiti /
children.translated_text:
If one asks: what then is a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>)? It is that without which the co-presence of two things is not observed, and through which the deviation of one from the other [occurs] — that is the <s>upādhi</s> with respect to that.
Or, [it is] what pervades only the example, or what, being pervaded by the <s>sādhana</s> (probans), also pervades the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum).
It is of two kinds: a positive limiting condition (<s>anvayopādhi</s>) and a negative limiting condition (<s>vyatirekopādhi</s>).
Both are either suspected or ascertained.
In 'the subject of dispute is devoid of universal being (<s>sattā</s>), because it is a universal (<s>jāti</s>), like [something] possessing <s>sattā</s>' — the nature of <s>sattā</s> is suspected as a limiting condition.
In 'the violence of the <s>Agniṣomīya</s> sacrifice is a means of sin, because it is violence' — being prohibited is ascertained as a limiting condition, because even though there is no invariable co-presence with the <s>sādhana</s>, the co-presence of the <s>upādhi</s> with the <s>sādhya</s> is observed in cases like theft of gold.
In 'earth and the like are not produced by an agent, because they are not produced by an embodied being, like space' — non-producedness is an ascertained limiting condition, because there is no means of valid knowledge for imagining the particular [attribute] as the operative factor.
In 'everything that is an effect is preceded by the eternal effort [of God], because it is an effect, or by elimination, like space' — not-being-preceded-by-effort is the limiting condition.
Adopting a qualifier in the probandum is a fault in a positive [concomitance] proof; but in a negative one, when the absence of that [qualifier] is useful as the probans, and when it [merely] delimits, it is of no use — hence the purposelessness of the qualifier.
Like the pungency and such [properties] belonging to smoke, this is indeed a fault.
With this, suspected limiting conditions too should be inferred.
And the relation of probandum and probans is intended only at the locus of pervasion.
Since by negative concomitance too the situation there is the same as for positive concomitance, the last definition also applies there.
Nor is the absence of a limiting condition impossible to know.
For things not [yet] observed, the impossibility of being a limiting condition through absence at the very first instance [of observation] —
for a non-existent <s>japā</s>-flower does not become a limiting condition.
The absence [of an upādhi] for those [cases] is ascertained by the non-observation in the five instances.
But the suggestion of a supersensory limiting condition cannot arise even from the mere existence of an inference, since it is without basis.
In a particular inference, however, what is accepted by both proponent and opponent should be refuted through determining the nature of the particular category concerned.

children.text:
(4.3 parārthānumānam--) tatra pratijñāhetunidarśanānusandhānapratyāmnānātmakaṃ vākyarūpaṃ parārthānumānam /
tatrākāṃkṣākrameṇa laukikapadapravṛtteḥ /
siddhasādhyatāyāśca parihārārthamāśrayajñānasya ca prathamamākāṃkṣitatvāt prathamataḥ pratijñāvacanam /
tadanantaraṃ hetoḥ, tadāśrayatvāt /
kāraṇamātrasiddhau viśeṣe jijñāsāyāṃ satyāmākāṃkṣāparyālocanayā hetumātrasyaiva vacanam /
tadanu dharmajijñāsāyāṃ satyāṃ vyāpterākāṃkṣitatvāttannirūpaṇam /
tadanantaraṃ sarvavākyānāmekavākyatāpratipādanāya sādhyasiddherabhilaṣitāyāḥ khyāpanāya nigamanavacanam /
tathā hi śabdo 'nityaḥ kāryatvād, yatkāryaṃ tadanityaṃ yathā ghaṭaḥ, kāryaśca śabdaḥ, tasmācchabdo 'nityaḥ /
pakṣavacanaṃ pratijñā, hetuvacanamapadeśaḥ, dṛṣṭāntavacanamudāharaṇam, dṛṣṭāntavacanānantarahetuvacanamupanayaḥ, upanayānantaraṃ sahetukaṃ pratijñāvacanaṃ nigamanam /
gamyamānārthatvānnigamanaṃ na prayoktavyamiti cenna, tasyādūṣaṇatvāt /
anyathā hetumātrameva prayoktavyaṃ syād, viduṣāṃ viśiṣṭārthasyārthādeva pratīteḥ /
children.translated_text: (4.3 Inference for others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>)) Therein, inference for others is of the nature of a sentence (<s>vākyarūpa</s>) consisting of thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>), reason (<s>hetu</s>), illustration (<s>nidarśana</s>), application (<s>anusandhāna</s>), and restatement (<s>pratyāmnāna</s>). Therein, the statement of the thesis comes first, because of the sequence of expectation in the usage of ordinary words, for the purpose of avoiding the fallacy of proving what is already established, and because the knowledge of the locus is desired first. Then the reason, because it is dependent on that [locus]. When merely the cause is established, and when there is a desire to know the particular, by deliberation on the expectation, the statement of merely the reason [suffices]. Then, when there is a desire to know the property, because the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is desired, its determination [follows]. Then, for establishing the unity of all the sentences and for proclaiming the desired establishment of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), the statement of the conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>). For example: 'Sound is non-eternal, because of being an effect; whatever is an effect is non-eternal, like a pot; and sound is an effect; therefore sound is non-eternal.' The statement of the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) is the <s>pratijñā</s>; the statement of the reason is the designation (<s>apadeśa</s>); the statement of the example is the <s>udāharaṇa</s>; the statement of the reason following the statement of the example is the application (<s>upanaya</s>); and the statement of the thesis together with the reason following the application is the conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>). If it be objected that the conclusion need not be stated because its meaning is already understood — no, because it is not a fault. Otherwise, only the reason alone should be stated, since for the learned, the qualified meaning is understood by implication.

children.text: (4.4 avayavadvayavādaḥ--)
children.translated_text: (4.4 The doctrine of two members (<s>avayavadvayavāda</s>))

children.text:
vayaṃ tanna budhyāmahe, sādhanānupayuktavacanasyādhikatvāt /
prativādinā hi sādhanajijñāsā kṛtā kiṃ pramāṇamiti /
tatra yāvadaṅgaviśiṣṭaṃ sādhanam, tāvad vaktavyam /
aṅge ca dve eva vyāptipakṣadharmatve /
na hi tato 'dhikaṃ pravṛtyaṅgam /
children.translated_text: We do not understand that [five-membered view], because statements not useful for the proof are excessive. For the opponent has made an inquiry about the proof: 'what is the means of knowledge?' Therein, as much as the proof qualified by its members, that much should be stated. And the members are only two: <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) and <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> (the property of the thesis). For there is no member of activity beyond those two.

children.text:
tadadhikabhūtaṃ jñātavyaṃ kimasti? kālātyayāpadiṣṭasyānaikāntike 'ntarbhāvāt /
nirupādhikānumānadvayasya caikatrāsambhavāt /
sambhave vā vastuno dvyātmakatvaṃ ko nivārayet? nirupādhikasya sādhyaparityāge svabhāvaparityāgaprasaṅgāt /
tadevaṃ sthite rūpadvaye, tatpratipādanārthaṃ vacanadvayameva vaktavyam, hetoḥ pakṣadharmatāvacanena viśiṣṭavācinā tatsiddheḥ /
tasmādyatkāryam, tadanityaṃ yathā ghaṭaḥ, kāryaśca śabda ityanvayini /
yannityam, tadakāryaṃ yathā vyoma, kāryaśca śabda iti vyatirekiṇi /
tasmādavayavadvayameva prayoktavyam /
anvayavyatirekītyaparo neṣyate, ekenaivānumitisiddhau samuditasya hetutve pramāṇābhāvāt /
avinābhāvajanitaparokṣānubhavo 'numitiḥ tatsādhakatamamanumānam /
tallakṣaṇarahitaṃ tatsadṛśamanumānābhāsam /
children.translated_text: What more is there to be known beyond those? Because the fallacy of advancing an expired argument (<s>kālātyayāpadiṣṭa</s>) is subsumed under the inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). And because two inferences without limiting conditions cannot [validly] apply to a single [subject]. Or, if they can, who would prevent the thing from having a dual nature? Because for one without limiting conditions, the abandonment of the <s>sādhya</s> would entail the abandonment of its own nature. Thus, when the matter stands with two forms, only two statements should be made for establishing those — since their establishment is achieved by a statement of the reason qualified by the statement of the property of the thesis. Therefore: 'whatever is an effect is non-eternal, like a pot; and sound is an effect' — in the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>). 'Whatever is eternal is not an effect, like space; and sound is an effect' — in the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>). Therefore, only two members should be employed. The [third type called] 'positive-and-negative' (<s>anvayavyatirekī</s>) is not accepted by another [school], because when inference is established by even one alone, there is no means of knowledge for the combined being the cause. An inferential cognition (<s>anumiti</s>) is an indirect experience generated by invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>); that which most effectively produces it is inference (<s>anumāna</s>). What lacks that definition but resembles it is a semblance of inference (<s>anumānābhāsa</s>).

children.text:
(4.5 hetvābhāsāḥ--) taccāsiddhaviruddhānaikāntikabhedabhinnam /
aniścitapakṣavṛttirasiddhaḥ, śabdo 'nityaḥ cākṣuṣatvāditi /
sa cobhayāsiddho 'nyatarāsiddhaśca /
pakṣavipakṣayoreva vartamāno heturviruddhaḥ, nityaḥ śabdaḥ kāryatvāditi /
asādhakatvajñāpakatvaṃ hi dūṣaṇam /
sādhyaviparītānaupādhikasambandhitayā viruddhasya liṅgatā /
nanu sādhyaviparītagāmitā kvacidvyabhicarati, yenānaupādhikatve samarthaṃ syādato viśiṣṭaṃ na dūṣaṇamiti cet /
tanna, jalpavādayorhi parasādhanaṃ nivartya svapakṣe sādhanaṃ vācyam, ato lāghavāya viśiṣṭopanyāsaḥ /
sādhanāntaraṃ tu na vācyameva /
vitaṇḍāyāṃ tu vipakṣavṛttitā paramudbhāvyā, anumityutpattipratibandhakatvaṃ ca dūṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: (4.5 Fallacies of the reason (<s>hetvābhāsas</s>)) And that [semblance] is divided into the unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), the contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), and the inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). That whose presence in the thesis is uncertain is unestablished, as in 'sound is non-eternal, because of being visible.' That is [further divided into] unestablished for both parties and unestablished for one party. A reason that is present only in the thesis and its opposite is contradictory, as in 'sound is eternal, because of being an effect.' For being a fault consists in making known the inability to prove. The status of the contradictory as a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is by virtue of its having a non-contingent connection with the opposite of the <s>sādhya</s>. If it be objected that going toward the opposite of the <s>sādhya</s> sometimes deviates, and therefore the qualified [version] is not a fault because the non-contingent [connection] would be effective — no, because in <s>jalpa</s> (disputation) and so forth, having set aside the opponent's proof, one must state one's own proof; therefore the qualified [version] is presented for the sake of economy. But an alternative proof need not be stated at all. In <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (destructive criticism), however, the presence in the counter-position should be highlighted for the opponent, and the obstruction of the arising of inference is the fault.

children.text:
sādhyatadabhāvayorvartamānatvena jñāto 'naikāntikaḥ /
sa ca niścitaḥ, śaṅkitaśca /
sa kaḥ? anityaḥ śabdaḥ, prameyatvāditi niścitaḥ /
mano vibhu, sarvadā sparśarahitadravyatvāditi śaṅkitaḥ, sopādhikatvāt /
children.translated_text: That which is known as present in both the <s>sādhya</s> and its absence is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). And that is [of two kinds]: ascertained and suspected. What is the ascertained? 'Sound is non-eternal, because of being a knowable object (<s>prameya</s>)' — this is ascertained. 'The mind is all-pervading, because it is a substance always devoid of touch' — this is suspected, because it has a limiting condition.

children.text: (4.6 dṛṣṭāntābhāsaḥ--)
children.translated_text: (4.6 Fallacies of the example (<s>dṛṣṭāntābhāsa</s>))

children.text:
dṛṣṭāntābhāsastu sādhyavikalasādhanavikalavyāptyakathanaviparītavyāptikathanāśrayahīnāḥ /
sādharmyodāharaṇavaidharmyodāharaṇe sādhyavyāvṛttasādhanavyāvṛttāvyāptikathanaviparītavyāptikathanādīnāmudāharaṇāni tu praśastapādairabhihitānīti na prapañcyante /
ubhayavikalastu nāsti, tasya sādhyasādhanavikalābhyāmanatirekāt /
na hi kālātyayāpadiṣṭānaikāntikatvaṃ nāma samuditamasti dūṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: A fallacy of the example is: lacking the <s>sādhya</s>, lacking the <s>sādhana</s>, not stating the pervasion, stating a reversed pervasion, or lacking a locus. For the positive example (<s>sādharmya</s>) and the negative example (<s>vaidharmya</s>), the instances of lacking the <s>sādhya</s>, lacking the <s>sādhana</s>, not stating the pervasion, and stating a reversed pervasion have been presented by <s>Praśastapāda</s> and are not elaborated here. A [fallacy] lacking both [<s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s>] does not exist, because it does not differ from one lacking the <s>sādhya</s> or lacking the <s>sādhana</s>. For the combined fault of advancing an expired argument and being inconclusive does not exist as a single fault.

children.text: (5 ārṣajñānasya nirūpaṇam--)
children.translated_text: (5 Examination of seer's knowledge (<s>ārṣajñāna</s>))

children.text:
ārṣasadbhāve kiṃ pramāṇamiti cet, pratyakṣamiti brumaḥ /
asti tāvadvipratipannā pratibhā kvacidarthāvisaṃvādinī /
tasyā anadhigatārthagantṛtvādanubhūtitvaṃ siddham /
na caitadatiriktaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ nāma yat sādhanīyamavaśiṣyate /
na cārthāvisaṃvāditvameva nāsti, bādhakābhāvāt /
na ca pratibhātvādarthavisaṃvādaḥ, aparokṣatvāt /
anyathā pratyakṣasyārthavisaṃvādaprasaṅgāt /
nanu jñānāvisaṃvāditvagrāhakapratyekṣaṇa tatpūrvakābādhitatatpravṛttibhyāṃ tajjñānaviṣayīkṛtārthasya yathārthasya kriyākāritvena bādhitaviṣayatvādanumānasyaiva durbalatvamiti cet, samaḥ samādhiḥ /
pratibhātvāviśeṣe 'pi kathamekasya saṃvāditvam, aparasya visaṃvāditvamiti cet, na, aparokṣatvāviśeṣe 'pi pratyakṣasya kasyacitsaṃvāditvaṃ kasyaciditi kutaḥ? avāntaravaijātyāditi cet, tulyamastu pratibhāyāṃ prāmāṇyam /
children.translated_text: If asked 'what is the means of knowledge for the existence of seer's [knowledge]?' — we say: direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). There does indeed exist a disputed intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>) that in some cases does not fail to correspond to its object. Its status as experience (<s>anubhūti</s>) is established because it reaches objects not previously known. And there is no additional validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) beyond this that remains to be established. And it is not the case that correspondence with the object is absent, because of the absence of an invalidator. Nor is there non-correspondence with the object merely because of being an intuition, because of being non-mediated (<s>aparokṣa</s>). Otherwise, there would be the undesirable consequence of non-correspondence for perception as well. If it be objected that the perception apprehending the non-deceptiveness of a cognition, together with the subsequent uncontradicted activity based on it, establishes that the object of that cognition is veridical and effective — and therefore [intuition], being an object of contradiction, means that inference itself is weaker — the answer is the same. If asked 'even though there is no difference in being an intuition, how is one [instance] veridical and another deceptive?' — no, because even though there is no difference in being non-mediated, how is one [instance of] perception veridical and another not? If answered 'because of internal sub-type differences' — let the same hold for the validity of intuition.

children.text:
tathāpi pūrvayorantarbhāva iti cet, na, avinābhāvānapekṣatvenānumitāvanantarbhāvāt /
parokṣatvānna ca pratyakṣam /
kathaṃ punarasyāḥ parokṣatvamiti cet, anumiterapi parokṣatā katham? indriyavyāpārābhāve utpadyamānatvāditi cet, samānametat /
antaḥkaraṇasya vyāpāro 'stīti cet, samānam /
dharmaviśeṣajatvādyogipratyakṣāntarbhūtamiti cet, na, dharmaviśeṣajatvāsiddheḥ, dharmaviśeṣamātrajanyatvasya vyabhicārāt /
avinābhāvanirapekṣaḥ samyak parokṣānubhava ārṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: If even so [it be argued that] it is subsumed under the earlier [two means of knowledge] — no, because it is not subsumed under inference (<s>anumiti</s>), since it does not depend on invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>). Nor is it perception, because of being indirect (<s>parokṣa</s>). If asked 'how is it indirect?' — well, how is inference also indirect? If answered 'because it arises in the absence of sense-organ activity' — the same applies [to seer's knowledge]. If [one says] 'there is activity of the inner organ' — the same applies. If [it be argued] 'because it is produced by a specific merit (<s>dharmaviśeṣa</s>), it is subsumed under yogic perception' — no, because the production by a specific merit is not established, because mere production by some specific merit deviates [from yogic perception]. A correct indirect experience that does not depend on invariable concomitance is seer's knowledge (<s>ārṣa</s>).

children.text:
svasamānaviṣayasaṃskārajaṃ smaraṇam /
yathārthasya pramāṇabhāve nāsti vipratipattiḥ, parairapi tasya samyaganubhavatvābhyupagamāt, tārkikairapi yathārthajñānatvasya tatrānirākaraṇāt /
tasmātsamyaganubhavaḥ prameti pūrvācāryāḥ /
yathārthaṃ jñānaṃ prameti navīnāḥ /
ayameva ca bhāṣyakartturabhiprāya, anyathā pramāṇamadhye tatpaṭhanamasaṅgataṃ syāt /
na hi pramitividyāśabdayorloke 'rthabhedo 'sti /
tasmāccaturvidhaṃ pramāṇam /
((tathā śrutismṛtipratyakṣamaitihyamānacatuṣṭayamiti / ))
children.translated_text: Memory (<s>smaraṇa</s>) is produced by latent impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) of the same content as itself. There is no disagreement about its being a means of knowledge when it corresponds to reality, because even by others its status as correct experience is accepted, and because even logicians do not refute its being veridical knowledge. Therefore the earlier teachers [say]: a correct experience is valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>). The later [teachers say]: knowledge that corresponds to reality is valid cognition. And this is indeed the intent of the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> [i.e., <s>Vātsyāyana</s>]; otherwise, its enumeration among the means of knowledge would be incongruous. For in common usage there is no difference in meaning between the words <s>pramiti</s> (valid cognition) and <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge). Therefore the means of knowledge are fourfold. ((Similarly, scripture (<s>śruti</s>), tradition (<s>smṛti</s>), perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), and history (<s>itihāsa</s>) — a group of four.))

children.text: (6 śabdapramāṇasyānumāne 'ntarbhāvanirūpaṇam--)
