children.translated_text: (6 Examination of the subsumption of verbal testimony (<s>śabdapramāṇa</s>) under inference)

children.text:
nanu tato 'tiriktānyapi śabdādīni santīti cet, na aprasiddheḥ /
nadyāstīre pañca phalāni santīti vākyādarthapratyayo jāyate iti cet, atra kasya kāraṇatvamiti vibhāvyatām--- na pratyakṣasya, arthasyāvispaṣṭatvāt /
nānumānasya vyāpterabhāvāt /
na hi nadyāstīre pañca phalāni santīti vākyena nadītīraphalasambandhasyāvyabhicaritaḥ sambandhaḥ, anāptavākye tadabhāvāt /
āptatve satīti viśeṣaṇe pūrvamarthasiddherasiddho vākyārthaḥ, samyagjñānavata eva tattvāt /
tadetadasat, puruṣaviśeṣoktatvasya hetuviśeṣaṇatvenaivopādānāt /
tena ca proktasyāpyanumānānnāprayojakatā /
yatra tu taduktasyāpi vyabhicāraḥ kvacit, tatra tadvyatiriktatve satītyapi viśeṣaṇam, viśiṣṭasya vyāptibalena sādhanatvam /
yatra tu vyabhicārasthalaṃ syāt, tatra nārthaniścayaḥ, kintu sandeha eva, etāvatāpi laukikānāmarthe sandehādeva pravṛttisiddheḥ /
children.translated_text: If it be objected that there are additional [means of knowledge] beyond those, such as verbal testimony and so forth — no, because they are not well-established. If [one argues] 'from the sentence "there are five fruits on the riverbank," a cognition of the object arises' — let it be examined what is the cause here. Not perception, because the object is not clearly [perceived]. Not inference, because of the absence of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion). For through the sentence 'there are five fruits on the riverbank,' the connection between the riverbank and the fruits is not an invariable connection, because in a sentence by an unreliable person that [connection] is absent. If the qualifier 'when there is reliability' [is added], the meaning of the sentence is already established beforehand — because only one who has correct knowledge has that [reliability]. This objection is wrong, because 'being uttered by a specific person' is adopted precisely as a qualifier of the reason. And even what is stated by that [specific person] does not lack purposefulness due to inference. But where even what is stated by that [person] deviates in some case, there too the qualifier 'when being distinct from that' [is added], and the qualified [reason] has probative force through the power of [its] pervasion. But where there would be a case of deviation, there is no certainty of the object, but only doubt; and even so much suffices for ordinary people, since their activity is established from mere doubt about the object.

children.text: (7 vedānāṃ pauruṣeyatvanirūpaṇam--)
children.translated_text: (7 Examination of the human authorship (<s>pauruṣeyatva</s>) of the <s>Vedas</s>)

children.text:
vedasya puruṣaviśeṣakṛtatvābhāvena kathamanumānamiti cet, tarhyāptoktatvasyāpyabhāvenāprāmāṇyaprasaṅgāt /
na ca svataḥ prāmāṇyaṃ vedasya, samyaṅmithyābodhasādhāraṇātiriktakāraṇajanyatvāt /
tathā hi pramā samyaṅmithyābodhasādhāraṇātiriktakāraṇajanyā, kāryatvād, apramāṇyavat /
samyaktvaṃ niyatajñāne 'pi kadācinna nirdhāryate, niścayatvāniścaye 'pi sandehaviṣayatvād, apramāvat /
vivādāspadaṃ kāryam, vedajanyamatijam, kāryatvādghaṭavat /
īśvarakṛtatvāviśeṣe 'pi buddhādivākyānāmāgantukadoṣasamavadhānādaprāmāṇyam, buddhādīnāmanāptatvāt /
vedārtho vedanirapekṣapramitivedyo, meyatvādghaṭavat /
vedārtho vedanirapekṣasvālambanamatyādhāraviracitavākyameyo meyatvāt, sampratipannavat /
yacca vedasyādhyayanaṃ sarvaṃ gurvadhyayanapūrvakam /
children.translated_text:
If one objects: how can there be inference regarding the <s>Veda</s>, since it was not composed by a particular person? Then there would be the unwanted consequence of invalidity, since it also lacks the property of being stated by a trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>).
Nor does the <s>Veda</s> have intrinsic validity (<s>svataḥ prāmāṇya</s>), because it is produced by a cause additional to [those] common to correct and erroneous cognition.
For indeed, valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>) is produced by a cause additional to [those] common to correct and erroneous cognition, because it is an effect, like invalidity.
Correctness is sometimes not determined even in definite knowledge, because even the certainty of certainty is a possible object of doubt, like non-valid cognition.
The subject of dispute is an effect — one produced by Vedic-generated understanding — because it is an effect, like a pot.
Even though there is no distinction in being created by <s>Īśvara</s>, the statements of <s>Buddha</s> etc. are invalid due to the presence of adventitious defects, because <s>Buddha</s> etc. are not trustworthy persons.
The meaning of the <s>Veda</s> is knowable through valid cognition independent of the <s>Veda</s>, because it is a knowable (<s>meya</s>), like a pot.
The meaning of the <s>Veda</s> is to be known through a sentence composed by a substratum of understanding whose own object is independent of the <s>Veda</s>, because it is knowable, like the acknowledged [knowables].
And all study of the <s>Veda</s> is preceded by study under a teacher.

children.text: vedādhyayanasāmānyādadhunādhyayanaṃ yathā //
children.translated_text: Just as present study [is preceded by a teacher], so too from the general practice of Vedic study.

children.text: (ślo vā vākya 366)
children.translated_text: (<s>Ślokavārttika</s>, sentence 366)

children.text:
tatra ca gurvadhyayanapūrvakatvamātre siddhasādhyatā /
brahmaṇo 'pi jīvaviśeṣasya suptaprabuddhavatkalpāntarānubhūtavedasmaraṇāt /
na ca pravāhavicchedādapraṇetṛpūrvakatvaprasaṅgaḥ, uccāryamāṇavākyasadṛśavākyajñānanirapekṣasyaiva tatra kartṛtvābhyupagamāt /
svatantrapuruṣapraṇetṛtvavivakṣāyāṃ tu sādhyavikalatvam /
ubhayavādisampratipannapakṣāṅgīkāre 'pi siddhasādhyatā /
aparatra cāśrayāsiddhiḥ /
bhāratādhyayanāderapi evaṃ kuśaṃkyatvāt /
tatsaṃpradāyāvicchede satyasmaryamāṇakartṛkatvāditi tu mama? tava? uta yasya kasya sādhāraṇyena veti? prathamatṛtīyacaturtheṣvasiddhiḥ /
dvitīye tu vyabhicāraḥ /
ata eva madanumāne ... {One line lost in the MS.} anyathā siddhasādhanatvādakāryatvaṃ copādhiḥ /
children.translated_text:
Therein, if it is [proved] merely that [Vedic study] is preceded by study under a teacher, there is the fallacy of proving what is already established.
Even <s>Brahmā</s>, being a particular <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), remembers the <s>Veda</s> experienced in a previous cosmic cycle, just as one who has slept and awakened [remembers].
Nor is there the unwanted consequence of being without a prior author due to the interruption of the stream, because authorship is accepted there only for one who is independent of knowledge of a sentence similar to the sentence being uttered.
But if the intention is authorship by an independent person, then the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is deficient.
Even if one accepts the position acknowledged by both disputants, there is the fallacy of proving what is already established.
In the other [position], there is the fallacy of unestablished substratum.
Because the study of the <s>Mahābhārata</s> etc. too can be similarly suspected.
[The argument:] 'because, when the tradition is unbroken, it has an unremembered author' — is this mine? Yours? Or someone's in general? In the first, third, and fourth [options], there is non-establishment.
In the second, there is deviation.
Therefore, in my inference... {One line lost in the manuscript.} Otherwise, because of proving what is already established, non-effectness too is a limiting condition.

children.text: (8 upamānapramāṇasyānumāne 'ntarbhāvanam--)
children.translated_text: (8. Subsumption of the means of valid cognition of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) under inference:)

children.text:
upamānaṃ tu madīyā gauranena sadṛśīti gosadṛśagavayamālokayato 'numānameva /
kathamiti cet, bhavati hi pūrvaṃ gavi gavayasādṛśyamityanumitiḥ /
anugatadharmasya gavaye 'pi vartamānasya pratyakṣagrahaṇārhatvāt, mānāntaropanītasyāpi viśeṣaṇatvopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Upamāna</s> (comparison), however — 'my cow is similar to this [gavaya]' — is just inference for one observing a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) similar to a cow.
If one asks how, [we reply]: there is indeed first the inference 'in a cow, there is similarity to a <s>gavaya</s>.'
Because the common property existing in the <s>gavaya</s> too is worthy of being grasped by perception, and because even what is brought by another means of knowledge can serve as a qualifier.

children.text:
athavā madīyā gauranena sadṛśī, svasādṛśyenaitadavacchedakatvād, bhrātṛbhaginīvat /
anyathā gavayasādṛśyasyāpyagrahaṇaprasaṅgāt /
pratyakṣamate tadanu viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvasya kāmacāratvadarśanena sādṛśyāvacchinnagavyanumānam /
children.translated_text:
Alternatively: 'my cow is similar to this,' because through its own similarity, it delimits this [gavaya], like a brother and sister.
Otherwise, there would be the unwanted consequence that the similarity of the <s>gavaya</s> too would not be grasped.
In the perceptual view, seeing that the qualifier-qualificand relation is arbitrary, there is inference of the <s>gavaya</s> delimited by similarity.

children.text:
saṃjñāsaṃjñisambandhakaḥ svasandigdhe nyāyasampāditavyaktiḥ paścānniścitavākyārthamavabudhyate iti /
sādṛśyamātrasya gavayapadavācyate apratītagūnāmavyavahāraprasaṅgaparyālocanayā nirnimittapraśnānanuguṇyacintyamānāptasyānyathākathakatvāsambhāvanena ca sādṛśyasyopalakṣaṇatve nirṇīte tadeva vākyaṃ gavayapadasya gavayatvanimittatvaṃ bodhayati /
gavayaśabdaḥ gavayatvavācakaḥ, asati vṛttyantare 'bhiyuktaiḥ prayujyamānanaimittikapadatvādgotve gośabdavat /
na ca viśeṣaṇāsiddhiḥ, vṛttyantarābhāvatvasya tvayāpyabhyupagatatvāt /
anyathānumānasyāpravṛttiḥ, anugrāhakatarkābhāvāt /
vivādapadaṃ gavayapadanimittam, viśiṣṭajātitvādvyatirekeṇa gotvavaditi /
children.translated_text:
One who has the relation of name and named, whose instance is established by reasoning in the case of one's own doubt, subsequently understands the meaning of a sentence that has been ascertained.
When, through the consideration that there would be the unwanted consequence of non-usage for those who have not understood that mere similarity is what is denoted by the word '<s>gavaya</s>,' and through the inconceivability of the trustworthy person explaining otherwise being contrary to the unprompted question, it is determined that similarity is merely indicatory — that very sentence teaches that the word '<s>gavaya</s>' has <s>gavayatva</s> (gavaya-ness) as its denotative basis.
The word '<s>gavaya</s>' denotes <s>gavayatva</s>; in the absence of another semantic function, being used with [that function].

children.text: (9 arthāpatterapyanumānatvopavarṇam--)
children.translated_text: (9. Description of presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>) as being inference:)

children.text:
arthāpattirapyanumānam /
tathā hi sambandhabodhamantareṇānupapadyamānārthadarśane 'pi pramiterupapattiḥ, buddhe tu sambandhe bhavato 'pyanumitireva /
pramāṇadvayavirodho 'pi sāvakāśānavakāśayoḥ sāvakāśasya viṣayasaṃkoca iti vyāptidarśanavato gehānupalabdhiṃ niravakāśāṃ paśyatastadvirodhijīvanavākyaṃ sāvakāśaṃ paśyatastasya vākyasya bahirviṣayatvapramitiranumitireva /
children.translated_text:
<s>Arthāpatti</s> (presumption) too is inference.
For indeed, even when seeing a fact that is inexplicable without the knowledge of a relation, valid cognition is possible; but when the relation is known, for you too it is just inference.
The conflict between two means of knowledge [is resolved as follows]: between one that has scope and one that has no scope, the one with scope has its domain restricted. Thus, for one who sees the pervasion, who sees the non-apprehension in the house as having no scope, and who sees the sentence about [his] being alive as having scope — the cognition that that sentence has the external [location] as its domain is just inference.

children.text:
śrutārthāpattistu na śaṅkāmapyārohati, vākyamantareṇa vākyānupapatterabhāvāt na hi pīno devadatto divā na bhuṃkte' iti vākyaṃ `rātrau bhuṃkte' iti vākyena vinānupapannam /
śābdī hyākāṃkṣā śabdenaiva paripūryate, na hi pacatīti padaṃ pratyakṣādinā nirākāṃkṣamapi tu odanapadeneti cet, na, asmin vākye ākāṃkṣāyogyatayorabhāvāt kriyākārakayoḥ sampūrṇatvāt /
pīnatvaṃ bhojanena vinā 'nupapannam, bhojanakāryatvāditi cet, na tarhyākāṃkṣāvirahaḥ, yogyatāvirahastu syāt /
na ca so 'pyasti traikālikabhojananiṣedhe hi sa syāt, na hyabhuktvā pīnaḥ kṣaṇamapi tiṣṭhati /
traikālikabhojananiṣedhastu viśiṣṭakāryādrātribhojanakāraṇānumānaṃ svairaṃ pravartatām, na rātrivākyakalpanāvakāśaḥ /
children.translated_text:
But <s>śrutārthāpatti</s> (verbal presumption) does not even raise a doubt, because in the absence of a sentence, the inexplicability of a sentence does not exist. For the sentence 'Fat <s>Devadatta</s> does not eat during the day' is not inexplicable without the sentence 'he eats at night.'
If one objects: verbal expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) is fulfilled by a word alone — for the word 'cooks' is not freed from expectancy by perception etc., but rather by the word 'rice' — [we reply]: No, because in this sentence there is absence of both expectancy and semantic fitness, since the action and its factors are complete.
Fatness is inexplicable without eating; eating [is the explanation].

children.text:
astu tarhi pacatītyatraivodanapadakalpanā śrutārthāpattiriti cet, tatrāpyarthasyaiva kalpanāt /
śabdākṣipto 'pi śabda eveti niyame 'tiprasaṅgaḥ /
athavā tathāvidhapadasya viśiṣṭasaṃsargeṇaiva vyāptyā tatkalpanamiti /
api ca keyamākāṃkṣā nāma? jijñāseti cet, sā tu kutaḥ? śabdārthayoraparyavasānāditi cet, tarhīṣṭāpattireva /
na caivaṃ śabdavilopaprasaṅgaḥ, iṣṭatvāt, tasya vākyānumāne 'ntarbhāvo 'bhyadhāyi /
children.translated_text:
If one says: then let the postulation of the word 'rice' in 'cooks' itself be <s>śrutārthāpatti</s> — even there, it is just the postulation of a meaning.
If the rule is that what is prompted by a word is itself a word, there is over-extension.
Alternatively, the postulation of such a word is through the pervasion of a particular connection.
Moreover, what is this 'expectancy'? If [one says] 'the desire to know' — then from where [does it arise]? If [one says] 'from the incompleteness of the word and its meaning' — then it is just <s>iṣṭāpatti</s> (desired presumption).
Nor is there the unwanted consequence of the elimination of [verbal testimony as a] word [pramāṇa], because this is desired, since its subsumption under sentence-inference is accepted.

children.text: (10 anupalabdheḥ pratyakṣe 'ntarbhāvaḥ--)
children.translated_text: (10. Subsumption of non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) under perception:)

children.text:
abhāvaḥ pratyakṣaḥ, prameyatvād, ghaṭavat /
na cendriyārthasambandhābhāvo bādhakaḥ, asambaddhasyāpi pratyakṣatve ko doṣaḥ? atiprasaṅga iti cet, tatparihārikā dṛśyānupalabdhirbhaviṣyati /
na ca tāvanmātrasya kāraṇatvamastīti vācyam, andhasyāpi śuklapaṭe pītatvābhāvapratītiprasaṅgāt /
na hi pratiyogī yenaivendriyeṇa gṛhyate, tenaivāśrayo grahītavyaḥ vyomni sparśābhāvagrahaṇaprasaṅgāt /
smaryamāṇe 'pi devakule devadattābhāvasaṃvido 'bhyupagamāt /
vistarastu nyāyalakṣmīvilāse ityuparamyate /
children.translated_text:
Absence is perceptible, because it is knowable (<s>prameya</s>), like a pot.
If one objects that the absence of sense-object contact is a defeater — what fault is there if even what is unconnected is perceptible? If [one says] 'over-extension' — the apprehension of the visible-but-unapprehended (<s>dṛśyānupalabdhi</s>) will serve as the remedy.
Nor should it be said that merely that much is not sufficient as a cause, because there would be the unwanted consequence that even a blind person would have the cognition of the absence of yellowness in a white cloth.
For it is not the case that the counter-positive must be grasped by the very sense organ by which the substratum is grasped — because there would be the unwanted consequence of grasping the absence of touch in space.

children.text: (13--14 sukhaduḥkhayornirūpaṇam--)
children.translated_text: (13-14. Examination of pleasure and pain (<s>sukha</s> and <s>duḥkha</s>):)

children.text:
pratyakṣeṇa sukhamupalabhyate, ahaṃ sukhīti vyavahāradarśanāt /
na ca duḥkhābhāva eva sukham, satyapi duḥkhe tadvyavahāradarśanāt --- santāpavataḥ śītahrade nimagnārdhakāyasya sukhyahamiti mateḥ /
katipayaduḥkhābhāvaśca nārakīyasyāpyasti /
na ca tannityam, kāraṇaviśeṣopādānavaiyarthyaṃ syāt /
jñāyamānaṃ nirupādhikṛtivyāpyaṃ sukham /
evaṃ duḥkhamiti vaktavyam --- nirupādhikaheyaṃ duḥkham /
children.translated_text:
Pleasure is apprehended by perception, because of observing the usage 'I am happy.'
Nor is pleasure merely the absence of pain, because even when pain is present, that usage [of happiness] is observed — [as in the case of] one afflicted by heat whose lower body is immersed in a cold lake thinking 'I am happy.'
Even a hell-being has the absence of some pains.
Nor is that [pleasure] eternal, because the adoption of special causes would be purposeless.
Pleasure is that which, when cognized, is pervaded by unconditional desirability (<s>kṛti</s>).
Pain should be stated similarly — pain is that which is unconditionally to be avoided.

children.text: (15--17 icchādveṣaprayatnānāṃ nirūpaṇam--)
children.translated_text: (15-17. Examination of desire, aversion, and effort (<s>icchā</s>, <s>dveṣa</s>, <s>prayatna</s>):)

children.text:
karma prayatnasādhanaguṇajanyam, karmatvādvyatirekeṇa ghaṭavat /
karmakāraṇamapi vipratipanno guṇo jñānajanyaḥ, karmakāraṇaguṇatvāt /
tattatkāraṇasya sukhaduḥkhajñānasya vaijātyātkāryasya vaijātyamiti icchādveṣaprayatnasiddhiḥ /
tatrecchāprayatnāvapi nityāvanityau ca buddhivat /
karmakāraṇaguṇanimittasukhajñānajanyena guṇatvāvāntarajātīyecchā /
karmakāraṇaguṇanimittaduḥkhajñānajanyena guṇatvāvāntarajātīyo dveṣaḥ /
asmadādipratyakṣaceṣṭānimittena guṇatvāvāntarajātīyaḥ prayatnaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Action is produced by a quality that is the means of effort (<s>prayatnasādhana</s>), because it is an action, by negative concomitance, like a pot.
The disputed quality that causes action is produced by cognition, because it is a quality that causes action.
From the heterogeneity of the [respective] causes — the cognitions of pleasure and pain — there is heterogeneity of the effect, and thus desire, aversion, and effort are established.
Therein, desire and effort too are eternal and non-eternal, like cognition.
Desire belongs to the sub-universal of the quality-type that is produced by the cognition of pleasure occasioned by the quality that causes action.
Aversion belongs to the sub-universal of the quality-type that is produced by the cognition of pain occasioned by the quality that causes action.

children.text: (18-20 gurutvadratvasnehānāṃ nirūpaṇam--)
children.translated_text: (18-20. Examination of heaviness, fluidity, and viscosity (<s>gurutva</s>, <s>dravatva</s>, <s>sneha</s>):)

children.text:
(1 gurutvam--) vivādapadamasamavāyikāraṇajanyam, karmatvāt, sampratipannavat vipratipannamasmadādyapratyakṣam, gurutvād, vyatirekeṇa ghaṭavat /
ādyapatanāsamavāyikāraṇena guṇatvāvāntarajātīyaṃ gurutvam /
children.translated_text:
(1. Heaviness:) The subject of dispute is produced by a non-inherent cause, because it is an action, like the acknowledged [actions].
The subject under dispute is imperceptible to us, because of being heaviness, by negative concomitance, like a pot.
Heaviness belongs to the sub-universal of the quality-type — a quality whose non-inherent cause is the first falling.

children.text:
(2 dravatvam--) syandanamasamavāyikāraṇajanyam, kāryatvād, ghaṭavaditi dravatvasiddhiḥ /
pratyakṣeṇa ca /
ādyasyandanāsamavāyikāraṇena guṇatvāvāntarajātīyaṃ dravatvam /
taijasāḥ paramāṇavo dravatvādhārāḥ, rūpiparamāṇutvāt pārthivaparamāṇuvat /
na ca gurutvarasavattve upādhī, ghaṭe sādhyābhāvāt /
na ca paramāṇutvaviśiṣṭametadupādhiḥ, ghṛtādau sādhyasiddhatve 'pyabhāvātsādhyāvyāpakatvam /
children.translated_text:
(2. Fluidity —) Flowing is produced by a non-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>), because it is an effect, like a pot — thus fluidity (<s>dravatva</s>) is established.
And [it is established] by perception as well.
Fluidity, belonging to the sub-universal of quality-hood, is [produced] by the non-inherent cause of the initial flowing.
Fire-atoms (<s>taijasa paramāṇu</s>) are the substrata of fluidity, because they are atoms with form, like earth-atoms.
Nor are heaviness (<s>gurutva</s>) and possessing taste (<s>rasavatva</s>) limiting conditions, because the probandum is absent in a pot.
Nor is this qualified by atomhood a limiting condition, since even when the probandum is established in ghee and the like, its absence [in the counter-example shows] it does not pervade the probandum.

children.text:
(3 snehaḥ--) udakaṃ guṇatvāvāntarajātyā svāśrayavyāvarttakaguṇāśrayaḥ, rasavatvāt, pṛthivīvat /
na ca pṛthivītvamupādhiḥ, sapakṣāvyāpakatvāt /
tadevaṃ sthite pratyakṣeṇāpi snehaḥ siddhaḥ /
cakṣuḥsparśanagrāhyatve sati guṇatvāvāntarajātyā svāśrayavyavartakaḥ snehaḥ /
children.translated_text:
(3. Viscosity —) Water is a substratum of a quality that differentiates its own substrate through a sub-universal of quality-hood, because it possesses taste, like earth.
Nor is earth-hood a limiting condition, because it does not pervade the positive instances.
Thus being established, viscosity (<s>sneha</s>) is also established by perception.
Viscosity, which differentiates its own substrate through a sub-universal of quality-hood while being apprehensible by both eye and touch, [is thus established].

children.text: (21 saṃskārasya nirūpaṇam--)
children.translated_text: (21. Examination of <s>saṃskāra</s> [latent impression] —)

children.text:
(1 vegaḥ--) vimatipadamadviṣṭhakarmāsamavāyikāraṇāśrayaḥ paramāṇutvāt, pārthivaparamāṇuvat /
na ca rūpitvamupādhiḥ, āloke vyabhicārāt /
na ca rūpyaṇutvaṃ prayojakam, sapakṣāvyāpakatvāt /
prativaddhadravatvasya taijasadvyaṇukasyāpyutpattisambhavāt, tannivṛtyarthaṃ paramāṇutve satīti viśeṣaṇe vaiyarthyam /
sa ca vegaḥ pratyakṣe dravye pratyakṣeṇaiva gṛhyate, vegena gacchatīti pratīteḥ /
children.translated_text:
(1. Velocity —) The subject of dispute is a substratum of a non-inherent cause in a bi-atomic [substance] that is not a <s>karma</s>, because of being an atom, like an earth-atom.
Nor is having form (<s>rūpitva</s>) a limiting condition, because of deviation in [the case of] light.
Nor is 'having-form-and-being-atomic' the operative factor, because it does not pervade the positive instances.
Since even a fire-dyad possessing constrained fluidity can possibly arise, to prevent that [from being included], the qualifier 'in atomhood' would be purposeless.
And that velocity (<s>vega</s>) is apprehended by perception itself in a perceptible substance, since the cognition 'it moves with velocity' is experienced.

children.text:
(2 sthitisthāpakaḥ--) vivādādhyāsitāḥ paramāṇavaḥ [karmāsamavāyikāraṇādviṣṭhaguṇā]dhārāḥ, sparśavattvādaśrautrānityaviśeṣaguṇattvādiṣuvadātmavacca /
anyathākṛṣṭamuktānāṃ śākhādīnāṃ punarmaṇḍalībhāvo na syāt /
vivādādhyāsito vegātiriktasaṃskārāśrayaḥ, aśrautrānityaviśeṣaguṇavattvād, ātmavaditi sthitisthāpakasiddhiḥ /
unnamanakarmāsamavāyikāraṇādviṣṭhaguṇāvāntarajātīyaḥ saṃskāraḥ sthitisthāpakaḥ /
children.translated_text:
(2. Elasticity —) The atoms under dispute are substrata of a quality in a bi-atomic [substance] that is a non-inherent cause other than <s>karma</s>, because they possess tangibility, because they are non-auditory, non-eternal specific qualities, and so forth — like the self.
Otherwise, the re-curving of branches and the like that have been pulled and released would not occur.
The subject of dispute is a substratum of a <s>saṃskāra</s> beyond velocity, because of possessing non-auditory, non-eternal specific qualities, like the self — thus elasticity (<s>sthitisthāpaka</s>) is established.
Elasticity is a <s>saṃskāra</s> belonging to the sub-universal of qualities in a bi-atomic [substance] that is a non-inherent cause of upward <s>karma</s>.

children.text:
(3 bhāvanā--) smṛttyanyathānupapattyā bhāvanāsiddhiḥ /
pūrvānubhavasya cirātītatvāt /
svotpādakānityajñānasamānaviṣayajñānajanakena guṇāvāntarajātīyā bhāvanā /
children.translated_text:
(3. Dispositional tendency —) <s>Bhāvanā</s> (dispositional tendency) is established through the impossibility of otherwise explaining memory.
Because the prior experience has long passed.
<s>Bhāvanā</s>, belonging to the sub-universal of quality-hood, is that which produces a cognition having the same object as the non-eternal cognition that generated it.

children.text: (22--23 dharmādharmayornirūpaṇam)
children.translated_text: (22-23. Examination of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> —)

children.text:
(1 dharmaḥ--) yāgaḥ svargotpādanasamarthāvāntaravyāpārakaḥ, anyathā yāgasvargayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvasya pratītasyānirvāhāt /
pratīyate ca kāmanāviṣayatvena sādhyatvaṃ svargasya, vidhibalādyāgasya sādhanatvenānuṣṭheyatvam /
na ca vācyaṃ sādhyasādhanabhāvaḥ kṣaṇikasya yāgasya kālāntarabhāvini svarge vināvāntaravyāpāraṃ upapadyate iti madhye 'pūrvasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text:
(1. <s>Dharma</s> —) A sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) operates through an intermediate process (<s>avāntaravyāpāra</s>) capable of producing heaven — otherwise the experienced relation of means and end between sacrifice and heaven could not be maintained.
And it is experienced: heaven's being-the-end is [known] through its being the object of desire, and the sacrifice's being-the-means, to be performed, is [known] through the force of injunction.
Nor should it be said that the means-end relation between the momentary sacrifice and heaven, which exists at a later time, is tenable without an intermediate process — for this [requires] the establishment of <s>apūrva</s> (unseen potency) in between.

children.text:
apare ca yāgasvargayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvo nāpūrvavākyātpratīyate, yogyatāvirahāt /
ato liṅevāpūrvamabhidhatte, vyutpattistu lokavedābhyām /
loke 'pi kriyākārye liṅprayogadarśanāditi bruvate /
tatrānyathākhyātipakṣe yogyatāmantareṇāpi pratipatterabhyupagamāt /
kāmādhikāreṣu phalaṃ prati kāraṇasyaiva satastasya niyogaṃ prati viṣayatvābhyupagamāt /
anyathā nityakāmyavaiṣamyavigamaḥ syāt /
vihitabhāvārthajātyāsmadādyatīndriyātmaguṇo dharmaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Others say that the means-end relation between sacrifice and heaven is not cognized from the <s>apūrva</s> statement, due to the absence of fitness.
Therefore the optative mood alone denotes <s>apūrva</s>, while etymological derivation [of the word] is from both worldly usage and the Vedas.
Because even in worldly usage the optative is seen employed for the result of an action — so they say.
Therein, on the <s>anyathākhyāti</s> (misapprehension) view, cognition is accepted even without fitness.
In injunctions involving desire, since an existing cause with respect to the result is accepted as the subject matter of the injunction —
otherwise the asymmetry between permanent and desiderative [injunctions] would be eliminated.
<s>Dharma</s> is a quality of the self, supersensory to us and others, belonging to the universal of what is enjoined and what exists.

children.text:
(3 adharmaḥ--) yo brāhmaṇāyāvagurettaṃ śatena yātayāt' (tai saṃ 2.6.10.2) iti śatayātanāyāḥ sādhyatvāvagamāt /
avagūrṇasya cirātītatve tatsādhanatvaṃ sākṣādanupapannamityantarāpūrveṇa bhavitavyam /
adharmatvayogādadharmaḥ /
children.translated_text:
(3. <s>Adharma</s> —) From the passage 'whoever would revile a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, let him be beaten with a hundred [strokes]' (<s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.6.10.2), the end-status of the hundred beatings is understood.
When the reviling has long since passed, its being-the-means cannot be direct, so there must be an intervening <s>apūrva</s>.
Due to its connection with demerit-hood, it is <s>adharma</s>.

children.text: (24 śabdasya nirūpaṇam--)
children.translated_text: (24. Examination of sound —)

children.text:
1 śabdo guṇaḥ, bāhyendriyāṇāṃ madhye avayavyagrāhakeṇaiva gṛhyamāṇāyā jāteradhikaraṇatvādgandhavat /
yadi śabdo dravyaṃ syāt, kenacidviśeṣaguṇena bhavitavyam, anyathā pratyakṣatvānupapatteḥ, viśeṣaguṇapratyakṣatānibandhanatvāddravyapratyakṣatāyāḥ /
children.translated_text:
1. Sound is a quality, because it is the substrate of a universal (<s>jāti</s>) apprehended by that very [sense faculty] among the external sense faculties which grasps composites, like odor.
If sound were a substance, it would need to possess some specific quality; otherwise its perceptibility would be untenable, since the perceptibility of a substance depends on the perceptibility of its specific qualities.

children.text:
2 śabdo dravyaṃ sākṣādindriyasambandhena gṛhyamāṇatvādghaṭavaditi cet, na, vyarthaviśeṣaṇatvāt /
na hi bhedābhedavādināṃ rūpādibhirvyavahitaḥ sambandho 'sti /
atha svasambaddhendriyeṇa gṛhyamāṇatvāditi, tathāpi vaiyarthyamindriyapadasya /
svapadasya grāhyapadasya na vyāvartanamasti adravyasya bhavatāṃ naye sambandhānabhyupagamāt, saṃyogasambandhayoḥ paryāyatvāt, anyatropacaritatvāt /
anyathā yogyatāsambandhalakṣaṇena rūpasyāpi sākṣātsambandhenāvedyatvena vyabhicāraḥ /
sambandhitvāditi prativādyanaikāntikam /
children.translated_text:
2. If [one argues:] 'sound is a substance because it is apprehended through direct sense-contact, like a pot' — no, because the qualifier is purposeless.
For those who hold the identity-in-difference doctrine (<s>bhedābhedavādin</s>), there is no relation mediated by form and the like.
If [one argues:] 'because it is apprehended by a sense faculty connected with it' — even so, the word 'sense faculty' would be purposeless.
The words 'own' and 'apprehensible' do not exclude [anything], since in your system there is no acceptance of a relation for non-substances — because conjunction and relation are synonymous, and [the term is used only] metaphorically elsewhere.
Otherwise, there would be deviation, since form too would be not apprehensible through direct relation via the relation-of-fitness.
And 'because of being a relatum' is inconclusive for the opponent.

children.text:
3 śabdo guṇo na bhavati, śrāvaṇatvāt, śabdatvavaditi cet, na, adravyatvena hyasya samānatvāt /
anaikāntikaśca śabdagatasaṃkhyāyāṃ bhavataḥ /
4 śabdo guṇaḥ, ātmavyatiriktatve sati indriyāṇāṃ madhye nityenaivādhyakṣīkṛtāyā jāteradhikaraṇatvātsukhavat /
anityaḥ śabdaḥ, indriyaviśeṣaguṇatvāccakṣurgatarūpavat /
na cākāśa eva vartamānatvāt, tanmahatvavaditi satpratipakṣatvam, ākāśabhāgavinaṣṭaghaṭa iva svasaṃyoge vyabhicārāt /
anitya śabdaḥ arasatve satyavayavyagrāhakeṇaiva gṛhyamāṇajāteradhikaraṇatvādgandhavaditi bhāṭṭaṃ prati /
yacca nityaḥ śabda, ātmaviśeṣaguṇānyatve sati indriyāṇāṃ madhye nityenaiva gṛhyamāṇatvāditi, [tad] duḥkhābhāve 'naikāntikam /
sāmānyavattve satīti viśeṣaṇe 'pi tathā, paramate tatrāpi jāterabhyupagamāt /
yadāha-
children.translated_text:
3. If [one argues:] 'sound is not a quality, because it is auditory, like sound-hood' — no, since it [sound-hood] is similar [to sound] in being a non-substance.
And [the reason] is inconclusive with respect to the number belonging to sound, according to you.
4. Sound is a quality, because when different from the self, among the sense faculties, it is the substrate of a universal that is always apprehended by an eternal [faculty], like pleasure.
Sound is non-eternal, because it is a specific quality of a sense faculty, like the color belonging to the eye.
Nor is the counter-argument valid that 'because it exists in space itself, it is like the magnitude of space' — because of deviation in its own conjunction, like a pot that has been destroyed in a portion of space.
Sound is non-eternal — because, when devoid of taste, it is the substrate of a universal apprehended by that very [sense faculty] which grasps composites among the external sense faculties, like odor — this [is directed] against the <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> [school].
As for [the argument:] 'sound is eternal, because when different from specific qualities of the self, among the sense faculties it is always apprehended by an eternal [faculty]' — that is inconclusive regarding the absence of suffering.
Even with the qualifier 'when possessing a universal,' the same [applies], because even according to the opponent's view, universal is accepted there too.
As it is said —

children.text: yadvānuvṛttivyāvṛttibuddhigrāhyo yatastvayam /
children.translated_text: That which is apprehended by the cognitions grasping inclusion and exclusion by you —

children.text: tasmādgavādibaddhastu prameyatvācca gamyatām //
children.translated_text: therefore, being bound to [universals like] cow-hood and the like, let it be understood from its being knowable.

children.text: (ślo vā abhāva 9) iti
children.translated_text: (<s>Ślokavārttika</s>, <s>Abhāva</s> 9) — thus.

children.text:
prativādyanaikāntikaṃ ca, ākāśavāyusaṃyogasyāpi yogyatākaraṇagrāhyasya tathābhāvāt /
asmadādīti viśeṣaṇe vaiyarthyāt, nādaiśca vyabhicārāt /
evaṃ vyavasthite pratyakṣeṇāpi sādhyate naṣṭaḥ śabda iti pratīteḥ /
ākāśaviśeṣaguṇaḥ śabdaḥ /
yadaparajātīyena vinā samavāyikāraṇatvābhāvaḥ, sa guṇaḥ /
kevalanimittakāraṇe ca vartamānāparajātīyatvaṃ vā /
samavāyyasamavāyikāraṇarahite 'pi vartamānāparajātīyatvaṃ vā /
children.translated_text:
And it is inconclusive for the opponent, since the conjunction of space and air, which is apprehensible through the [relation of] fitness, is also of that nature.
With the qualifier 'for us and others,' there is purposelessness, and deviation with respect to river-sounds.
Thus being established, [the non-eternality of sound] is also established by perception, since there is the experience 'the sound has perished.'
Sound is a specific quality of space (<s>ākāśa</s>).
That which does not have the status of inherent cause without [something of] another universal — that is a quality.
Or, having the nature of another universal that exists in a mere efficient cause.
Or, having the nature of another universal that exists even without an inherent and non-inherent cause.

children.text: karmapadārthaprakaraṇam
children.translated_text: Chapter on the category of <s>karma</s> (motion)

children.text:
1) ādyasaṃyogāvibhāgāvasamavāyikāraṇajau, kāryatvād, ghaṭavaditi karmasiddhiḥ /
tacca pratyakṣam, prameyatvād, ghaṭavat /
vimatipadamindriyasaṃyogavyatiriktaṃ saṃyogāsamavāyikāraṇagrāhakam, dravyagrāhakendriyatvāt, manovat /
karma, apratyakṣam, karmatvāditi dṛṣṭāntāsiddhiḥ /
ayogīti viśeṣaṇena vyāptyasiddhiḥ, yogyanabhyupagamāt /
tatkāraṇādeva saṃyogavibhāgasiddhiḥ /
karmāsiddhiprasaṅgaśca /
children.translated_text:
1) The initial conjunction and non-disjunction are produced by a non-inherent cause, because they are effects, like a pot — thus <s>karma</s> (motion) is established.
And that is perceptual, because it is knowable, like a pot.
The subject of dispute apprehends the non-inherent cause of conjunction other than sense-contact, because it is a sense faculty that apprehends substances, like the mind.
'<s>Karma</s> is imperceptible, because it is <s>karma</s>' — the example is unestablished.
With the qualifier 'non-yogic,' the pervasion is unestablished, because yoga is not accepted [by the opponent].
From that very cause, conjunction and disjunction are established.
And there would be the consequence that <s>karma</s> is unestablished.

children.text:
2) taccānantāparajātīyam, patanotkṣepaṇādipratyayānāṃ tulyatvāt /
ādyavibhāgāsamavāyikāraṇajātīyaṃ karma saṃyogavibhāgayoranapekṣakāraṇatvārhaṃ vā /
etena viśvasmādbhedagrāhibhyo guṇebhyo 'pi bhedasiddhiḥ karmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text:
2) And that [karma] has infinite sub-universals, since the cognitions of falling, throwing upward, and the like are equal [in status].
<s>Karma</s>, belonging to the universal of that which is produced by the non-inherent cause of initial disjunction, is worthy of being the cause independent of conjunction and disjunction.
With this, the distinction of <s>karma</s> from qualities too — which grasp difference from everything — is established.

children.text: sāmānyapadārthaprakaraṇam
children.translated_text: Chapter on the category of <s>sāmānya</s> (universal)

children.text:
yadyapyekākārapratyayasya bhinneṣvekanimittamantareṇānupapadyamānatvena sāmānyasiddhiriti na yuktam, tathāvidhadarśane 'pi vipratipatteḥ /
sati kalpakasya prāmāṇye 'vivādāttatsādhitamiti na yuktam, tadvādhitamityasyāpi vaktuṃ śakyatvāt /
tathāpi ---
kāraṇasya hi siddhatvādvikalpasyāpi bhedataḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the cause is established, and since the conceptual cognition is also distinct,

children.text: vyāvṛtterapi bhinnatvādanyonyāśrayadūṣaṇāt //
children.translated_text: and since exclusion too is different, [this avoids] the fault of mutual dependence.

children.text: tasmādasti jātiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the universal (<s>jāti</s>) exists.

children.text:
(1 sattā--) vivādapadaṃ dravyaṃ samānajātīyasamavāyikāraṇam, samavāyikāraṇatvāt, mṛdvat /
na ca sparśavattvamupādhiḥ, antyāvayavini tava vyabhicārāt /
asmākaṃ tu vyāptikāle sattāpratipattau cānyatrāpi siddhiḥ, vyāptivighaṭakatvena vyāptikāle evāsya dūṣaṇatvāt /
vyāptyuttarakālabhāvitatvāt pakṣādivyavasthāyāḥ /
vihāya sattāmantyāvayaviṣu sādhyābhāve 'pyupādherbhāvāt /

(2 dravyatvam--) vivādādhyāsitaṃ rūpavṛttisparśavajjātimat, samavāyikāraṇatvād ghaṭavat --- atra vipratipattiviṣayasyaiva tathāvidhatvānna sādhye viśeṣaṇopādānād dūṣaṇam, anyathā udghāṭitamātrameva sādhanīyam /
children.translated_text: (2 <s>Dravyatva</s> (Substancehood)--) The subject under dispute possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that resides in what possesses <s>rūpa</s> (color), is present in touch, because it possesses <s>samavāyikāraṇatva</s> (the nature of being an inherent cause), like a pot --- Here, since the very object of dispute is of such a nature, there is no fault in introducing a qualifier in the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum); otherwise, only what is already exposed would need to be proved.

children.text: (3 pṛthivītvam--) vivādādhyāsitamudakāvṛttijātimad, gandhatvādghaṭavat /
children.translated_text: (3 <s>Pṛthivītva</s> (Earthness)--) The subject under dispute possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in water, because of possessing <s>gandhatva</s> (the quality of smell), like a pot.

children.text: (4 jalatvam--) vivādādhyāsitaṃ pṛthivyavṛttijātimad, gurutvādghaṭavat /
children.translated_text: (4 <s>Jalatva</s> (Waterness)--) The subject under dispute possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in earth, because of possessing <s>gurutva</s> (heaviness), like a pot.

children.text:
(5 tejastvam--) vivādādhyāsitamanuṣṇāvṛttijātimad, uṣṇatvāddīpavat /
vāyvavṛttitvasādhane rūpitvāditi vācyam /
children.translated_text:
(5 <s>Tejastva</s> (Fireness)--) The subject under dispute possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in what is not hot, because of possessing <s>uṣṇatva</s> (heat), like a lamp.
For proving non-occurrence in air, it should be stated: because of possessing <s>rūpitva</s> (visibility).

children.text: (6 vāyutvaṃ--) vivādādhyāsitamākāśāvṛttijātimat, sparśatvādghaṭavaditi /
children.translated_text: (6 <s>Vāyutva</s> (Airness)--) The subject under dispute possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in <s>ākāśa</s> (space), because of possessing <s>sparśatva</s> (tangibility), like a pot.

children.text: (7 ātmatvam--) vipratipannamākāśāvṛttijātivad, aśrautraviśeṣaguṇādhāratvādghaṭavat /
children.translated_text: (7 <s>Ātmatva</s> (Selfhood)--) The disputed entity possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in <s>ākāśa</s> (space), because of being the substratum of non-auditory particular qualities (<s>aśrautraviśeṣaguṇa</s>), like a pot.

children.text: (8 manastvam--) vivādapadamātmāvṛttijātimad, mūrtatvādghaṭavat /
children.translated_text: (8 <s>Manastva</s> (Mind-ness)--) The subject under dispute possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in <s>ātman</s> (self), because of possessing <s>mūrtatva</s> (corporeality), like a pot.

children.text: (9 dravyatvādeḥ pratyakṣatvam--) vivādapadaṃ karmāvṛtticākṣuṣajātigrāhakam, indriyatvānmanovat /
children.translated_text: (9 Perceptibility of <s>dravyatva</s> (substancehood) and the like--) The subject under dispute is a grasper of a visual <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in <s>karman</s> (action), because of possessing <s>indriyatva</s> (the nature of being a sense organ), like the mind.

children.text: (10 rūpatvam--) asamavāyikāraṇaṃ pītamapītavṛttigandhāvṛttimat, kevalanimittakāraṇavyatiriktakāraṇatve sati gandhānyatvādghaṭavat /
children.translated_text: (10 <s>Rūpatva</s> (Colorness)--) The <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s> (non-inherent cause), namely yellow color, possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that occurs in non-yellow things but does not occur in smell, because of being different from smell while being a cause other than a mere efficient cause (<s>kevalanimittakāraṇa</s>), like a pot.

children.text:
(11 rūpatvasya pratyakṣatvam--) vipratipannaṃ sparśanendriyāgrāhyajātigrāhakam, sparśanavyatiriktendriyatvānmanovat /
evaṃ rasatvāderapi pratyakṣatvaṃ vācyam /
children.translated_text:
(11 Perceptibility of <s>rūpatva</s> (colorness)--) The disputed entity is a grasper of a <s>jāti</s> (universal) not graspable by the tactile sense organ, because of being a sense organ other than the tactile sense, like the mind.
Similarly, the perceptibility of <s>rasatva</s> (tasteness) and others should also be stated.

children.text:
(12 nīlatvam--) nīlamanīlarūpāvṛttijātimat, kevalanimittakāraṇavyatiriktakāraṇatve satyanīlavyatiriktatvādghaṭavat /
evaṃ pītatvādiṣvapi vācyam /
children.translated_text:
(12 <s>Nīlatva</s> (Blueness)--) Blue color possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in non-blue colors, because of being different from non-blue while being a cause other than a mere efficient cause (<s>kevalanimittakāraṇa</s>), like a pot.
Similarly, this should also be stated for <s>pītatva</s> (yellowness) and others.

children.text: (13 rasatvam--) rasaḥ saṃyogāvṛttijātimān, kevalanimittakāraṇavyatiriktakāraṇatve sati saṃyogānyatvādghaṭavat /
children.translated_text: (13 <s>Rasatva</s> (Tasteness)--) Taste possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), because of being different from conjunction while being a cause other than a mere efficient cause, like a pot.

children.text:
(14 madhuratvam--) madhuro 'madhurarasāvṛttijātimān, kevalanimittakāraṇavyatiriktakāraṇatve satyamadhurarasavyatiriktatvādghaṭavat /
evaṃ tiktatvādiṣvapi vācyam /
children.translated_text: (14 <s>Madhuratva</s> (Sweetness)--) Sweet taste possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in non-sweet tastes, because of being different from non-sweet while being a cause other than a mere efficient cause, like a pot.

children.text: (15 gandhatvam--) gandho rūpāvṛttijātimān, kevalanimittakāraṇatve sati rūpānyatvādghaṭavat /
children.translated_text: (15 <s>Gandhatva</s> (Smellness)--) Smell possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in <s>rūpa</s> (color), because of being different from color while being a mere efficient cause (<s>kevalanimittakāraṇa</s>), like a pot.

children.text: (16 surabhitvam--) surabhirasurabhigandhāvṛttijātimān, kevalanimittakāraṇavyatiriktakāraṇatve satyasurabhigandhānyatvād, ghaṭavat /
children.translated_text: (16 <s>Surabhitva</s> (Fragrancy)--) A fragrant smell possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in non-fragrant smells, because of being different from non-fragrant smell while being a cause other than a mere efficient cause, like a pot.

children.text: (17 sparśatvam--) sparśo rasāvṛttijātimān, kevalanimittakāraṇavyatiriktakāraṇatve sati rasānyatvādghaṭavat /
children.translated_text: (17 <s>Sparśatva</s> (Touchness)--) Touch possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in taste, because of being different from taste while being a cause other than a mere efficient cause, like a pot.

children.text:
(18 śītatvam--) śīto 'śītasparśāvṛttijātimān, kevalanimittakāraṇavyatiriktakāraṇatve satyasparśānyatvādghaṭavat /
evamaśītatvādiṣvapi vācyam /
children.translated_text: (18 <s>Śītatva</s> (Coldness)--) Cold touch possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in non-cold touches, because of being different from non-cold touch while being a cause other than a mere efficient cause, like a pot.

children.text:
(19 saṃkhyātvam--) saṃkhyā parimāṇāvṛttijātimatī, kevalanimittakāraṇavyatiriktakāraṇatve sati parimāṇānyatvād, ghaṭavat /
evaṃ dvitvādiṣvapi vācyam /
children.translated_text: (19 <s>Saṃkhyātva</s> (Numberness)--) Number possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in <s>parimāṇa</s> (magnitude), because of being different from magnitude while being a cause other than a mere efficient cause, like a pot.

children.text: (20 parimāṇatvam--) asamavāyikāraṇaṃ mahattvaṃ saṃkhyāvṛttimahattvānyaparimāṇavṛttijātimat, kevalanimittakāraṇavyatiriktakāraṇatve sati saṃkhyāvyatiriktatvāt, tadvat /
children.translated_text: (20 <s>Parimāṇatva</s> (Magnitudeness)--) The <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s> (non-inherent cause), namely largeness (<s>mahattva</s>), possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that occurs in magnitudes other than largeness and number but does not occur in number or in magnitudes other than largeness, because of being different from number and magnitudes other than largeness while being a cause other than a mere efficient cause, like a pot.

children.text:
(21 pṛthaktvam--) asamavāyikāraṇaṃ pṛthaktvaṃ parimāṇavṛttyekapṛthaktvavyatiriktavṛttijātimat, parimāṇavyatiriktatve sati kevalanimittakāraṇavyatiriktakāraṇatvāttadvat /
evaṃ caikapṛthaktvādiṣvapi vācyam /
na ca tatra sāmānyabhāvaḥ, ekapṛthaktvadvipṛthaktvaśabdānāmanyathopapattāvapi niyāmakāparajātimantareṇa dvipṛthaktvotpattāvekapṛthaktvasya hetutvānirṇayāt /
anvayavyatirekavyavasthāpakābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: (21 <s>Pṛthaktva</s> (Separateness)--) The <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s> (non-inherent cause), namely separateness, possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that occurs in things other than magnitude and unit-separateness but does not occur in magnitude or unit-separateness, because of being different from magnitude and unit-separateness, like a pot.

children.text: (22 saṃyogatvam--) vipratipannamasamavāyikāraṇaṃ pṛthaktvāvṛttijātimat kevalanimittakāraṇavyatiriktakāraṇatve sati pṛthaktvānyatvāttadvat /
children.translated_text: (22 <s>Saṃyogatva</s> (Conjunctionness)--) The disputed <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s> (non-inherent cause) possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in separateness, because of being different from separateness while being a cause other than a mere efficient cause, like a pot.

children.text: (23 vibhāgatvam--) vibhāgaḥ saṃyogāvṛttijātimān, saṃyogavyatiriktatve sati dvayāsamavāyikāraṇatvād dvitantukavat /
children.translated_text: (23 <s>Vibhāgatva</s> (Disjunctionness)--) Disjunction possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in conjunction, because of being different from conjunction and being a <s>dvayāsamavāyikāraṇa</s> (non-inherent cause of a dyad), like a dyad (<s>dvyaṇuka</s>).

children.text:
(24 paratvam--) paratvaṃ vibhāgāvṛttijātimat, saṃyogāsamavāyikāraṇatvāt /
aparatvabuddhitvādiṣvapyevaṃ vācyam /
gurutvadravatvasnehasaṃskāreṣvapi prācīnamanumānaṃ vācyam /
children.translated_text:
(24 <s>Paratva</s> (Priority/Remoteness)--) Priority possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in disjunction, because of possessing <s>saṃyogāsamavāyikāraṇatva</s> (the nature of being a non-inherent cause of conjunction).
Similarly, this should be stated for <s>aparatva</s> (posteriority), <s>buddhi</s> (cognition), and others as well.

children.text: (25 brāhmaṇatvasya pratyakṣatvam--) vivādādhyāsitaṃ brāhmaṇavyatiriktavarṇāvṛttijātigrāhakam, indriyatvāt, cakṣurvat /
children.translated_text:
(25 Perceptibility of <s>brāhmaṇatva</s> (Brahminhood)--) The subject under dispute is a grasper of a <s>jāti</s> (universal) that does not occur in <s>varṇas</s> (castes) other than Brahmins, because of possessing <s>indriyatva</s> (the nature of being a sense organ), like the visual perception that grasps the <s>jāti</s> (universal) of color inhering in a pot.
Similarly, this should also be stated for <s>kṣatriyatva</s> (Kshatriyahood) and others.

children.text:
(26 brāhmaṇatvam--) brāhmaṇo 'brāhmamanuṣyānādhārajātyādhāraḥ, abrāhmaṇamanuṣyavyatiriktatve satyavayavitvād, govat /
vivādādhyāsitaḥ śarīrasantāno 'yonijaḥ, śarīrasantānatvād, gomayajavṛścikaśarīrasantānavadityanumānenābrāhmaṇapūrvake kvacid brāhmaṇaśabde prāpte na brāhmaṇajanyaśarīranibandhano brāhmaṇaśabdaḥ /
evaṃ śūdratvādiṣvapyaupādhikanirākaraṇaṃ vācyam /
children.translated_text:
(26 <s>Brāhmaṇatva</s> (Brahminhood)--) A Brahmin is the substratum of a <s>jāti</s> (universal) whose substratum is not a non-Brahmin human, because of being different from non-Brahmin humans and possessing <s>avayavatva</s> (the nature of having parts), like a pot.
Similarly, this should also be stated for <s>kṣatriyatva</s> (Kshatriyahood) and others.

children.text:
(27 karmatvam--) utkṣepaṇaṃ guṇānāśrayākṣepaṇatvavyatiriktajātimat, kevalanimittakāraṇavyatiriktakāraṇatve satyaguṇatvādghaṭavat /
nanvatra karmamātrapakṣīkāre vāyvādiṣu vyabhicāraḥ, avipratipannānāmapi pakṣīkāre karmatvāsiddhiḥ, kintvanyadeva karmavāyvoranugataṃ sāmānyaṃ syāt /
naivam, na hyatra paramamīṣāmekajātīyatvaṃ sādhyate, kintu guṇānāśrayotkṣepaṇatvavyatiriktajātimātram /
yā caikānekatātītijyāmānāṃtanirṇayathā(?) /
tatrākāśavṛttijātimatvāditi sādhanairatiriktajātiprasaktau tadviṣayatvenāpyasya nirvāhāt, na vāyvādiṣvatiriktānugame pramāṇamasti /
karmaṇi tvanena sādhyamānaṃ na karmatvādatiricyate /
guṇāvṛttitve sati sakalakarmavṛttyutkṣepaṇatvavyatiriktatvasya vā tattvāt /
tathāvidhasyātra pratīteḥ kevalakarmatvasādhanasyātra vāyvādāvanaikāntikatvaparihārārthaṃ vipratipannapadopādānam /
vāyvādigataṃ mānāntaropanītaṃ bhedamavagāhate 'to na karmatvāsiddhiḥ /
parantu vāyvādau praśnaḥ syāt /
kathakānāṃ kathāntarahetvantarāṇyapyanusandheyāni /
evaṃ rūpatvādiṣvapyanusandheyam /
tasmādabhipretasaṃsiddhau pītāpītādisamavetatve sati gandhāvṛttitvamiti rūpatvamityalam /
nityatve satyanekasamavetaṃ sāmānyam /
children.translated_text: (27 <s>Karmatva</s> (Actionhood)--) Upward movement (<s>utkṣepaṇa</s>) possesses a <s>jāti</s> (universal) distinct from the quality of not being a substratum of qualities and from throwing-ness (<s>ākṣepaṇatva</s>), because of being different from throwing-ness while being a cause other than a mere efficient cause, like a pot.

children.text: viśeṣapadārthaprakaraṇam
children.translated_text: Chapter on the Category of <s>Viśeṣa</s> (Particularity)

children.text:
vivādapadaṃ guṇasāmānyavyatiriktasamavāyi, dravyatvādghaṭavat /
niḥsāmānya ekenaikasamavāyī viśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
The subject under dispute inheres in something different from <s>guṇasāmānya</s> (quality-universal), because of possessing <s>dravyatva</s> (substancehood), like a pot.
<s>Viśeṣa</s> (particularity) is that which is without a universal, singular, and inheres in one thing alone --- the nature of <s>viśeṣa</s> is established thus: because of being eternal while being the substratum of the substratum of mental qualities, like <s>ākāśa</s> (space).

children.text: samavāyasya nirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Examination of <s>Samavāya</s> (Inherence)

children.text:
vivādāspadaṃ ghaṭasambaddham, dravyatvādātmavat /
vivādāspadaṃ nityasaṃbandhena sambaddhaṃ, dravyatvādākāśavat /
ākāśaśabdayośca nityasambandho bhāṭṭairabhyupagamyate, ato na sādhyavikalatā tatra saṃyogasamavāyamātre viprattipattirna dharmiṇi /
children.translated_text:
The subject under dispute is connected with the pot, because of possessing <s>dravyatva</s> (substancehood), like <s>ātman</s> (self).
The subject under dispute is connected by a permanent relation, because of possessing <s>dravyatva</s> (substancehood), like <s>ātman</s> (self).
Being connected by a permanent relation is itself the nature of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) --- that is understood by both disputants.
Since it is understood by both disputants, there is no dispute regarding the particular nature that is arrived at.
A relation is like a means of proof that resides in two things; that in which it resides is the relation.

children.text:
apare tu saṃyogaḥ svavyatiriktasambandhādbhinnaḥ, meyatvāditi bruvate /
kaḥ punaratrānukūlatarkaḥ? [na tāvat] samānādhikaraṇapratītyanupapattiḥ, sā hi na sambandhamātre, nāpyasati sambandhe rajjughaṭayorhimavadvindhyayośca tadabhāvāt /
bhedābhedanibandhanāsāviti cet, asti tāvadbhedaḥ sampratipanno ghaṭarūpayoḥ, abhedaḥ punaḥ kaḥ syāt? bhedābhāvaḥ, tadvirodhastadanyo vā? na tāvat prathamaḥ, virodhāt /
na dvitīyaḥ, āśrayakṛtaḥ svarūpakṛtaḥ kāryakṛto vā virodhaḥ syāt, sarvathā tadvirodhānuvṛtteḥ /
dvitīye tu tadevāstu kimanena prathamena? tṛtīyaḥ, samavāyenānatirekānnāsti tatra vipratipattiḥ /
ghaṭarūpayoritaretarābhāvo nāstīti cet, bhedo 'sti, itaretarābhāvo nāstīti vyāhatam, tayoḥ paryāyatvāt /
svarūpaṃ bhedaścet, tarhi tatpratīteḥ pratiyogisāpekṣatvaṃ durghaṭam /
na ca prathamadvitīyau, ghaṭarūpayorubhayorabhāvaprasaṅgāt /
nāpi caramaḥ, tayorhi kāryaṃ pratipattiḥ syāt, tadvyatiriktaṃ vā kiñcit? tatraiva sthitiritaraprativirodhinī tadatiriktāpekṣiṇī vā? prathame na kadācidapi tayoḥ pratipattiḥ syāt, sarvadā tadvirodhānuvṛtteḥ /
dvitīye tu tāvadevāstu kimanena? tṛtīye savidāṃ janmaiva durghaṭam /
yadyasmādbhinnaśabdavācyam, tattadapekṣayā bhinnam, yathā ghaṭāpekṣayā ghaṭagataṃ rūpamiti /
children.translated_text: Others, however, say: conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) is distinct from a relation different from itself, because it is knowable. What, then, is the supporting reasoning here? Not the impossibility of co-referential cognition (<s>samānādhikaraṇapratīti</s>), for that [impossibility] does not [apply] in the case of a mere relation, nor in the absence of a relation — since it is absent in the case of a rope and a pot, or <s>Himavat</s> and <s>Vindhya</s>. If [one says] 'that [co-referential cognition] is grounded in both difference and non-difference' — well, there is indeed difference acknowledged between a pot and its color; but what would non-difference be? The absence of difference, the opposite of that, or something else? Not the first, because of contradiction. Not the second — [for] the contradiction would be based on the locus, on the essential nature, or on the effect; in every case, the contradiction of that persists. In the second [alternative], let that alone suffice — what need of this first? The third, since it does not differ from <s>samavāya</s> (inherence), there is no disagreement there. If [one objects] 'between a pot and its color, the mutual absence of one from the other does not exist' — [saying] 'difference exists, mutual absence does not exist' is contradictory, since the two are synonymous. If essential nature is difference, then it is difficult to explain why the cognition of that requires a counter-correlate. And not the first or second [alternatives], because of the undesirable consequence that both pot and color would be absent. Nor the last, for the effect of those [two] would be either cognition or something distinct from it. Is the state there contrary to the other, or does it require something beyond that? In the first case, there would never be cognition of those two, since the contradiction always persists. In the second, let just that suffice — what need of this? In the third, for the wise, even birth itself is difficult to explain. If what is expressible by the word 'distinct' is distinct from that with reference to which it is [distinct], then [it is distinct] like color residing in a pot, with reference to the pot.

children.text:
vivādādhyāsitāḥ śabdā ākāśasamavāyenaiva samavāyinaḥ, samavāyitvāt, śabdākāśavat /
na ca samavāyasyaikatve vastusaṅkaraprasaṅgaḥ, tasya samastaviśvāsaṃkaratvenaiva parikalpitatvāt /
na hi tasyāpratyakṣasya pūrvaṃ svabhāvo nirdhāritaḥ /
ekasya bhinnasvabhāvatve 'nya iti cet, na, citrarūpavattathāvidhasyaikasvabhāvāt /
evaṃ ca kalpanālāghavātsamavāyasya niyatvaṃ kvacitpareṇābhyupagamāt /
tasmāttatsamavāyasya nityatvam, ekatvasya sādhitatvāt /
samavāyo 'smadādipratyakṣo na bhavati, asmādādipratyakṣāpratyakṣasambandhatvād, ghaṭākāśasambandhavat /
nityasambandhaḥ samavāyaḥ /
ihapratyayaviṣayībhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sounds that are the subject of dispute inhere in <s>ākāśa</s> (space) precisely through <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) with <s>ākāśa</s>, because they are inherent, like sound and <s>ākāśa</s> [themselves]. And if <s>samavāya</s> is one, there is no undesirable consequence of a confusion of entities, because it is conceived precisely as the non-confusion of the entire universe. For its nature, being imperceptible, was not previously determined. If [one objects] 'if one [thing] has different natures, it would be another' — no, because like a variegated form, such a thing has a single nature. And thus, due to the parsimony of postulation, since the invariability of <s>samavāya</s> is accepted somewhere by the opponent, therefore the eternality of that <s>samavāya</s> [holds], since its oneness has been established. <s>Samavāya</s> (inherence) is not perceptible to us and others, because it is a relation imperceptible to our perception, like the relation between a pot and <s>ākāśa</s>. <s>Samavāya</s> is an eternal relation. Its being the object of the 'here'-cognition [is established].

children.text: abhāvapadārthaprakaraṇam
children.translated_text: Chapter on the Category of Absence (<s>Abhāvapadārthaprakaraṇa</s>)

children.text:
yadi nāstīti pratyayavedyamāno 'pi tvayā neṣṭa iti vaktuṃ nocitam /
kevalajñānaṃ cāsmābhirabhyupagatamiti, tadapi vikalpya dūṣaṇīyam /
patanādikāryaṃ pratibandhakābhāvotpādakakāraṇādevotpādyate kāryatvāddāhādivat /
children.translated_text: It is not fitting for you to say that [absence], even though cognized as 'it is not,' is not accepted by you. And what we accept as mere cognition — that too should be examined and refuted [by you]. Effects such as falling and so forth are produced by the causal complex that includes the absence of an obstruction, because they are effects, like burning and so forth.

children.text:
aghaṭaṃ bhūtalamiti vyavahāro bhūtalātiriktaviṣayaḥ, bhūtalamātravyavahārātiriktatve sati bhūtalavyavahāratvāditi mānaṃ bhūtalamiti vyavahāreṇānaikāntikam /
tathāpyabhāvo 'bhyupagantavyaḥ kevalajñānābhāve 'pyabhāvavyahāradarśanāt /
bhavati hi ghaṭatadrūpayoḥ sahopalambhe 'pi rūpaṃ ghaṭo na bhavatīti bhinnaścotpādavyavahāraḥ, na ca tatra kevalajñānamasti /
ādhārāgrahaṇe 'pi sarveṣāmantarāle ālokābhāvavyavahārāt /
karaparāmarśeṇāndhakāre 'ndhasyāpi mūrtābhāvavyavahāradarśanāt /
kiñca cakṣuścakṣurgrāhyabhāvavyatiriktagrāhakam, indriyatvāt /
children.translated_text: The verbal usage 'the ground without a pot' has an object beyond the ground [alone], because while being distinct from the verbal usage 'merely the ground,' it is a verbal usage about the ground — the reasoning by [the usage] 'the ground' is inconclusive due to non-exclusiveness. Nevertheless, absence (<s>abhāva</s>) must be accepted, because even in the absence of mere cognition, the verbal usage of absence is observed. For indeed, even when the pot and its form are apprehended together, there is the separate usage 'the form is not the pot' — and therein there is no mere cognition. Even without apprehending the substrate, all [persons] use the expression 'absence of light' in the interval [between lights]. From the observation that even a blind person, by touch, uses the expression 'absence of a corporeal [thing]' in darkness. Moreover, the eye apprehends what is other than that which is apprehended by visual [perception] as the absence [of that thing], because it is a sense organ.

children.text:
sa caturvidhaḥ, prāgabhāvapradhvaṃsābhāvānyonyābhāvātyantābhāvabhedāt /
pratiyogibhedādbhinnatvamabhāvasya, tādātmyasaṃsṛṣṭapūrvāparasaṃsṛṣṭānāṃ pratiyogitvāt /
anyathā pratibandhakābhāvasya kāraṇatvaṃ durghaṭam /
atyantābhāvasyāpītaretarābhāve 'ntarbhāvāt /
tasya ca satyapi pratibandhe bhāvādvyabhicāraḥ /
samavāyānyo 'samavāyyabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: That [absence] is fourfold, due to the distinction of prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>), destructive absence (<s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s>), mutual absence (<s>anyonyābhāva</s>), and absolute absence (<s>atyantābhāva</s>). The distinctness of absence is due to the difference of counter-positives, because [entities] conjoined with identity, [entities] conjoined with prior and posterior [temporal] relations serve as counter-positives. Otherwise, the causal status of the absence of an obstruction would be difficult to explain. And absolute absence is included within mutual absence. And even in the case of that [absolute absence], there is deviation from [i.e., it does not hold for] positive entities even when there is obstruction. Absence (<s>abhāva</s>) is a non-inherent [relation] other than <s>samavāya</s> (inherence).

children.text: padārthāntaranirākaraṇam
children.translated_text: Refutation of Additional Categories (<s>Padārthāntaranirākaraṇa</s>)

children.text:
(1 śakteḥ padārthāntaratvanirāsaḥ--) śaktirapi padārthāntaramastīti cet, na, tatsadbhāve pramāṇābhāvāt /
sphoṭānupapattiriti cet, na, pratibandhābhāvenāpyupapatteḥ /
tatra ca prāgabhāvādivikalpāḥ yogyatānupalabdhisāmānyena parihartavyāḥ /
kāryalakṣaṇābhyupagamenottambhakamantrasya sphoṭotpattāvapi nāniyatahetutvam /
children.translated_text: (1. Refutation of <s>śakti</s> (potency) as a separate category) If [one claims] that <s>śakti</s> (potency) is also an additional category — no, because there is no means of knowledge for its existence. If [one argues] 'because <s>sphoṭa</s> is otherwise impossible to explain' — no, because it can be explained even through the absence of an obstruction. And therein, the alternatives of prior absence and so forth should be answered by the general principle of non-observation of the competent (<s>yogyānupalabdhi</s>). Even if one accepts the definition through effects, there is no non-determining causal status in the production of <s>sphoṭa</s> by a sustaining mantra.

children.text:
brīhīn prokṣatīti dvitīyāyāśca na tatsamavetasaṃskāravācakatvaṃ kriyājanyaphalabhāgitvaṃ ca na tatsamavāyinamākṣipati, kintu tādarthyamātram /
anyathopayuktānāṃ prastarādīnāṃ homenotpādyamānaḥ saṃskāro na teṣāṃ syāt, teṣāṃ vinaṣṭatvāt /
na ca tatra saṃskāryatvaṃ nāsti, ``bhūtabhāvyupayogaṃ ca dravyaṃ saṃskāramarhati'' iti nyāyāt /
tatra ca nirāśrayasya saṃskārasyāvasthānānupapatterātmāśrayatvaṃ kalpanīyam /
tadvaditaratrāpi bhavatu, ko doṣaḥ?
children.translated_text: In the [sentence] 'he sprinkles the rice-grains,' the second [case-ending i.e., accusative] does not convey that the <s>saṃskāra</s> (consecration) inheres in them; and 'being a recipient of the fruit produced by the ritual act' does not imply that which inheres in them [either], but merely 'being for that purpose.' Otherwise, the <s>saṃskāra</s> produced by the <s>homa</s> (oblation) of accessories used [in the ritual] such as the altar and so forth would not belong to them, since they have been destroyed. And it is not the case that consecratability is absent there, by the maxim: 'A substance that has been used or will be used is worthy of consecration.' And therein, since a <s>saṃskāra</s> without a substrate cannot subsist, its substrateship in the self (<s>ātman</s>) must be postulated. Let the same hold elsewhere also — what fault is there?

children.text:
(2 jñātatāyāḥ padārthāntaratvanirāsaḥ--) ghaṭamahaṃ jānāmītyatra prābhākarāṇāṃ naye jñānajanitaphalasya ghaṭe kasyacidabhāvāt tatra kathaṃ karmatvamiti cintyam /
ata eva bhāṭṭairjñātatā 'bhyupagamyate iti cet, teṣāmapyatītānāgateṣu kā vārttā? tatrāpi jāteranuvartamānatvādadoṣa iti cet, kathaṃ tarhi vyaktau jñātatvam? tayorabhedāditi cet, na, bhedasyāpi vidyamānatvāt /
bhede 'pyadoṣa iti cet, na, rasanena rasajñānamātreṇaiva tadāśrayasyāpi jñātatvaprasaṅgāt /
sattājñānatvamātreṇaiva jātyandhasyāpi rūpajñānaprasaṅgaḥ /
jñātatānabhyupagamāt kathaṃ jñānasya viṣayaniyama iti cet, jñātatāyā eva kathamāśrayaniyamaḥ? kāraṇamahimneti cet, samaḥ samādhiḥ /
children.translated_text: (2. Refutation of <s>jñātatā</s> (known-ness) as a separate category) In the [cognition] 'I know the pot,' according to the <s>Prābhākara</s> doctrine, since the fruit produced by cognition is absent in the pot, how can it have objecthood there? — this should be considered. If [one responds] 'therefore the <s>Bhāṭṭas</s> accept <s>jñātatā</s> (known-ness)' — what is the situation for them too regarding past and future [objects]? If [one says] 'no fault, because the universal (<s>jāti</s>) persists [even in those cases]' — then how [can there be] known-ness in an individual (<s>vyakti</s>)? If [one says] 'because of their non-difference' — no, because difference also exists. If [one says] 'no fault even with difference' — no, because through the sense of taste alone, by mere taste-cognition, there would be the undesirable consequence of known-ness even for the substrate [of taste]. Through mere existence-cognition alone, there would be the undesirable consequence that even one born blind would have cognition of form. If [one asks] 'without accepting <s>jñātatā</s>, how is there a determination of the object of cognition?' — well, how is there a determination of the substrate of <s>jñātatā</s> itself? If [answered] 'by the power of the cause' — the same answer applies [to our position].

children.text:
(3 viśiṣṭatayāḥ padārthāntaratānirāsaḥ--) etena viśiṣṭatāpi nirākṛtā, tadutpādakasāmagryā eva vijātīyajñānotpattāvapyupapatteḥ /
na ca viṣayavailakṣaṇyābhāve vaijātyaṃ durghaṭam, anubhavasmṛtyoravaijātyaprasaṅgāt, adhikaviṣayatve smṛterapi pramāṇatvaprasaṅgāt /
anyāyā viśiṣṭatāyā atītānāgateṣvavasthanaṃ durghaṭam, āśrayābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: (3. Refutation of <s>viśiṣṭatā</s> (qualified-ness) as a separate category) By this, <s>viśiṣṭatā</s> (qualified-ness) is also refuted, because even the causal complex that produces it can explain the production of a different kind of cognition. And it is not difficult to explain the difference of kind in the absence of a difference of object, because of the undesirable consequence that experience (<s>anubhava</s>) and memory (<s>smṛti</s>) would not be of different kinds; and because of the undesirable consequence that even memory would be a means of knowledge if it had an additional object. The subsistence of any other <s>viśiṣṭatā</s> in past and future [objects] is difficult to explain, because of the absence of a substrate.

children.text:
(4 viṣayībhāvasya padārthāntaranirāsaḥ--) etena viṣayībhāvarūpaḥ sambandho nirastaḥ, tanniyāmakenaiva jñānārthayorniyamopapatteḥ /
evaṃ sānnidhyādayo 'pi nirākartavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: (4. Refutation of <s>viṣayībhāva</s> (objecthood) as a separate category) By this, the relation in the form of <s>viṣayībhāva</s> (objecthood) is also refuted, because the determination of cognition and object is possible through that alone which determines that [relation]. Likewise, <s>sānnidhya</s> (proximity) and so forth should also be refuted.

children.text:
(5 sādṛśyasya padārthāntaratvanirāsaḥ--) astu tarhi sādṛśyaṃ padārthāntaramiti cet, na, mānābhāvāt /
na ca vyavahāro mānam, tasya sāmānyādisambandhatvenāpyupapatteḥ /
kathaṃ tarhi sāmānye sādṛśyavyavahāraḥ, kutaḥ śyenacitaṃ cinvīta (tai saṃ 5.4.11) ityatrātideśanam? tatrāpi vyaktisādṛśyasyaiva pratīteḥ /
vyakteśca śabdārthatvāt, śyenatvaikārthasamavetadvitradharmavato 'nuṣṭhānasya sambhavāt /
saṃketagrahasyaupādhikaśabdavadupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: (5. Refutation of <s>sādṛśya</s> (similarity) as a separate category) If [one claims] 'let <s>sādṛśya</s> (similarity) then be an additional category' — no, because of the absence of a means of knowledge [for it]. And verbal usage is not a means of knowledge [here], because it can be explained through the relation with a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) and so forth. Then how is there the usage of 'similarity' regarding a universal, [and] whence the analogical extension (<s>atideśa</s>) in 'one should pile up the fire-altar in the shape of a hawk' (<s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 5.4.11)? Because therein too, only the similarity of individuals is cognized. And because the individual is the meaning of the word, because the performance is possible through one possessing two or three properties of the same meaning as hawk-ness, and because the apprehension of convention can be explained as in the case of a contingent word (<s>aupādhika-śabda</s>).

children.text:
(6 pradhānasya padārthāntaratvapratyākhyānam--) evaṃ pradhānādayo 'pi nirākāryāḥ, sādhakābhāvāt /
na ca vivādapadaṃ sākṣātparamparayā vā prakṛtijanyam, kāryatvādityavītamiti vācyam, vyaptyasiddheḥ /
na ca sukhaduḥkhamohāḥ kāraṇapūrvakāḥ, kāryatvāditi sāmpratam, saṃyogādiṣu vyabhicārāt /
na ca sadutpattiparyālocanayā tatsiddhaḥ, tatraiva vivādāt /
na ca tadarthamupādīyamānatvāt tatra sattvam, nimittakāraṇe vyabhicārāt /
na ca sati kāraṇavyāpāraḥ asārthakatvāditi jātiniyamajñena vyavasthā ghaṭate /
yenaiva pramāṇena ghaṭabhāvasiddhistenaiva pramāṇena yogyānupalabdhyā paṭotpatteḥ pūrvaṃ tantuṣvapi paṭābhāvasiddhiḥ /
ayogyatvenānupalabdhiśaṅkāyāmitaratrāpi sambhāvanāṃ ko nivārayet? kāryāpekṣayā caramasahakārikāraṇādutpattiriti nānavasthādūṣaṇam, mūlakṣaterabhāvāt /
nāpi punaruktatvavirodho ghaṭādibhistasyāścotpatterabhyupagamāt /
abhivyakte tu sarvāsāmabhivyaktīnāṃ sadātanatvād dṛṣṭādṛṣṭavyāsthādauḥsthyam /
kiṃ bahunā ``parasparavirodhe hi na prakārāntarasthitiḥ'' iti nyāyāt padārthāntarāṇāṃ na sambhavaḥ, saptalakṣaṇānāṃ parasparavirodhāditi /
children.translated_text:
(6. Rejection of <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) as a separate category:) Thus <s>pradhāna</s> and the like too are to be refuted, due to the absence of establishing means.
Nor should it be said that 'the subject of dispute is produced directly or indirectly by <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), because it is an effect' is unrefuted — because the pervasion is unestablished.
Nor is it correct [to argue] that pleasure, pain, and delusion are preceded by a cause, because they are effects — because there is deviation in conjunction etc.
Nor is that established by the consideration of production from what exists (<s>sadutpatti</s>), because there is dispute precisely on that point.
Nor is there existence there because [things] are adopted for that purpose, because there is deviation in the efficient cause.
Nor does the arrangement succeed through one who knows the restriction of universals, since 'causal operation occurs only in what exists' is purposeless.
By the very means of knowledge by which the existence of a pot is established, by that very means the non-existence of a cloth in threads prior to the production of a cloth is established, through qualified non-apprehension (<s>yogyānupalabdhi</s>).
If there is suspicion that the non-apprehension is of an unqualified [entity], who could prevent the same possibility elsewhere? The objection of infinite regress does not apply since production is from the last auxiliary cause relative to the effect, because the root deficiency is absent.
Nor is there a contradiction of repetition, since the production of that [capacity] from pots etc. is also accepted.
But in the theory of manifestation (<s>abhivyakti</s>), since all manifestations are eternal for all [entities], there is the difficulty of maintaining the arrangement of seen and unseen.
In short, by the principle 'when there is mutual contradiction, there is no existence of another mode,' other categories are not possible, because the seven categories are mutually contradictory.

children.text: mokṣaprakaraṇam
children.translated_text: Section on liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>)

children.text:
tatra hi dravyādināṃ heyopādeyasvarūpeṇa jñāne sati saṃsārasya duḥkhabhūyastvaṃ paśyataḥ sukhamapi duḥkhānuṣaṅgādduḥkhapakṣe nikṣiptam /
upaniṣadā ca jñātajīvātmabrahmaṇo vaiśeṣikoktadṛśā bhagavadbhaktimanaskasya sadgurukaṭākṣapātakṣīṇāntarāyasya parameśvarasākṣātkārakutūhalino 'horātraṃ nididhyāsanamācarato 'nantakālakrameṇa paripakvajñānasya prakṛṣṭayogajadharmaśālinaḥ kathañcitsākṣātkṛtaparameśvarasya pravṛddhapratipakṣaniravakāśīkṛtamithyājñānasya kāraṇābhāvādapagatarāgadveṣapravṛttisambhāvanasyāśeṣaduḥkhābhāvāt svena rūpeṇāvasthānaṃ bhavati /
sa cāyaṃ mokṣa iti manīṣibhirudāhriyate /
children.translated_text:
For therein, when one has knowledge of substances etc. in the form of what is to be rejected and what is to be adopted, seeing that <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) is predominantly suffering — even pleasure is placed in the category of suffering due to its association with suffering.
And through the <s>Upaniṣad</s>, for one who has known the identity of <s>jīvātman</s> (individual self) and <s>Brahman</s>, who views [things] through the Vaiśeṣika perspective, whose mind is devoted to the Lord (<s>Bhagavān</s>), whose obstacles have been diminished by the gracious glance of a true teacher (<s>sadguru</s>), who is eager for the direct realization of <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), who practices <s>nididhyāsana</s> (meditation) day and night, whose knowledge has matured over an immense course of time, who possesses the qualities born of advanced <s>yoga</s>, who has somehow directly realized <s>Parameśvara</s>, whose false knowledge has been rendered scope-less by the growth of the counteragent — due to the absence of the cause [of bondage], for one in whom the possibility of attachment, aversion, and activity has departed, there is abiding in one's own nature, due to the absence of all suffering.
And this is declared by the wise to be <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).

children.text:
na ca sukhasyāpyabhāvādapravṛttiḥ, bhavatāmapi sukhasyāpravṛttikaratvāt /
na hi tatsādhyam, nityatvavyāghātāt /
na hi siddhārthe kaścitprayatate iti bhavatāmapi avidyānivṛttireva kṛtisādhyā, tataśca tadeva prayojanaṃ yathāha- ``yamarthamadhikṛtya pravartate, tat prayojanam'' (nyā sū 1.1.24) /
``ānandaṃ brahmaṇo rūpaṃ tacca mokṣe 'bhivyajyate'' iti santoṣajasukhabhiprāyeṇa gauṇyā vṛttyā duḥkhābhāvābhiprāyeṇa vā kathaṃcidguṇavāda iti, ``aśarīraṃ vāva santaṃ na priyāpriye spṛśataḥ'' (chā u 8.12.1) iti vacanāt /
na ca sāṃsārikasukhābhiprāyeṇa tat, sāṃsārikasukhasyāpi brahmasukhānatiriktatvāt /
svayamprakāśatve ca svasya muktisaṃsārayoraviśeṣaprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text:
Nor is there non-activity due to the absence of pleasure too, since according to you also, pleasure does not cause activity.
For that [pleasure] is not to be accomplished, because it would contradict eternality.
Since no one makes effort for what is already accomplished, even according to you, only the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is to be accomplished by effort — and therefore that alone is the purpose, as stated: 'That for the sake of which one acts, that is the purpose' (<s>Nyāya Sūtra</s> 1.1.24).
'Bliss is the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, and that is manifested in <s>mokṣa</s>' — this is [said] with the intention of the pleasure born of contentment, through a secondary meaning, or with the intention of the absence of suffering; it is somehow a statement of praise (<s>guṇavāda</s>). [As the <s>śruti</s> says:] 'Indeed, when one is incorporeal, the pleasant and unpleasant do not touch one' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.12.1).

children.text:
atra kecit-- duḥkhaparihārārthaṃ jñānasukhayoḥ pūrvaṃ viṣayaviṣayibhāvo 'nupapannaḥ paścādutpādya iti brūyuḥ /
tadasāmpratam, tatsadbhāve pramāṇābhāvāt /
yasya loke 'prasiddhiḥ, tasya prayojakatvamityapi durghaṭameva /
neha jñānamasti, viṣayaviṣayibhāvo nāstīti dṛṣṭapūrvam, jñānasya vākyenotpādakasāmagryā eva vā tadutpādakatvāt /
pradhānādinirāsenaiva taduktamokṣasyāpi bhaṅgo veditavyaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Here some [say]: the subject-object relation between knowledge and pleasure must be first untenable and then produced, for the purpose of removing suffering.
That is not correct, because there is no means of knowledge for its existence.
The claim that 'what is not well-known in the world has operative power' is also quite untenable.
'Here there is no knowledge, there is no subject-object relation' — this has never been observed, since it is the sentence alone or the causal aggregate that produces that cognition.
By the very refutation of <s>pradhāna</s> etc., the refutation of that kind of <s>mokṣa</s> too should be understood.

children.text:
vimataṃ kadācidviśeṣaguṇarahitam, vijñānāsamavāyikāraṇādhāratvādanityaviśeṣaguṇādhāratvānmanovadvyomavacca /
na ca jīvā nityajñānā ātmavadīśvaravaditi sāmpratam, īśvarasvarūpasyaivopādheḥ /
piṇḍavyabhicārābhāvāt /
na ca nityaviśeṣaguṇādhārā iti sādhyarthaḥ, apārthivadvyaṇukārambhakatve sati viśeṣaguṇavattvopādheḥ /
viśeṣaṇābhāvādbhavatāṃ punarviśeṣaguṇarahitatvāt /
sukhatvaṃ nityasamavetam, tajjātitvāditi tu tadgatanikarṣatvena vyabhicaratātyalamatiprasaṅgena /
children.translated_text:
The subject under dispute is at some time devoid of specific qualities, because it is a substratum that sustains the non-inherent cause of consciousness and because it is a substratum of non-eternal specific qualities — like <s>manas</s> (mind) and like <s>ākāśa</s> (space).
Nor is it correct [to argue] that <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) possess eternal knowledge like the <s>ātman</s> or like <s>Īśvara</s> — because the very nature of <s>Īśvara</s> is the limiting condition.
Because there is no deviation in the totality.
Nor does the <s>sādhya</s> mean 'substrata of eternal specific qualities,' because the limiting condition is 'possessing specific qualities while being a producer of non-earthen dyads.'
Due to the absence of a qualifier, because according to you [the souls] are devoid of specific qualities in certain states.
[The argument that] pleasure-ness is eternally co-inherent, because it is a universal of that — but that deviates due to being a proximity [of that universal] occurring there — enough with over-extension.

children.text: namastripathagākrāntajaṭājūṭāya śambhave /
children.translated_text: Salutations to <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva), whose matted locks are adorned by the triple-pathed [<s>Gaṅgā</s>].

children.text: namaste jagadutpattisthitidhvaṃsavidhāyine //
children.translated_text: Salutations to you, the ordainer of the creation, maintenance, and destruction of the world.

children.text: iti śrīvādivāgīśvarācāryaviracitaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus [the work] composed by the venerable <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Vādivāgīśvara</s>,

children.text: mānamanoharaḥ samāptaḥ //
children.translated_text: the <s>Mānamanohara</s>, is completed.
